outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Address & Signage Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IFC §505 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Property address numbers
•	Building identification signage
•	Unit identification signage (exterior facing)
•	Directional signage
•	Emergency access signage
•	Parking/drive signage
•	Fire lane and fire department access signage
If no exterior signage exists → Not Applicable.
2. Address Numbers – Primary Building Identification (IFC §505.1)
Inspect:
•	Address numbers visible from the street
•	Numbers contrasting with background
•	Numbers minimum 4 inches high (common ICC requirement)
•	Numbers not obstructed by vegetation, lighting fixtures, or architectural elements
•	Numbers illuminated at night (if required by jurisdiction)
•	Numbers permanently affixed (not temporary, paper, or taped)
Hazard Severity:
•	Address not visible from street → Immediate Hazard (emergency response delay)
3. Building Identification Signage (IPMC §304.3)
Inspect:
•	Building name/number clearly displayed
•	Signage readable from common access points
•	No missing, faded, or damaged signage
•	No peeling paint or corrosion affecting readability
•	Signage securely mounted (no loose or falling hazard)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing building identification → Severe
•	Loose signage that may fall → Immediate Hazard
4. Unit Number Signage (Exterior Facing Units)
Inspect:
•	Unit numbers present and readable
•	Numbers not faded, missing, or obstructed
•	Numbers permanently affixed (no paper/tape)
•	Numbers visible from exterior corridor or walkway
•	No damaged or sharp edge signage
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing unit number → Moderate/Severe (depending on access impact)
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
5. Directional & Wayfinding Signage
Inspect:
•	Directional arrows or building maps present (if required)
•	Signage readable and not faded
•	No missing directional signs for multi building sites
•	No obstructions blocking signage
•	No damaged or loose signs
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing critical directional signage → Severe
6. Emergency Access Signage (IFC §505 / §912)
Inspect:
•	Fire lane signage present and readable
•	Fire department connection (FDC) signage present
•	Hydrant markers visible
•	No faded or missing emergency signage
•	No vegetation blocking emergency signs
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing fire lane or FDC signage → Immediate Hazard
7. Parking & Drive Signage
Inspect:
•	Visitor parking signs readable
•	Handicap parking signs present and compliant
•	No missing or damaged parking signage
•	No sharp edges or loose mounting
•	No faded paint markings (arrows, stall identifiers)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing handicap signage → Severe
•	Loose metal signage → Immediate Hazard
8. Lighting for Signage Visibility (IPMC §402)
Inspect:
•	Exterior lighting adequate to illuminate address and signage
•	No burned out bulbs affecting visibility
•	No damaged fixtures
•	No lighting blocked by vegetation
Hazard Severity:
•	Address not visible at night → Severe
9. Weather Tightness & Durability
Inspect:
•	No rust or corrosion on metal signs
•	No peeling paint or fading reducing readability
•	No warped or cracked plastic signage
•	No water damage affecting mounting or visibility
Hazard Severity:
•	Signage deterioration affecting readability → Moderate/Severe

outside.deficiencySelected: A vertical or near vertical passageway connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance.
outside.deficiencyDetail: A visually accessible chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood‑burning appliance is deficient if it is incomplete or visibly damaged in a way that prevents it from safely containing fire or venting smoke and combustion gases to the exterior
outside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: A visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is incomplete (i.e., evidence of a previously installed component) that is now not present) such that it may not safely contain fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior. 
OR 
A visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is damaged (i.e., visibly defective; impacts functionality) such that it may not safely contain fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior.
outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Chimney Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §304 / IBC §2101–2104)
Inspection applies to:
•	Masonry chimneys
•	Metal chimneys
•	Factory built chimneys
•	Chimney chases
•	Roof penetrating flues
•	Shared multi unit chimney stacks
If no chimney is present → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Condition (IBC §2101–2104)
Inspect:
•	Cracks in masonry (vertical, horizontal, step cracks)
•	Spalling, flaking, or missing bricks
•	Loose or deteriorated mortar joints
•	Leaning, tilting, or out of plumb chimney stack
•	Separation from exterior wall or roof structure
•	Rust or corrosion on metal chimneys
Immediate Hazard: Chimney leaning, unstable, or showing collapse risk.
3. Chimney Cap, Crown & Spark Arrestor (IFC §603.6)
Inspect:
•	Cap/crown intact (no cracks or missing sections)
•	Spark arrestor present (if required)
•	No rust, holes, or deterioration
•	No debris blocking cap or arrestor
•	No gaps allowing water intrusion
Severe: Missing or damaged spark arrestor.
4. Flashing & Roof Penetration (IPMC §304.7)
Inspect:
•	Flashing intact and sealed
•	No gaps or lifting of flashing
•	No water stains on roof materials near chimney
•	No rust or corrosion on metal flashing
•	No vegetation growing in flashing joints
Severe: Flashing failure causing active water intrusion.
5. Chimney Chase (If Applicable)
Inspect:
•	Siding intact (no rot, cracks, or holes)
•	No missing panels
•	No loose or unstable chase structure
•	No moisture staining or mold like substance
•	No pest entry points
Severe: Chase deterioration exposing flue or structure.
6. Flue Condition (Visible Portions Only)
Inspect:
•	No visible cracks in flue tile
•	No missing flue sections
•	No soot staining indicating improper draft
•	No obstructions visible from top or bottom
•	No rust or deterioration on metal flues
Immediate Hazard: Severe flue damage or obstruction.
7. Fire Safety & Clearances (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	No combustible materials stored near chimney base
•	No vegetation touching chimney
•	No tree branches overhanging chimney top
•	No signs of chimney fire (soot, cracking, warping)
Immediate Hazard: Combustibles contacting chimney or signs of past fire.
8. Moisture & Weathering Indicators (IPMC §304.2 / §304.7)
Inspect:
•	Water stains on chimney exterior
•	Efflorescence (white mineral deposits)
•	Moss or vegetation growth
•	Freeze thaw damage
•	Rust streaks on metal chimneys
Severe: Moisture damage compromising masonry or metal integrity.
9. Foundation & Base Condition
Inspect:
•	Cracks at chimney base
•	Settlement or sinking
•	Gaps between chimney and foundation
•	Soil erosion around chimney base
Severe: Foundation movement affecting chimney stability.
10. Safety Interaction (IFC §603 / IPMC §304)
Inspect:
•	Falling hazards from loose bricks or components
•	Water + electrical interaction (if exterior lighting nearby)
•	Trip hazards from broken chimney base materials
•	No destructive inspection allowed (no roof walking unless authorized)
Immediate Hazard: Loose masonry that may fall.

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Clothes Dryer Exhaust Vent Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IMC §504 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior dryer vent terminations
•	Exterior wall caps / hood vents
•	Roof dryer vent terminations
•	Multi unit shared dryer exhaust systems
•	Exterior duct sections (if visible)
If no exterior dryer vent exists → Not Applicable.
2. Exterior Vent Termination Condition
Inspect:
•	Vent hood present and securely attached
•	No missing, broken, or loose vent covers
•	No cracks, holes, or gaps in hood
•	No sharp edges or damaged metal/plastic
•	No rust or corrosion on metal components
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose or missing vent hood → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Backdraft Damper (Required by IMC §504.6)
Inspect:
•	Damper present
•	Damper opens freely and closes fully
•	No lint buildup preventing movement
•	No damaged or missing damper flap
•	No obstructions (paint, debris, screws) blocking operation
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing or stuck damper → Severe
•	Damper blocked open → Severe
4. Lint Accumulation (Fire Safety – IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Lint buildup at exterior vent
•	Lint blocking hood or damper
•	Lint accumulation on siding or ground near vent
•	Lint clinging to screen (if present — screens are prohibited)
Hazard Severity:
•	Heavy lint buildup → Immediate Hazard (fire risk)
•	Screen installed over dryer vent → Immediate Hazard
5. Exterior Ducting (Visible Portions Only)
Inspect:
•	Metal duct only (no plastic or foil flex allowed outdoors)
•	No crushed, kinked, or disconnected duct sections
•	No gaps allowing air leakage
•	No rust or deterioration
•	No duct termination into attic, crawlspace, or interior cavity
Hazard Severity:
•	Improper duct material → Severe
•	Disconnected duct → Immediate Hazard
6. Moisture & Heat Interaction
Inspect:
•	Moisture staining on siding near vent
•	Mold like substance around vent hood
•	Peeling paint or warped siding from heat/moisture
•	Condensation dripping from vent
Hazard Severity:
•	Moisture damage indicating improper venting → Severe
7. Pest & Bird Intrusion
Inspect:
•	No bird nests inside or around vent
•	No rodent screens installed (prohibited)
•	No gaps allowing pest entry
•	No debris blocking vent opening
Hazard Severity:
•	Nest or obstruction → Severe
•	Pest screen installed → Immediate Hazard
8. Roof Mounted Dryer Vents (If Applicable)
Inspect:
•	Cap intact and secure
•	No missing shingles around vent
•	Flashing intact (no gaps or lifting)
•	No debris blocking roof vent
•	No signs of water intrusion at roof penetration
Hazard Severity:
•	Roof vent obstruction → Severe
•	Flashing failure → Severe
9. Multi Unit Shared Exhaust Systems
Inspect:
•	No cross connection between units
•	No shared ducting unless engineered
•	No backdrafting signs (lint on multiple units’ siding)
•	No exhaust discharge near windows or air intakes
Hazard Severity:
•	Shared dryer exhaust without design approval → Immediate Hazard
10. Safety Interaction (IFC §603 / IPMC §304)
Inspect:
•	No combustibles stored near vent discharge
•	No vegetation blocking vent
•	No electrical fixtures exposed to lint discharge
•	No trip hazards from damaged vent components
Hazard Severity:
•	Combustibles near vent → Immediate Hazard
•	Electrical + lint interaction → Immediate Hazard

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Non Entry / Non Exit Door 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §304 / IBC §1008)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior non entry doors
•	Exterior non exit doors
•	Exterior utility / mechanical room doors
•	Exterior storage room doors
•	Exterior stairwell doors
•	Exterior garage vehicle doors
•	Exterior garage service doors
•	Any exterior door not designated as a primary egress or entry point
If none exist → Not Applicable.
2. Exterior Non Entry / Non Exit Doors (General)
A. Structural Condition (IPMC §304.15)
Inspect:
•	Door intact (no holes, cracks, rot, rust)
•	No loose or missing panels
•	No warping or swelling
•	No sharp edges or protruding fasteners
•	Hinges secure; door not sagging
•	Frame intact and securely attached
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose or unstable door → Immediate Hazard
B. Operation & Hardware
Inspect:
•	Door opens/closes without binding
•	Latch/lock operable (if required for security or access control)
•	No missing or broken handles, hinges, or closers
•	No obstruction preventing full swing
•	No excessive force required
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable door required for maintenance access → Severe
•	Loose hardware creating falling hazard → Immediate Hazard
C. Weather Tightness & Moisture
Inspect:
•	No water intrusion at frame or threshold
•	No swollen or deteriorated trim
•	No mold like substance
•	Weatherstripping intact
•	No gaps allowing pests or water
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + moisture → Severe
D. Security & Safety
Inspect:
•	Locks present and functional (if required)
•	No broken glass in door panels
•	No loose strike plates
•	No gaps allowing unauthorized access
•	No sharp edges on metal doors
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken glass → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable lock → Severe
E. Fire Rated general Non Entry Doors (Mechanical/Utility Rooms)
Inspect:
•	Fire label present
•	Door closes and latches automatically
•	No penetrations compromising rating
•	No missing or damaged self closing device
•	No damaged frame or threshold
Hazard Severity:
•	Fire rated door not self closing → Severe
3. Exterior Garage Doors (Vehicle Doors)
A. Structural Condition
Inspect:
•	Panels intact (no cracks, holes, rust)
•	No bent tracks or damaged rollers
•	No loose or missing hardware
•	No sharp edges
•	No separation from frame or header
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose panel or track → Immediate Hazard
B. Operation & Safety (IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Door opens/closes smoothly
•	No binding or jerking
•	Manual doors lift without excessive force
•	Powered doors operate safely
•	Auto reverse safety feature functional
•	No obstruction in travel path
Hazard Severity:
•	Auto reverse failure → Immediate Hazard
•	Door that may fall → Immediate Hazard
C. Weather Tightness & Moisture
Inspect:
•	No water intrusion at garage door
•	No damaged bottom seal
•	No mold like substance
•	No moisture damage to adjacent walls or trim
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Severe
D. Fire Separation (Garage to Dwelling)
Inspect:
•	Garage service door self closing
•	No penetrations in fire rated door
•	No damaged frame or threshold
•	No missing weatherstripping
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing self closing device → Severe
E. Electrical Interaction (Powered Doors)
Inspect:
•	No exposed wiring
•	No damaged opener motor housing
•	No water near electrical components
•	No frayed or damaged opener cables
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
4. Surrounding Exterior Conditions
Inspect:
•	No trip hazards at door thresholds
•	No vegetation blocking access
•	No loose concrete, pavers, or steps
•	Adequate lighting at exterior doors
•	No pests entering through gaps
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard at access point → Severe
•	Poor lighting → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Drain/ Site Drainage Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302 / §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Surface drainage
•	Grading and slope
•	Swales and drainage channels
•	Storm drains and catch basins
•	Area drains
•	Downspouts and splash blocks
•	Drainage around foundations
•	Parking lot drainage
•	Courtyard and walkway drainage
If no drainage components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Grading & Site Slope (IBC §1805.3)
Inspect:
•	Soil slopes away from building (minimum 6" fall in first 10 feet recommended)
•	No negative grading directing water toward structures
•	No erosion channels or washouts
•	No ponding near foundations, walkways, or entries
Hazard Severity:
•	Negative slope causing water intrusion → Severe
•	Ponding near foundation → Severe
3. Surface Drainage Paths
Inspect:
•	Swales clear and unobstructed
•	No debris, vegetation, or trash blocking flow
•	No standing water in swales
•	No erosion undermining sidewalks or slabs
•	No sediment buildup reducing capacity
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked swale causing water backup → Severe
4. Storm Drains, Catch Basins & Area Drains (IPC Chapter 11)
Inspect:
•	Grates present and secure
•	No broken or missing grates
•	No debris, leaves, or trash blocking inlet
•	No standing water indicating clog
•	No structural damage to basin or surrounding concrete
•	No foul odors indicating sewer cross connection
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing grate → Immediate Hazard
•	Clogged drain causing flooding → Severe
5. Downspouts, Gutters & Splash Blocks
Inspect:
•	Downspouts intact and connected
•	No crushed or disconnected sections
•	No missing splash blocks
•	Water discharged away from building
•	No gutter overflow signs (staining, streaking)
•	No vegetation growing in gutters
Hazard Severity:
•	Disconnected downspout → Severe
•	Water discharging at foundation → Severe
6. Drainage Around Foundations (IPMC §304.2)
Inspect:
•	No ponding against foundation walls
•	No moisture staining or efflorescence
•	No erosion exposing foundation
•	No settlement or soil gaps
•	No mold like substance on exterior walls
Hazard Severity:
•	Water intrusion at foundation → Severe
•	Erosion undermining foundation → Immediate Hazard
7. Parking Lot & Driveway Drainage
Inspect:
•	No ponding in drive lanes or parking stalls
•	No clogged parking lot drains
•	No asphalt depressions holding water
•	No sediment buildup blocking flow
•	No water flowing toward building entries
Hazard Severity:
•	Ponding in vehicle or pedestrian paths → Severe
8. Walkway & Courtyard Drainage
Inspect:
•	No standing water on walkways
•	No slippery algae or mold from poor drainage
•	No trip hazards from erosion or undermining
•	No blocked courtyard drains
Hazard Severity:
•	Standing water causing slip hazard → Immediate Hazard
9. Retaining Walls & Drainage Interaction
Inspect:
•	Weep holes present and unobstructed
•	No hydrostatic pressure signs (bulging, cracking)
•	No water staining or seepage
•	No erosion at wall base
Hazard Severity:
•	Bulging retaining wall → Immediate Hazard
10. Safety Interaction (IFC §603 / IPMC §302)
Inspect:
•	No water near exterior electrical equipment
•	No trip hazards from drainage failures
•	No mosquito breeding standing water
•	No blocked emergency access routes
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
•	Standing water in egress path → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Egress Inspection (Site & Building Exterior)
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1001–1003 / IPMC §302–304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior exit doors
•	Exterior exit discharge paths
•	Exterior stairs, ramps, landings
•	Exterior corridors and breezeways
•	Egress gates and fences
•	Exterior lighting for egress
•	Exterior signage for egress
•	Fire department access routes
If no exterior egress components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Exit Discharge Path (IBC §1028)
Inspect:
•	Path from exit door to public way is continuous and unobstructed
•	No vegetation, debris, furniture, or storage blocking path
•	Surface even and slip resistant
•	No holes, trip hazards, or broken pavement
•	No ponding water or mud obstructing movement
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked exit discharge → Immediate Hazard
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
3. Exterior Stairs & Landings (IBC §1011)
Inspect:
•	Treads and risers intact and uniform
•	No cracks, breaks, or loose steps
•	No slippery surfaces (algae, moss, water)
•	Landings present at required intervals
•	No structural deterioration (rot, rust, corrosion)
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose or unstable stair → Immediate Hazard
•	Slippery stair surface → Severe
4. Exterior Ramps (IBC §1012)
Inspect:
•	Slope compliant (max 1:12)
•	Surface intact and slip resistant
•	No cracks, holes, or deterioration
•	No obstructions blocking ramp
•	Handrails present where required
Hazard Severity:
•	Ramp obstruction → Immediate Hazard
•	Excessive slope → Severe
5. Handrails & Guardrails (IBC §1014–1015)
Inspect:
•	Handrails present on stairs and ramps
•	Guardrails present on elevated walking surfaces
•	No loose, missing, or unstable rails
•	No openings >4 inches
•	No sharp edges or broken components
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing or loose handrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Guardrail openings >4 inches → Severe
6. Exterior Exit Doors (IBC §1008 / IPMC §304.15)
Inspect:
•	Doors operable without special knowledge
•	No binding, sticking, or blocked swing
•	No damaged or missing hardware
•	No broken glass
•	No obstructions behind or in front of door
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable exit door → Immediate Hazard
7. Egress Gates & Fences (IBC §1028.5)
Inspect:
•	Gates operable without keys or special tools
•	No locks that impede egress
•	No rust, deterioration, or structural failure
•	Gate path unobstructed
•	No sharp edges or protruding hardware
Hazard Severity:
•	Locked egress gate → Immediate Hazard
8. Exterior Egress Lighting (IBC §1008.2 / IPMC §402)
Inspect:
•	Adequate illumination along egress path
•	No burned out bulbs
•	No damaged fixtures
•	No vegetation blocking light
•	Lighting functional during nighttime conditions
Hazard Severity:
•	Insufficient lighting → Severe
9. Egress Signage (IBC §1013 / IFC §505)
Inspect:
•	Exit signs visible and readable
•	Directional signage present where needed
•	No faded, missing, or damaged signs
•	No obstructions blocking signage
•	Signs illuminated (if required)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing critical exit signage → Severe
10. Fire Department Access (IFC §503–505)
Inspect:
•	Fire lanes unobstructed
•	No parked vehicles blocking access
•	Hydrants accessible and visible
•	Fire department connection (FDC) signage present
•	No vegetation blocking access routes
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked fire lane → Immediate Hazard

outside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Electrical conductor is not enclosed or properly insulated (e.g., damaged sheathing, open port, missing knockout, missing outlet or switch cover, missing breaker or fuse).  OR. An opening or gap is present and measures greater than ½”

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Fence & Gate Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302 / §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Perimeter fences
•	Privacy fences
•	Security fences
•	Pool barrier fences
•	Courtyard fences
•	Pedestrian gates
•	Vehicle access gates
•	Fire department access gates
If no exterior fencing or gates exist → Not Applicable.
2. Fence Structural Condition
Inspect:
•	No leaning, sagging, or unstable sections
•	No broken, cracked, or missing boards/panels
•	No rust, corrosion, or rot
•	No loose posts or footings
•	No separation from ground or foundation
•	No sharp edges or protruding nails/screws
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaning or unstable fence → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Fence Material Condition
Inspect:
•	Wood: no rot, termite damage, splintering
•	Metal: no rust compromising strength
•	Vinyl: no cracks, holes, or warping
•	Masonry: no loose blocks, cracks, or spalling
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural deterioration affecting stability → Severe
4. Gate Operation & Safety
Inspect:
•	Gate opens/closes smoothly
•	No binding, sticking, or obstruction
•	Hinges intact and secure
•	Latch functional (if required)
•	No excessive force needed
•	No sagging gate causing ground drag
Hazard Severity:
•	Gate that cannot open (blocking access) → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose or falling gate → Immediate Hazard
5. Security & Access Control
Inspect:
•	Locks present and operable (if required)
•	No missing or broken latch hardware
•	No gaps allowing unauthorized access
•	No damaged chain link mesh
•	No cut or removed fence sections
Hazard Severity:
•	Security breach (missing lock/latch) → Severe
6. Pool Barrier Fences (IBC §3109 / Local Code)
Inspect:
•	Minimum height (typically 48" or local requirement)
•	No gaps >4 inches
•	Self closing, self latching gate
•	Latch height compliant (typically 54" above grade)
•	No climbable elements within 45" radius
Hazard Severity:
•	Non compliant pool barrier → Immediate Hazard
7. Vehicle Access Gates
Inspect:
•	Gate track intact (no bends, obstructions)
•	Rollers functional
•	Motor housing intact (if powered)
•	Auto reverse safety functional
•	No exposed wiring
•	No pinch points accessible to public
Hazard Severity:
•	Auto reverse failure → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
8. Fire Department Access Gates (IFC §503–505)
Inspect:
•	Fire access gate operable without delay
•	Knox box or fire department override present (if required)
•	No locked gates blocking emergency access
•	No vegetation obstructing fire lane or gate
Hazard Severity:
•	Locked emergency gate → Immediate Hazard

1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302 / §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Perimeter fences
•	Privacy fences
•	Security fences
•	Pool barrier fences
•	Courtyard fences
•	Pedestrian gates
•	Vehicle access gates
•	Fire department access gates
If no exterior fencing or gates exist → Not Applicable.
2. Fence Structural Condition
Inspect:
•	No leaning, sagging, or unstable sections
•	No broken, cracked, or missing boards/panels
•	No rust, corrosion, or rot
•	No loose posts or footings
•	No separation from ground or foundation
•	No sharp edges or protruding nails/screws
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaning or unstable fence → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Fence Material Condition
Inspect:
•	Wood: no rot, termite damage, splintering
•	Metal: no rust compromising strength
•	Vinyl: no cracks, holes, or warping
•	Masonry: no loose blocks, cracks, or spalling
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural deterioration affecting stability → Severe
4. Gate Operation & Safety
Inspect:
•	Gate opens/closes smoothly
•	No binding, sticking, or obstruction
•	Hinges intact and secure
•	Latch functional (if required)
•	No excessive force needed
•	No sagging gate causing ground drag
Hazard Severity:
•	Gate that cannot open (blocking access) → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose or falling gate → Immediate Hazard
5. Security & Access Control
Inspect:
•	Locks present and operable (if required)
•	No missing or broken latch hardware
•	No gaps allowing unauthorized access
•	No damaged chain link mesh
•	No cut or removed fence sections
Hazard Severity:
•	Security breach (missing lock/latch) → Severe
6. Pool Barrier Fences (IBC §3109 / Local Code)
Inspect:
•	Minimum height (typically 48" or local requirement)
•	No gaps >4 inches
•	Self closing, self latching gate
•	Latch height compliant (typically 54" above grade)
•	No climbable elements within 45" radius
Hazard Severity:
•	Non compliant pool barrier → Immediate Hazard
7. Vehicle Access Gates
Inspect:
•	Gate track intact (no bends, obstructions)
•	Rollers functional
•	Motor housing intact (if powered)
•	Auto reverse safety functional
•	No exposed wiring
•	No pinch points accessible to public
Hazard Severity:
•	Auto reverse failure → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard

Inspect:
•	Fire access gate operable without delay
•	Knox box or fire department override present (if required)
•	No locked gates blocking emergency access
•	No vegetation obstructing fire lane or gate
Hazard Severity:
•	Locked emergency gate → Immediate Hazard
9. Vegetation & Surrounding Conditions
Inspect:
•	No vegetation growing through fence
•	No tree roots lifting fence posts
•	No vines compromising structure
•	No debris or trash against fence
•	No erosion undermining posts
Hazard Severity:
•	Vegetation compromising structural stability → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Fire Safety Inspection (Multi Unit Property)
1. Exterior Exit Signs (IBC §1013 / IFC §1027)
Visibility & Placement
•	Sign visible from approach path
•	No vegetation or objects blocking view
•	Directional arrows present where needed
•	Sign readable day and night
Hazard Severity:
•	Not visible → Severe
•	Misleading or incorrect direction → Immediate Hazard
Condition
•	No fading, peeling, or weather damage
•	No broken or missing panels
•	No loose mounting or sharp edges
Immediate Hazard: loose sign at risk of falling.
Illumination
•	Lighting functional at night
•	No burned out bulbs
•	No exposed wiring
•	No water intrusion
Immediate Hazard: water + electrical.
2. Exterior Fire Extinguishers (NFPA 10 / IFC §906)
Presence & Accessibility
•	Extinguishers present where required (parking garages, exterior mechanical rooms)
•	Mounted, visible, unobstructed
•	Cabinet intact (if present)
Immediate Hazard: missing required extinguisher.
Condition
•	Gauge in green
•	Pin and tamper seal intact
•	No rust, dents, or damage
•	Label readable
Severe: discharged or damaged extinguisher.
Maintenance
•	Annual inspection tag current
•	No expired units
•	No missing cabinet glass
Immediate Hazard: expired or non functional extinguisher.
3. Exterior Flammable / Combustible Materials (IFC §605 / IPMC §302)
Storage Compliance
•	No gasoline, propane, kerosene stored outdoors improperly
•	No flammable liquids near ignition sources
•	No combustible debris near building
•	No oily rags or chemical waste outdoors
Immediate Hazard: fuel stored near building or ignition source.
Containers
•	Approved containers only
•	No leaking or damaged containers
•	No unapproved plastic fuel cans
Severe: improper container or leak.
Location
•	Minimum clearance from building per local code
•	No storage blocking egress or fire department access
Immediate Hazard: flammables blocking egress.
4. Exterior Fire Sprinkler Assembly (NFPA 13 / IFC §903)
Sprinkler Heads
•	No paint, corrosion, or foreign material
•	No obstructions within 18 inches
•	No missing or damaged escutcheons
•	No leaks or moisture staining
Immediate Hazard: painted or obstructed sprinkler head.
Exterior Riser / PIV / FDC
•	Fire department connection (FDC) accessible
•	No missing caps
•	No leaks at riser
•	Post indicator valve (PIV) operable
•	No vegetation blocking access
Immediate Hazard: blocked FDC.
System Condition
•	No broken pipes
•	No rust compromising integrity
•	No exposed or damaged insulation on exterior piping
Severe: damaged sprinkler piping.

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Foundation Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1801–1805 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Concrete slab on grade foundations
•	Stem walls
•	Masonry foundations
•	Piers, posts, grade beams
•	Crawlspace foundation walls
•	Perimeter footings
•	Exterior foundation exposures
•	Foundation transitions at garages, stair towers, breezeways
If no exterior foundation exposure exists → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Integrity (IBC §1807 / §1901–1908)
Inspect:
•	Vertical, horizontal, or diagonal cracks
•	Step cracks in masonry
•	Spalling, flaking, or exposed aggregate
•	Exposed or corroded rebar
•	Bulging, leaning, or displacement
•	Settlement or heaving at foundation line
•	Separation between foundation and exterior wall
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural displacement or bulging → Immediate Hazard
•	Cracks indicating structural movement → Severe
•	Exposed rebar → Severe
3. Moisture Intrusion & Water Interaction (IPMC §304.2 / IBC §1805.4)
Inspect:
•	Moisture staining on foundation
•	Efflorescence (white mineral deposits)
•	Active water intrusion
•	Ponding water near foundation
•	Soil erosion exposing footing
•	Mold like substance on exterior wall near foundation
Hazard Severity:
•	Active water intrusion → Severe
•	Water undermining foundation → Immediate Hazard
4. Grading & Drainage Interaction (IBC §1805.3)
Inspect:
•	Soil slopes away from building
•	No negative grading directing water toward foundation
•	No erosion channels
•	No settlement gaps between soil and foundation
•	No downspouts discharging at foundation
Hazard Severity:
•	Negative slope causing water intrusion → Severe
•	Erosion undermining foundation → Immediate Hazard
5. Foundation Coatings & Protection
Inspect:
•	No peeling waterproofing membrane
•	No damaged parge coat
•	No missing protective coatings
•	No exposed insulation (if used)
•	No UV damaged protective barriers
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing waterproofing causing moisture intrusion → Severe
6. Masonry Foundation Walls (IBC §2101–2104)
Inspect:
•	No loose or missing blocks/bricks
•	No deteriorated mortar joints
•	No step cracks
•	No displacement or bowing
•	No vegetation growing through masonry
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose masonry → Immediate Hazard
•	Step cracks indicating movement → Severe
7. Concrete Foundation Walls (IBC §1901–1908)
Inspect:
•	No spalling or delamination
•	No honeycombing
•	No exposed rebar
•	No shrinkage cracks >1/8 inch
•	No structural cracks with displacement
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural cracks with displacement → Immediate Hazard
8. Crawlspace Foundation & Vents
Inspect:
•	Vents present and unobstructed
•	No broken or missing vent screens
•	No moisture staining at vent openings
•	No pest entry points
•	No soil contact with siding or framing
Hazard Severity:
•	Soil contact with siding → Severe
•	Pest entry through foundation vents → Moderate/Severe
9. Foundation at Exterior Stairs, Landings & Breezeways
Inspect:
•	No settlement at stair landings
•	No cracks at transition points
•	No separation between stair foundation and building
•	No trip hazards from foundation movement
Hazard Severity:
•	Settlement causing stair instability → Immediate Hazard
10. Garage Foundation Interface
Inspect:
•	No cracking at garage to unit transition
•	No moisture intrusion from driveway slope
•	No structural separation at fire rated wall
•	No settlement at garage slab edges
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural separation at garage wall → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Hazard Inspection 

1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302–304)
Inspection applies to:
•	All exterior site areas
•	Walkways, drive lanes, parking lots
•	Landscaping, planters, retaining walls
•	Exterior building surfaces
•	Exterior mechanical areas
•	Trash enclosures and dumpsters
•	Exterior stairways, ramps, breezeways
If no exterior hazards exist → Not Applicable.
2. Infestation (Pests) – Exterior (IPMC §302.5)
A. Evidence of Pests
Inspect:
•	Rodent droppings
•	Burrows near foundations
•	Gnaw marks on exterior materials
•	Insect nests (bees, wasps, ants)
•	Bird nests in eaves or fixtures
•	Pest trails or grease marks
B. Conditions Conducive to Infestation
Inspect:
•	Standing water
•	Food waste or trash overflow
•	Gaps in siding or foundation
•	Damaged vent screens
•	Vegetation contacting building
Hazard Severity:
•	Active rodent or insect infestation → Immediate Hazard
•	Pest entry points → Severe
3. Litter / Debris – Exterior (IPMC §302.1)
A. General Site Cleanliness
Inspect:
•	Trash, debris, or discarded items
•	Broken glass
•	Food waste attracting pests
•	Dumping or illegal disposal
•	Accumulated leaves blocking drainage
B. Trash Enclosures
Inspect:
•	Dumpster lids closed
•	No overflow or spillage
•	No damaged or missing enclosure gates
•	No sharp edges on dumpster metal
Hazard Severity:
•	Litter attracting pests → Severe
•	Broken glass → Immediate Hazard
4. Sharp Edges – Exterior (IPMC §304)
A. Exterior Building Components
Inspect:
•	Damaged metal flashing
•	Broken siding
•	Exposed nails, screws, staples
•	Damaged fences or gates
•	Broken window frames
•	Sharp edges on utility boxes
B. Site Fixtures
Inspect:
•	Damaged signage
•	Broken light fixtures
•	Bent metal posts
•	Damaged playground or recreation equipment

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior HVAC Exhaust Vent Inspection (Multi Unit Property)
1. Scope & Applicability (IMC §501–504 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Furnace exhaust vents
•	Water heater exhaust vents
•	Boiler exhaust vents
•	PTAC/heat pump exhaust vents
•	Mechanical room exhaust terminations
•	Mini split condenser discharge areas
•	Any HVAC exhaust vent located outdoors
If no exterior HVAC exhaust vents exist → Not Applicable.
2. Vent Termination Condition (IMC §501.3 / §504)
Inspect:
•	Vent hood/cap present and secure
•	No missing, broken, or loose components
•	No cracks, holes, or gaps
•	No rust or corrosion compromising integrity
•	No sharp edges or damaged metal/plastic
•	No separation from wall or roof penetration
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose or missing vent hood → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Exhaust Clearance & Location (IMC §501.3.1 / §501.3.2)
Inspect:
•	Proper clearance from windows, doors, and air intakes
•	No exhaust discharging toward walkways
•	No exhaust directed toward combustible materials
•	No exhaust located under decks or enclosed spaces
•	No vegetation blocking airflow
Hazard Severity:
•	Exhaust too close to window/air intake → Severe
•	Vegetation blocking exhaust → Severe
4. Obstructions & Blockages
Inspect:
•	No debris blocking exhaust
•	No bird nests or rodent intrusion
•	No screens installed (prohibited for HVAC exhaust)
•	No snow, soil, or landscaping blocking vent
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstructed exhaust → Immediate Hazard
•	Screen installed → Immediate Hazard
5. Combustion Exhaust (Furnace / Water Heater / Boiler)
Inspect:
•	No soot staining indicating improper combustion
•	No melted or discolored siding near vent
•	No signs of backdrafting
•	No carbon monoxide discharge toward occupied areas
•	No corrosion on metal vent pipes
Hazard Severity:
•	Soot indicating combustion failure → Immediate Hazard
•	CO discharge toward occupied areas → Immediate Hazard
6. PTAC / Heat Pump / Mini Split Exhaust
Inspect:
•	No obstruction of discharge airflow
•	No vegetation blocking condenser
•	No damaged fan guards
•	No exposed wiring
•	No refrigerant leaks (oil staining)
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked condenser airflow → Severe
7. Roof Mounted Exhaust Vents
Inspect:
•	Cap intact and secure
•	Flashing intact (no gaps or lifting)
•	No debris blocking roof vent
•	No signs of water intrusion at roof penetration
Hazard Severity:
•	Flashing failure → Severe
•	Roof vent obstruction → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Gas or Oil Leak Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IFGC / IPMC §302–304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior natural gas piping
•	Exterior propane tanks & piping
•	Exterior fuel oil tanks
•	Gas meters & regulators
•	Exterior HVAC combustion exhaust
•	Exterior water heater/furnace exhaust
•	Exterior appliance gas connections
•	Exterior generator fuel systems
If no exterior fuel systems exist → Not Applicable.
2. Gas Odor, Smell & Atmospheric Indicators (IFGC §702)
Inspect:
•	Sulfur/rotten egg odor (mercaptan)
•	Hissing sound near piping or meter
•	Dead vegetation near buried gas line
•	Dust blowing from soil (gas escaping)
•	Bubbles in standing water near piping
Hazard Severity:
•	Any gas odor → Immediate Hazard
•	Hissing or bubbling → Immediate Hazard
3. Exterior Gas Piping Condition (IFGC §404 / §407)
Inspect:
•	No corrosion, rust, or pitting
•	No bent, cracked, or damaged piping
•	No loose fittings or unions
•	No exposed threads
•	No missing protective coating
•	No improper materials (e.g., plastic not rated for gas)
Hazard Severity:
•	Damaged or corroded gas pipe → Immediate Hazard
4. Gas Meter & Regulator Assembly (IFGC §410)
Inspect:
•	Meter intact (no cracks, dents, or leaks)
•	Regulator vent unobstructed
•	No debris blocking vent
•	No rust compromising structural integrity
•	No signs of over pressurization (frosting, noise)
•	No vegetation obstructing access
Hazard Severity:
•	Regulator vent blocked → Immediate Hazard
•	Meter leak → Immediate Hazard
5. Exterior Fuel Oil Tanks (IFC §5704 / NFPA 30)
Inspect:
•	No oil odor
•	No wet spots or staining on tank
•	No rust, corrosion, or bulging
•	No damaged fill or vent piping
•	No oil on soil or pavement
•	No leaks at filter or shutoff valve
Hazard Severity:
•	Any oil leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Tank corrosion compromising integrity → Severe
6. Exterior Appliance Gas Connections
Inspect:
•	No leaks at appliance shutoff valves
•	No damaged flexible connectors
•	No improper connectors (unlisted hoses)
•	No exposed or deteriorated seals
•	No gas odor near appliance
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaking appliance connector → Immediate Hazard
7. Propane Tanks & Regulators (IFC §6103 / NFPA 58)
Inspect:
•	No leaks at tank valve
•	No frost buildup indicating leak
•	No damaged regulator
•	No rust or corrosion on tank
•	No vegetation or debris blocking tank
•	No improper tank placement (too close to building)
Hazard Severity:
•	Propane leak → Immediate Hazard

outside.deficiencySelected: Blocked sewage system.
outside.deficiencyDetail: Wastewater is unable to drain resulting in sewer backup.
outside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Wastewater is unable to drain resulting in sewer backup.
outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Sewage Leak Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPC §701–802 / IPMC §302–304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior sanitary sewer lines
•	Exterior sewer cleanouts
•	Exterior manholes
•	Exterior lift stations / ejector pumps
•	Exterior building sewer connections
•	Exterior drainage areas receiving wastewater
•	Any exterior location where sewage may leak or discharge
If no exterior sewer components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Evidence of Sewage Leakage (IPC §701.2 / §802.1)
Inspect for:
•	Visible wastewater on soil or pavement
•	Wet, foul smelling areas
•	Toilet paper or solids outside piping
•	Graywater discharge from broken lines
•	Standing wastewater near cleanouts
•	Sewage surfacing from soil
Hazard Severity:
•	Any visible sewage → Immediate Hazard
•	Foul odor indicating active leak → Immediate Hazard
3. Exterior Sewer Piping Condition (IPC §704 / §708)
Inspect:
•	Cracked, broken, or collapsed piping
•	Separated joints
•	Improper slope causing backup
•	Corroded cast iron piping
•	PVC piping exposed to UV damage
•	Tree root intrusion at joints
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken or separated pipe → Immediate Hazard
•	Root intrusion causing blockage → Severe
4. Sewer Cleanouts (IPC §708.3)
Inspect:
•	Cleanout caps present and secure
•	No missing or broken caps
•	No sewage leaking from cleanout
•	No obstruction around cleanout
•	No signs of recent overflow
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing cleanout cap → Immediate Hazard
•	Sewage overflow at cleanout → Immediate Hazard
5. Manholes & Lift Stations (IPC §801 / IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Manhole covers present and secure
•	No broken or displaced covers
•	No sewage seepage around manhole
•	Lift station pumps operating (audible/visual indicators)
•	No alarm indicators (flashing lights, audible alarms)
•	No sewage pooling around lift station
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing manhole cover → Immediate Hazard
•	Lift station overflow → Immediate Hazard
6. Drainage Interaction (IPC §801.3)
Inspect:
•	No sewage entering storm drains
•	No cross connection between sewer and stormwater
•	No wastewater flowing across walkways or parking lots
•	No sewage entering landscaping or planters

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Water Leak Inspection 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPC §601–604 / IPMC §302–304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior potable water lines
•	Exterior hose bibs/spigots
•	Exterior irrigation systems
•	Exterior water meters & backflow devices
•	Exterior building envelope leaks
•	Exterior wall/roof penetrations
•	Exterior drainage areas receiving water discharge
If no exterior water related components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Evidence of Water Leakage (IPC §604 / §701)
Inspect for:
•	Active dripping or flowing water
•	Wet soil or pavement with no rain present
•	Water stains on exterior walls
•	Efflorescence (white mineral deposits)
•	Mold like substance on exterior surfaces
•	Water pooling near foundation
•	Vegetation overgrowth caused by constant moisture
Hazard Severity:
•	Active water leak → Severe
•	Water pooling near foundation → Severe
3. Exterior Water Supply Piping (IPC §604.3)
Inspect:
•	Cracked, broken, or leaking pipes
•	Corroded copper or galvanized piping
•	Loose fittings or unions
•	Damaged insulation on exposed pipes
•	Improper materials (garden hoses used as supply lines)
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken pipe → Immediate Hazard
•	Corroded pipe leaking → Severe
4. Hose Bibs / Exterior Spigots
Inspect:
•	Dripping or leaking bibs
•	Loose handles or packing nuts
•	Missing vacuum breakers (required in most jurisdictions)
•	Water spraying from connection points
•	Damaged or missing anti siphon devices
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing vacuum breaker → Severe
•	Active leak → Severe
5. Irrigation Systems (IPC §603 / Backflow Protection)
Inspect:
•	Broken sprinkler heads
•	Constant running or seeping irrigation lines
•	Overspray onto building walls
•	Water pooling in landscape areas
•	Backflow device present and intact
•	No leaks at irrigation valves or manifolds
Hazard Severity:
•	Irrigation leak causing pooling → Severe
•	Backflow device damaged → Severe
6. Water Meter, Backflow Preventer & Vaults
Inspect:
•	Meter box free of standing water
•	No leaks at meter unions
•	No damaged or missing meter lids
•	Backflow preventer intact and not leaking
•	No corrosion compromising device integrity
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaking backflow preventer → Immediate Hazard
•	Standing water in meter vault → Severe
7. Exterior Building Envelope Water Intrusion (IBC §1805)
Inspect:
•	Water entering through siding, stucco, or brick
•	Damaged caulking at penetrations
•	Roof runoff hitting walls due to missing gutters
•	Water stains under windows or doors
•	Mold like substance on exterior wall
Hazard Severity:
•	Active water intrusion → Severe
•	Mold like substance → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Auxiliary Lighting & Exterior Light Fixtures
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §402–404 / IBC §1008)
Inspection applies to:
•	Building mounted exterior fixtures
•	Auxiliary lighting (security, signage, landscape, decorative)
•	Walkway/pathway lights
•	Parking lot pole lights
•	Stairway/landing lights
•	Breezeway/corridor lights
•	Garage exterior lights
•	Emergency/egress auxiliary lighting
If no exterior lighting exists → Not Applicable.
2. Fixture Condition (IPMC §304.15 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	No broken, cracked, or missing lenses
•	No exposed bulbs
•	No loose, unstable, or hanging fixtures
•	No rust, corrosion, or deterioration
•	No sharp edges or broken housings
•	No water intrusion inside fixture
•	No damaged or missing weatherproof gaskets
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose fixture at risk of falling → Immediate Hazard
•	Water inside fixture → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Illumination Performance (IBC §1008.2)
Inspect:
•	Adequate illumination for safe travel
•	No burned out bulbs
•	No flickering or intermittent operation
•	No dark spots in walkways, stairs, parking areas
•	Auxiliary lighting provides intended coverage (security, signage, landscape)
Hazard Severity:
•	Insufficient lighting in egress path → Severe
•	Burned out fixture in critical area → Severe
4. Electrical Safety (IFC §605 / IPMC §604)
Inspect:
•	No exposed wiring
•	No damaged conduit
•	No missing junction box covers
•	No overheating or burn marks
•	No water + electrical interaction
•	No loose electrical connections
•	No improperly spliced wires
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
5. Mounting & Structural Stability
Inspect:
•	Fixtures securely mounted
•	No loose brackets or arms
•	No leaning or unstable light poles
•	No rust at pole base
•	No cracks in concrete pole bases
•	No damaged mounting hardware
Hazard Severity:
•	Unstable pole → Immediate Hazard
•	Fixture detaching from wall → Immediate Hazard
6. Controls & Operation
Inspect:
•	Photocells functioning (lights turn on at dusk)
•	Timers operating correctly
•	Motion sensors responsive
•	No lights stuck “ON” or “OFF”
•	Auxiliary lighting operating per design (security, signage, landscape)
Hazard Severity:
•	Emergency/auxiliary lighting not functioning → Immediate Hazard
7. Auxiliary Lighting Categories
A. Security Lighting
Inspect:
•	Motion sensors functional
•	No blind spots
•	No glare affecting drivers or pedestrians
•	No exposed wiring
Hazard Severity:
•	Security light failure in high risk area → Severe
B. Signage Lighting
Inspect:
•	Sign lights intact
•	No flickering
•	No broken lenses
•	No water intrusion
Hazard Severity:
•	Sign lighting failure affecting navigation → Moderate/Severe
8. Egress & Emergency Auxiliary Lighting (IBC §1008 / IFC §1104)
Inspect:
•	Lighting present at all exterior exits
•	Lighting present along exit discharge path
•	No blocked or unlit stairways
•	No unlit ramps or landings
•	No missing emergency backup lighting (if required)
Hazard Severity:
•	Unlit exit discharge → Immediate Hazard
•	Emergency auxiliary lighting failure → Immediate Hazard

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Parking Lot, Driveway & Private Road Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302 / §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Parking lots (asphalt, concrete, gravel)
•	Driveways
•	Private roads within the property
•	Fire lanes
•	Loading zones
•	Vehicle circulation paths
•	Pedestrian crossings within vehicle areas
If no exterior vehicle use areas exist → Not Applicable.
2. Surface Condition (IPMC §302.3 / IBC §1003.2)
Inspect:
•	No potholes, depressions, or sinkholes
•	No broken, cracked, or heaving pavement
•	No loose gravel creating slip hazards
•	No standing water after normal weather
•	No oil slicks or slippery contaminants
•	No exposed rebar or reinforcing mesh
Hazard Severity:
•	Potholes creating trip or vehicle hazards → Severe
•	Standing water in pedestrian or vehicle paths → Severe
•	Exposed rebar → Immediate Hazard
3. Striping, Markings & Signage (IPMC §302.7)
Inspect:
•	Parking stall striping visible and intact
•	Fire lane striping visible and unobstructed
•	Accessible parking signage present and readable
•	Directional arrows and lane markings visible
•	Speed limit and stop signs present where required
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing fire lane markings → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing accessible parking signage → Severe
4. Curbs, Wheel Stops & Edges
Inspect:
•	No broken or displaced wheel stops
•	No cracked or deteriorated curbs
•	No sharp edges on damaged concrete
•	No wheel stops creating trip hazards
•	No curbs obstructing drainage flow
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken wheel stop causing trip hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp curb edges → Immediate Hazard
5. Drainage & Water Flow (IBC §1805 / IPMC §302.3)
Inspect:
•	No ponding water in drive lanes or parking stalls
•	No blocked storm drains or catch basins
•	No erosion at pavement edges
•	No water flowing toward building foundation
•	No sediment buildup restricting drainage
Hazard Severity:
•	Ponding in vehicle or pedestrian paths → Severe
•	Water undermining pavement → Immediate Hazard
6. Fire Department Access (IFC §503–505)
Inspect:
•	Fire lanes unobstructed
•	No parked vehicles blocking fire access
•	No vegetation encroaching fire lanes
•	Fire department connection (FDC) accessible
•	No gates or barriers restricting emergency access
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked fire lane → Immediate Hazard
7. Lighting & Visibility (IPMC §402 / IBC §1008)
Inspect:
•	Adequate illumination for nighttime use
•	No burned out pole lights
•	No flickering or dim fixtures
•	No dark zones in drive lanes or parking areas
•	No vegetation blocking lighting
Hazard Severity:
•	Insufficient lighting in vehicle/pedestrian areas → Severe
8. Pedestrian Safety (IBC §1003 / IPMC §302)
Inspect:
•	Marked pedestrian paths visible
•	No trip hazards at crosswalks
•	No broken sidewalks adjacent to parking areas
•	No abrupt level changes (>½ inch)
•	No slippery algae or oil residue
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard in pedestrian path → Immediate Hazard
9. Vehicle Barriers & Guardrails (IBC §1607.7)
Inspect:
•	Guardrails present where required (drop offs, retaining walls)
•	No loose or damaged barriers
•	No rust compromising structural integrity

outside.deficiencySelected: Paint outside on a target property is deteriorated, above the level required for lead-safe work practices by a lead-certified firm, and passing clearance.
outside.deficiencyDetail: Paint is deteriorated. (e.g., peeling, chipping, chalking,or detached from the substrate)For large surface areas in the Unit, deteriorated paint is more than 20 square feet (“significant”).
outside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Paint is deteriorated (e.g., peeling, chipping, chalking, cracking, or detached from the substrate). For large surface areas in the Unit, deteriorated paint is more than 2 square feet, per room; for small surface areas, greater than 10% per component (“significant”)
outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Outside Exterior Paint + Lead Based Hazard Inspection
1. Exterior Paint Condition (IPMC §304.2)
Inspect:
•	No peeling, flaking, chipping, blistering
•	No bare wood or exposed substrate
•	No chalking or powdering
•	No rust on metal components
•	No paint loss from moisture intrusion
Hazard Severity:
•	Peeling/chipping paint → Severe
•	Bare wood → Severe
•	Paint loss exposing structural deterioration → Immediate Hazard
3. Lead Based Paint Risk Indicators (EPA / HUD LSHR)
Inspect:
•	Deteriorated paint on pre 1978 structures
•	Paint debris on ground
•	Paint chips in soil or landscaping
•	Friction surfaces (doors, windows) with paint wear
•	Impact surfaces (rails, stairs) with paint damage
•	Soil within 3 feet of building for paint chips
Hazard Severity:
•	Deteriorated paint on pre 1978 building → Immediate Hazard
•	Paint chips in soil → Immediate Hazard
4. Moisture & Weather Exposure (IPMC §304.1)
Inspect:
•	No water intrusion causing paint failure
•	No damaged caulking or sealants
•	No rot or deterioration under paint
•	No mold like substance on painted surfaces
Hazard Severity:
•	Moisture damaged paint exposing substrate → Immediate Hazard

outside.deficiencySelected: Guardrail
outside.deficiencyDetail: A guardrail is deficient if it’s missing or not installed along a walking surface over 30 inches above the floor or grade in areas accessible to residents. Limiting its safe use
outside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: The guardrail is missing (i.e., evidence of prior installation but is now not present or is incomplete) or not installed (i.e., never installed, but should have been) along a walking surface that is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below.
outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Guardrail & Handrail Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1011–1015 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior stair handrails
•	Exterior balcony/landing guardrails
•	Exterior walkway guardrails
•	Exterior ramps and accessible routes
•	Exterior decks, porches, breezeways
•	Any elevated walking surface ≥ 30 inches above grade
If no exterior railings exist → Not Applicable.
2. Guardrail Requirements (IBC §1015)
A. Presence & Height
Inspect:
•	Guardrails present at all elevated surfaces ≥30"
•	Guardrail height ≥ 42 inches (ICC standard)
•	No missing sections
B. Openings & Safety
Inspect:
•	No openings > 4 inches
•	No climbable horizontal elements
•	No gaps at bottom of guardrail
•	No broken or missing balusters
C. Structural Stability
Inspect:
•	Guardrail firmly attached
•	No wobbling, movement, or loose posts
•	No rust, rot, or deterioration
•	No separation from wall or deck
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose/wobbly guardrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Openings >4" → Severe
•	Missing guardrail → Immediate Hazard
3. Handrail Requirements (IBC §1011–1014)
A. Presence & Height
Inspect:
•	Handrail present on stairs with ≥4 risers
•	Height between 34–38 inches
•	Continuous along full stair run
B. Graspability
Inspect:
•	Graspable profile (round/oval)
•	No wide, flat boards
•	Ends return to wall (no snag hazards)
C. Condition
Inspect:
•	No cracks, breaks, or splinters
•	No rust or rot
•	No loose brackets
•	No sharp edges or protruding fasteners
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing handrail → Severe
•	Loose handrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
4. Structural Condition (IPMC §304 / §305)
Inspect:
•	No cracked wood or metal
•	No rot, corrosion, or termite damage
•	No unstable posts or brackets
•	No sagging or bending under pressure
•	No separation from mounting surface
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural failure risk → Immediate Hazard
5. Stair, Ramp & Landing Interaction (IBC §1003)
Inspect:
•	Handrail present on required side
•	Guardrail present on open side of landing
•	No trip hazards affecting safe use
•	Adequate lighting for nighttime use
•	No obstructions blocking grasping of handrail
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard + missing/loose railing → Immediate Hazard
6. Surface Condition
Inspect:
•	No peeling paint exposing sharp edges
•	No rust flakes or splinters
•	No rough surfaces causing injury
•	No loose decorative elements
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Rust/rot compromising strength → Severe
7. Child Safety (IBC §1015.4)
Inspect:
•	No openings >4 inches
•	No climbable horizontal elements
•	No protruding fasteners
•	No gaps at bottom of guardrail
Hazard Severity:
•	Climbable guardrail → Severe
•	Large openings → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Roof & Roof Assembly Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1501–1507 / IPMC §304)
Inspection applies to:
•	Roof coverings (shingle, tile, metal, membrane)
•	Roof sheathing (visible edges)
•	Roof flashing (edge, valley, chimney, vent)
•	Roof penetrations (vents, pipes, skylights)
•	Roof drainage (gutters, downspouts, scuppers)
•	Roof edge protection (drip edge, fascia)
•	Roof structural elements (visible rafters, trusses)
•	Parapets, coping, roof mounted equipment
If no exterior roof exposure exists → Not Applicable.
2. Roof Covering Condition (IBC §1507)
Inspect:
•	Missing, broken, or loose shingles/tiles
•	Curling, blistering, or delaminated shingles
•	Cracked or displaced tiles
•	Exposed underlayment
•	Ponding water on flat roofs
•	Membrane bubbles, tears, or open seams
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing roof covering → Severe
•	Exposed underlayment → Severe
•	Ponding water → Severe
•	Torn membrane → Immediate Hazard (active leak risk)
3. Flashing & Weather Protection (IBC §1503.2)
Inspect:
•	Loose or missing flashing
•	Rusted or corroded metal flashing
•	Improperly sealed joints
•	Gaps at roof to wall intersections
•	Damaged valley flashing
•	Missing or damaged drip edge
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing flashing → Immediate Hazard
•	Open flashing gaps → Severe
4. Roof Penetrations (IBC §1503.3)
Inspect:
•	Vent boots cracked or deteriorated
•	Gaps around plumbing vents
•	Loose or damaged skylight frames
•	Missing or deteriorated skylight seals
•	HVAC penetrations not sealed
•	Chimney flashing loose or rusted
Hazard Severity:
•	Failed vent boot → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose skylight frame → Immediate Hazard
5. Roof Drainage System (IBC §1503.4 / IPMC §304.7)
Inspect:
•	Gutters intact and securely fastened
•	No sagging or detached gutters
•	Downspouts connected and discharging properly
•	No blockages (leaves, debris)
•	No water overflowing gutters
•	Scuppers and roof drains clear
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked drainage causing overflow → Severe
•	Detached gutter creating falling hazard → Immediate Hazard
6. Roof Edge, Fascia & Soffits
Inspect:
•	Fascia boards intact (no rot or separation)
•	Soffits intact (no holes or missing panels)
•	No pest entry points
•	No peeling paint exposing bare wood
•	No loose or falling trim
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose fascia/soffit → Immediate Hazard
•	Pest entry through soffit → Severe
7. Roof Structure (Visible Exterior Portions)
Inspect:
•	Sagging roofline
•	Visible structural deformation
•	Rotting or deteriorated rafters (at eaves)
•	Termite damage at exposed wood
•	Cracked or displaced parapet walls
•	Loose coping stones
Hazard Severity:
•	Sagging roof → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose parapet coping → Immediate Hazard
8. Roof Mounted Equipment (IBC §1509)
Inspect:
•	HVAC units securely mounted
•	No loose brackets or supports
•	No exposed wiring
•	No water pooling around equipment
•	No damaged or missing equipment flashing
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose roof mounted equipment → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
9. Safety Hazards
Inspect:
•	Falling hazards (loose tiles, shingles, fascia)
•	Sharp edges from damaged metal roofing
•	Trip hazards on accessible roof areas
•	Water intrusion into electrical components
•	Debris accumulation creating fire hazard
Hazard Severity:
•	Falling roof components → Immediate Hazard

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Sidewalk, Walkway & Ramp Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §302–304 / IBC §1003)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior sidewalks (concrete, asphalt, pavers)
•	Exterior pedestrian walkways
•	Exterior ramps (ADA or standard)
•	Breezeway walk paths
•	Pathways connecting parking lots to buildings
•	Exterior landings at stairs and ramps
•	Accessible routes
If no exterior pedestrian surfaces exist → Not Applicable.
2. Surface Condition (IPMC §302.3 / IBC §1003.2)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, breaks, or spalling
•	No heaving or settlement creating level changes
•	No holes, depressions, or missing sections
•	No loose pavers or bricks
•	No slippery surfaces (algae, moss, oil)
•	No exposed rebar or reinforcing mesh
Hazard Severity:
•	Level change > ½ inch → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed rebar → Immediate Hazard
•	Slippery algae/oil → Severe
3. Trip Hazards (IBC §1003 / NSPIRE)
Inspect:
•	Uneven slabs
•	Tree root uplift
•	Broken edges
•	Gaps between slabs
•	Loose or rocking pavers
•	Abrupt transitions at ramps or landings
Hazard Severity:
•	Any trip hazard in pedestrian path → Immediate Hazard
4. Ramp Requirements (IBC §1010 / ADA A117.1)
A. Slope & Rise
Inspect:
•	Slope ≤ 1:12 (8.33%) for accessible ramps
•	Cross slope ≤ 1:48
•	No excessive rise without landings
B. Landings
Inspect:
•	Level landings at top and bottom
•	Minimum landing length 60 inches
•	No obstructions in landing area
C. Handrails (if required)
Inspect:
•	Present on ramps with rise >6 inches
•	Height 34–38 inches
•	Continuous and graspable
Hazard Severity:
•	Ramp slope exceeding ADA limits → Severe
•	Missing required handrails → Severe
•	Obstructed landing → Immediate Hazard
5. Drainage & Water Flow (IBC §1805 / IPMC §302.3)
Inspect:
•	No ponding water on sidewalks or ramps
•	No water flowing across walkways
•	No blocked drainage grates
•	No erosion at walkway edges
•	No water directed toward building foundation
Hazard Severity:
•	Ponding water in walkway → Severe
•	Water undermining walkway → Immediate Hazard
6. Obstructions & Clearance (IBC §1003.6)
Inspect:
•	No vegetation blocking walkway
•	No debris, trash, or stored items
•	No protruding objects reducing headroom (<80 inches)
•	No signage or fixtures obstructing path
•	No vehicles blocking pedestrian routes
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstruction in accessible route → Immediate Hazard
7. Accessible Route Compliance (ADA / ANSI A117.1)
Inspect:
•	Clear width ≥ 36 inches
•	No abrupt level changes > ¼ inch
•	Proper ramp slope and landings
•	No gaps > ½ inch
•	Detectable warnings at curb ramps (if required)
Hazard Severity:
•	Non compliant accessible route → Severe
•	Missing detectable warnings → Severe

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Steps & Stairs Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1003 / §1011)
Inspection applies to:
•	Exterior stairways
•	Exterior steps (single or multiple)
•	Exterior landings
•	Exterior stair towers
•	Breezeway/porch steps
•	Exterior access stairs to units, laundry rooms, garages, community rooms
If no exterior steps/stairs exist → Not Applicable.
2. Tread & Riser Requirements (IBC §1011.5)
Inspect:
•	Treads uniform in depth
•	Risers uniform in height
•	No excessive variation (trip hazard)
•	No open risers that violate safety requirements
•	No slippery surfaces (algae, moss, oil, water)
Hazard Severity:
•	Non uniform risers/treads → Severe
•	Slippery stair surfaces → Severe
3. Handrail Requirements (IBC §1011.11 / §1014)
Inspect:
•	Handrail present on stairs with ≥4 risers
•	Height between 34–38 inches
•	Secure mounting (no wobbling)
•	Continuous along full stair run
•	Ends return to wall (no snag hazards)
•	Graspable profile
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing handrail → Severe
•	Loose handrail → Immediate Hazard
4. Guardrail Requirements (IBC §1015)
Inspect:
•	Guardrail present on open sides of landings or stairs
•	Height ≥ 42 inches
•	Openings < 4 inches
•	No climbable horizontal elements
•	No loose posts or sections
Hazard Severity:
•	Guardrail openings >4 inches → Severe
•	Missing or loose guardrail → Immediate Hazard
5. Landings (IBC §1011.6)
Inspect:
•	Landing present at top and bottom of stairs
•	Landing surface level and stable
•	No trip hazards
•	No obstructions blocking landing
•	Adequate size for safe use
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard on landing → Immediate Hazard
6. Lighting & Visibility (IBC §1003.2)
Inspect:
•	Adequate lighting for nighttime use
•	No dark areas or shadows hiding steps
•	No missing or burned out bulbs
•	Switches operable
Hazard Severity:
•	Insufficient lighting causing safety risk → Severe
7. Moisture & Water Intrusion (IPMC §304.2)
Inspect:
•	No water pooling on steps
•	No moisture causing slippery surfaces
•	No mold like substance on stair surfaces
•	No water damage to wood or metal stair components
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical interaction near stair lighting → Immediate Hazard

outside.deficiencySelected: Structural system exhibits signs of serious failure.

outside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Structural system exhibits signs of serious failure and may threaten the resident’s safety.
outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Structural System Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §304 / IBC Chapters 16–23)
Inspection applies to all exterior structural components:
•	Foundations & footings
•	Exterior load bearing walls
•	Columns, posts, piers
•	Beams, headers, lintels
•	Balconies, decks, stair towers
•	Parapets, retaining walls
•	Structural framing (wood, steel, masonry, concrete)
•	Roof structural elements (visible portions)
If no exterior structural elements are exposed → Not Applicable.
2. Foundations & Footings (IBC §1807–1809)
Inspect for:
•	Cracks (vertical, horizontal, diagonal, step cracks)
•	Spalling, delamination, exposed aggregate
•	Exposed or corroded rebar
•	Settlement, heaving, or displacement
•	Separation between foundation and exterior wall
•	Soil erosion undermining foundation
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural displacement or bulging → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed rebar → Severe
•	Settlement affecting stability → Immediate Hazard
3. Exterior Load Bearing Walls (IBC §1403 / §1607)
Inspect for:
•	Cracks in masonry or stucco
•	Loose bricks, blocks, or stone
•	Bowing or bulging walls
•	Rotting or deteriorated wood framing
•	Rusting steel components
•	Separation at wall to foundation or wall to roof connections
Hazard Severity:
•	Bowing/bulging wall → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose masonry → Immediate Hazard
•	Rot or rust compromising strength → Severe
4. Columns, Posts & Piers (IBC §1607 / §2304)
Inspect for:
•	Leaning or out of plumb posts
•	Rot, rust, or termite damage
•	Cracked or spalled concrete piers
•	Loose or deteriorated connections
•	Settlement at post bases
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaning structural post → Immediate Hazard
•	Rot/rust compromising load capacity → Severe
5. Beams, Headers & Lintels (IBC §2304 / §2104)
Inspect for:
•	Sagging or deflection
•	Cracked or split wood beams
•	Rusted steel lintels
•	Loose or missing fasteners
•	Deteriorated bearing points
Hazard Severity:
•	Sagging beam → Immediate Hazard
•	Rusted lintel affecting masonry support → Severe
6. Balconies, Decks & Exterior Walkways (IBC §1607.8)
Inspect for:
•	Rotting deck boards or joists
•	Loose or unstable balcony supports
•	Rusted metal connections
•	Cracked or spalled concrete decks
•	Loose guardrails or handrails
•	Water intrusion at deck ledger
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose balcony support → Immediate Hazard
•	Ledger failure risk → Immediate Hazard

outside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Exterior Wall & Retaining Wall Inspection
1. Exterior Wall Structural Condition (IBC §1403 / §1607)
Inspect:
•	Cracks (vertical, horizontal, diagonal, step cracks)
•	Bulging, bowing, or leaning walls
•	Loose bricks, blocks, stone, or siding
•	Spalling, delamination, or surface loss
•	Rot, rust, or termite damage
•	Separation at wall to foundation or wall to roof joints
•	Moisture intrusion causing deterioration
Hazard Severity:
•	Bowing/bulging wall → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose masonry → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural separation → Immediate Hazard
•	Rot/rust compromising strength → Severe
2. Exterior Wall Surface Condition (IPMC §304.2)
Inspect:
•	Peeling, flaking, or blistering paint
•	Cracked or deteriorated stucco
•	Damaged siding (vinyl, wood, fiber cement, metal)
•	Missing siding panels or trim
•	Exposed sheathing or framing
•	Efflorescence indicating moisture intrusion
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing siding exposing structure → Severe
•	Moisture intrusion → Severe
3. Wall Penetrations & Openings (IBC §1405)
Inspect:
•	Gaps around windows, doors, vents, pipes
•	Damaged or missing caulking/sealant
•	Loose or missing exterior fixtures
•	Improperly sealed utility penetrations
•	Pest entry points
Hazard Severity:
•	Open penetration allowing water intrusion → Severe
•	Pest entry point → Moderate/Severe
4 Veneer Systems (Brick, Stone, Manufactured Stone) (IBC §1405.6)
Inspect:
•	Loose veneer units
•	Cracked or deteriorated mortar joints
•	Missing or damaged weep holes
•	Separation between veneer and structural wall
•	Rusted or missing lintels supporting veneer
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose veneer → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing lintel support → Severe
5. Parapet Walls (IBC §1617)
Inspect:
•	Loose or leaning parapets
•	Cracked or deteriorated coping
•	Missing or loose coping stones
•	Water intrusion at parapet joints
•	Separation from roof membrane
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaning parapet → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose coping → Immediate Hazard
6. Retaining Wall Structural Condition (IBC §1807)
Inspect:
•	Leaning or tilting retaining walls
•	Cracks indicating soil pressure
•	Bulging or displacement
•	Missing or deteriorated mortar
•	Soil erosion at base or behind wall
•	Water pressure buildup (no drainage)
•	Failed or missing drainage weep holes
Hazard Severity:
•	Leaning retaining wall → Immediate Hazard
•	Bulging/displacement → Immediate Hazard
•	Soil pressure cracks → Severe

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Cabinets & Storage 
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305 / §309)
Inspection applies to all interior common area storage:
•	Hallway storage closets
•	Maintenance closets
•	Janitorial closets
•	Laundry area storage
•	Mechanical room storage cabinets
•	Storage rooms accessible to residents or staff
•	Built in cabinets, shelving, and storage enclosures
If no interior common area storage exists → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Condition (IPMC §305.4 / §305.5)
Inspect:
•	Cabinets securely mounted (no looseness or detachment)
•	Shelves intact (no cracks, breaks, or missing supports)
•	No rot, swelling, delamination, or structural failure
•	No sharp edges, splintered wood, or protruding fasteners
•	No holes exposing framing or pest pathways
Hazard Severity:
•	Collapse risk → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural failure (broken shelves, loose cabinet) → Severe
3. Operability (IPMC §305.3)
Inspect:
•	Doors open/close fully
•	Hinges secure and not bent
•	Drawer tracks functioning
•	Cabinet pulls/handles secure
•	Shelves stable under light load
•	Closet rods secure and properly supported
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable door creating obstruction → Severe
•	Loose hardware → Moderate

inside.deficiencySelected: System does not function properly.
inside.deficiencyDetail: A call-for-Aid system does not emit sound or light or send signal to annunciator.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: A call-for-aid system does not emit sound or light or send signal to annunciator.
OR

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Call for Aid System Inspection
1. Device Presence & Accessibility (IBC §1009.8 / ADA)
Inspect:
•	Call for aid device present where required
•	Device reachable (34–48 inches AFF typical)
•	No obstructions blocking access
•	Pull cord length adequate (reaches floor or near floor)
•	Clear signage identifying emergency device
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing required device → Immediate Hazard
•	Obstructed or unreachable device → Severe
2 Operability & Function (IPMC §604 / NFPA 72)
Inspect:
•	Device activates alarm when pulled/pressed
•	Audible alarm loud enough to be heard in common area
•	Visual alarm (strobe) activates if required
•	Monitoring panel receives signal
•	No delayed or failed activation
•	No intermittent or false alarms
Hazard Severity:
•	Device not functioning → Immediate Hazard
•	Alarm not audible/visible → Severe
3. Physical Condition of Device
Inspect:
•	No broken pull cords
•	No frayed or damaged cords
•	No missing pull handles
•	No cracked or broken call buttons
•	No loose or unstable mounting
•	No missing covers or faceplates
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken pull cord → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose device at risk of falling → Immediate Hazard
4. Alarm Notification Appliances (NFPA 72)
Inspect:
•	Audible alarms functioning
•	Visual strobes functioning
•	No blocked or covered alarm devices
•	No excessive dust or debris on alarm units
•	No loose or damaged alarm housings
Hazard Severity:
•	Non functioning alarm → Immediate Hazard
5. Monitoring Panel / Annunciator (IBC §1009.10)
Inspect:
•	Panel powered and operational
•	No trouble or fault indicators
•	No missing labels or zone indicators
•	No loose wiring or damaged components
•	Panel accessible to staff
Hazard Severity:
•	Panel in “trouble” or “fault” mode → Severe
•	Panel not receiving signals → Immediate Hazard
6. Fire & Life Safety (IBC §1003 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	No storage blocking electrical panels or shutoff valves
•	No combustible storage near heat producing appliances
•	No damaged wiring inside or near cabinets
•	No storage blocking egress pathways
•	No overloaded shelves creating falling hazards
Hazard Severity:
•	Combustibles near electrical/heat source → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked electrical panel → Immediate Hazard
•	Storage blocking egress → Immediate Hazard
7. Accessibility (ICC A117.1 / ISO 21542)
(Where applicable)
Inspect:
•	Reachable storage heights
•	Operable hardware (one hand operation, no tight grasping)
•	Clear floor space in front of storage
•	No obstructions limiting access
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstructed accessible storage → Severe

inside.inspectionProtocol:
Message Copilot
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Carbon Monoxide Alarm Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IRC §315 / IPMC §604–702)
Inspection applies to CO alarms located in:
•	Interior hallways serving dwelling units
•	Interior corridors connecting units to exits
•	Mechanical rooms (boilers, furnaces, water heaters)
•	Laundry rooms with gas dryers
•	Storage rooms containing fuel burning equipment
•	Garage adjacent interior areas
•	Any interior common area where CO exposure is possible
If CO alarms are missing in required areas → Immediate Hazard.
2. Required Presence & Placement (IRC §315.1)
Inspect:
•	CO alarms installed outside sleeping areas and in hallways serving units
•	CO alarms installed on every story containing fuel burning appliances
•	CO alarms installed inside or immediately outside mechanical rooms
•	CO alarms installed near gas fired boilers, furnaces, water heaters
•	CO alarms installed near gas dryers
•	Alarms mounted per manufacturer instructions (wall or ceiling)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing CO alarm in hallway or fuel burning area → Immediate Hazard
4. Power Source & Electrical Safety (IPMC §604)
Inspect:
•	Battery present and properly seated
•	No missing battery backup (for hardwired units)
•	No low battery chirping
•	Hardwired units securely connected
•	No open junction boxes
•	No water intrusion near electrical components
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing battery → Severe
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
5. Expiration & Compliance
Inspect:
•	Manufacture date on back of alarm
•	CO alarms expire at 7–10 years
•	Replace if expired or date unreadable
•	UL listed or equivalent certification
Hazard Severity:
•	Expired CO alarm → Immediate Hazard
6. Functional Test (NFPA 720). Ask for a certificate
Inspect:
•	Press TEST button ( If  individual)
•	Audible alarm activates
•	Visual indicator activates (LED or display)
•	For combination alarms: verify CO function, not just smoke
•	Hardwired/interconnected alarms activate other units
•	Reset function operates correctly
Hazard Severity:
•	Alarm fails to sound → Immediate Hazard
7. Hallway Specific Requirements
Inspect:
•	Alarm audible throughout hallway
•	Alarm not obstructed by décor, furniture, or signage
•	Alarm placed away from HVAC supply vents
•	Alarm placed away from dead air spaces (corners, ceiling peaks)
Hazard Severity:
•	Alarm obstructed or inaudible in hallway → Severe

inside.deficiencySelected: carbon monoxide alarm is missing, not installed or not installed in the proper location.
inside.deficiencyDetail: The location of the previous installation is not relevant. building contains a fuel-burning appliance or a fuel-burning fireplace. Carbon monoxide  alarm is missing alarms ( sleeping areas, laundry, mechanical room, remote furnaces,a nd water heater area) or a garage attached to the building, making the area noncompliant.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: One (1) or more of the following scenarios exists:

  1.    Unit contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace, and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:  
    a. in the immediate vicinity of each sleeping area.   
  OR
    b. within each bedroom.

  2. Bedroom or bathroom attached to bedroom:

  a. contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace.
 OR
  b. has adjacent spaces from which byproducts of combustion gases can flow.
 AND 
  c. Carbon monoxide alarm is not installed in each bedroom.    

3. Unit or sleeping area is served by a forced-air furnace that is located elsewhere and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
 a. in the immediate vicinity of each bedroom.
 OR
  b. within each bedroom.
 OR
c. within the room or area with the first duct register and the carbon monoxide alarm signals are automatically transmitted to an approved location

4. Unit or bedroom area is located in a building that contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace and:     
  a.    a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed in an approved location between the fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace and the Unit or bedroom
OR 
 b. a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed on the ceiling of the room containing the fuel burning appliance       or fuel-burning fireplace. 
OR
 c. the Unit or bedroom has communicated openings to the fuel-burning appliance or fuel burning fireplace and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
      i. in the immediate vicinity of each bedroom.
 OR
      ii. within each bedroom

5. Unit or bedroom is located one (1) story or less above or below an attached private garage that:
    a. does not have natural ventilation.
 OR
    b. is enclosed and does not have a ventilation system for vehicle exhaust.
 AND 
  c. Carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
      i. in the immediate vicinity of each sleeping area.
 OR
     ii. within each sleeping area.

Inspect:
•	Press TEST button ( If  individual)
•	Audible alarm activates
•	Visual indicator activates (LED or display)
•	For combination alarms: verify CO function, not just smoke
•	Hardwired/interconnected alarms activate other units
•	Reset function operates correctly
Hazard Severity:
•	Alarm fails to sound → Immediate Hazard

Inspect:
•	Alarm audible throughout hallway
•	Alarm not obstructed by décor, furniture, or signage
•	Alarm placed away from HVAC supply vents

•	Alarm obstructed or inaudible in hallway → Severe
