inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Ceiling & Ceiling Component Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305 / IBC §703–711)
Inspection applies to ceilings and ceiling components in:
•	Hallways & corridors
•	Stair towers
•	Lobbies
•	Laundry rooms
•	Community rooms
•	Storage rooms
•	Mechanical rooms
•	Any interior common area
If no ceiling surface exists → Not Applicable.
2. Ceiling Surface Condition (IPMC §305.3)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, holes, or missing sections
•	No sagging or separation from framing
•	No loose or falling ceiling tiles
•	No peeling paint, delamination, or blistering
•	No exposed gypsum board or insulation
Hazard Severity:
•	Sagging ceiling → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing ceiling sections → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose tiles at risk of falling → Immediate Hazard
3. Moisture, Water Intrusion & Staining (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect:
•	Water stains or discoloration
•	Active leaks or dampness
•	Soft, swollen, or deteriorated ceiling materials
•	Mold like substance
•	Bubbling or peeling paint from moisture
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Moisture damaged ceiling at risk of collapse → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance → Severe
4. Ceiling Components, Fixtures & Attachments (IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Light fixtures securely mounted
•	No loose or unstable fixtures
•	No damaged or missing fixture covers
•	No water intrusion into fixtures
•	No loose ceiling fans or mechanical units
•	No exposed wiring at fixtures
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose fixture → Immediate Hazard
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
5. HVAC, Mechanical & Utility Interaction (IMC / IPMC §304)
Inspect:
•	No condensation dripping from ducts
•	No damaged or missing HVAC diffusers
•	No gaps around duct penetrations
•	No rust or corrosion on mechanical supports
•	No ceiling damage caused by mechanical equipment
Hazard Severity:
•	Condensation causing ceiling deterioration → Severe
•	Mechanical equipment damaging ceiling → Severe
6. Suspended Ceiling Systems (Tiles & Grid)
Inspect:
•	Tiles properly seated in grid
•	No broken, cracked, or warped tiles
•	No missing tiles
•	Grid intact (no bent or loose sections)
•	No sagging tiles from moisture
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing tile → Immediate Hazard
•	Sagging tile → Immediate Hazard
7. Structural Integrity (IPMC §305.2)
Inspect:
•	No structural cracks indicating movement
•	No ceiling bowing or deformation
•	No separation between ceiling and wall junctions
•	No failing plaster or gypsum board
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural failure risk → Immediate Hazard
•	
•	Trip hazards from ceiling debris → Immediate Hazard

inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA:   A visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is incomplete (i.e., evidence of a previously installed component that is now not present) such that it may not safely contain fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior. 
OR
 A visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is damaged (i.e., visibly defective; impacts functionality) such that it may not safely contain fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Chimney Inspection
Multi Unit Residential Property
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §717 / IPMC §305)
Inspection applies to:
•	Chimney structural walls (masonry, concrete, metal)
•	Chimney chases and shafts
•	Chimney enclosures (fire rated gypsum board assemblies)
•	Chimney supports, anchors, and bracing
•	Chimney penetrations through floors, ceilings, and walls
•	Chimney structure visible in common areas or mechanical rooms
If no chimney structure is present → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Masonry / Chimney Wall Condition (IRC §1001 / IBC §2101)
Inspect:
•	No loose bricks, blocks, or stone
•	No cracked, spalled, or delaminated masonry
•	No deteriorated or missing mortar joints
•	No bulging, bowing, or leaning chimney walls
•	No separation between chimney and adjacent building structure
•	No signs of structural movement (step cracks, shear cracks)
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose masonry → Immediate Hazard
•	Bulging or leaning chimney → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural separation → Immediate Hazard
3. Chimney Chase / Shaft Structural Integrity (IBC §717)
Inspect:
•	Chase walls intact (no holes, gaps, missing sections)
•	No sagging or deformation of chase structure
•	No damaged or missing fire blocking
•	No separation at chase corners or joints
•	No structural cracks indicating movement
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing fire blocking → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural deformation → Immediate Hazard
4. Chimney Supports, Anchors & Bracing (IBC §1607 / §2304)
Inspect:
•	No loose or missing metal straps or anchors
•	No rusted or corroded support hardware
•	No deteriorated wood supports (rot, termite damage)
•	No failing brackets or fasteners
•	No sagging or unsupported chimney sections
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing or failed structural supports → Immediate Hazard
•	Rusted anchors compromising stability → Severe
5. Penetrations Through Floors, Ceilings & Walls (IBC §714)
Inspect:
•	No unprotected penetrations at floor/ceiling transitions
•	No gaps around chimney where it passes through assemblies
•	No missing fire rated collars or fire stopping
•	No exposed framing or insulation at penetration points
Hazard Severity:
•	Open penetration in fire rated assembly → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing fire stopping → Immediate Hazard
6. Chimney Flue Structural Indicators (IRC §1002)
(Structural only — not operational venting)
Inspect:
•	No visible cracks in flue tile (if exposed)
•	No missing or displaced flue sections
•	No soot leakage indicating structural breach
•	No gaps between flue and chimney wall
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural breach allowing soot leakage → Immediate Hazard

inside.deficiencySelected: Dryer transition duct is constructed of unsuitable material.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol  Common Area Clothes Dryer Exhaust Ventilation Inspection
1. Transition Duct Requirements (IMC §504.4)
Inspect:
•	Transition duct present and securely attached
•	Metal duct only (rigid or semi rigid)
•	No plastic, vinyl, or foil flex ducting
•	No crushed, kinked, or restricted duct sections
•	No excessive length or unsupported runs
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing or detached duct → Immediate Hazard
•	Improper material (plastic/vinyl/foil) → Immediate Hazard
•	Crushed/kinked duct restricting airflow → Severe
2. Exhaust Duct Requirements (IMC §504.6)
Inspect:
•	Exhaust duct runs to exterior (never into interior spaces)
•	Duct continuous and unobstructed
•	No open seams, gaps, or disconnected sections
•	No excessive lint accumulation
•	No shared ducting between multiple dryers unless manufacturer approved
Hazard Severity:
•	Venting into interior → Immediate Hazard
•	Disconnected duct → Immediate Hazard
•	Heavy lint accumulation → Severe
3. Vent Termination (IMC §504.6.1)
Inspect:
•	Exterior termination unobstructed
•	No screens installed (prohibited)
•	Backdraft damper present and operable
•	No lint buildup blocking termination
•	No damaged or missing vent hood
Hazard Severity:
•	Screen installed → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked termination → Severe
4 Dryer Condition & Installation (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Dryer securely installed
•	No excessive vibration
•	No damaged or missing lint filter
•	No lint accumulation around dryer body
•	No combustibles stored near dryer
Hazard Severity:
•	Combustibles near dryer → Immediate Hazard
•	Lint accumulation indicating fire risk → Severe
5. Gas Dryer Safety (IFGC §501–503)
(If applicable)
Inspect:
•	No gas odor
•	Gas shutoff valve present and operable
•	No damaged or corroded gas piping
•	No gaps at gas connection
•	No soot staining (indicates combustion failure)
Hazard Severity:
•	Gas odor → Immediate Hazard
•	Damaged gas piping → Immediate Hazard

inside.deficiencyDetail: Entry door cannot be secured.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Entry door cannot be secured  (i.e. access controlled) by at least 1 installed lock.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Door Inspection
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1010 / IPMC §305)
Inspection applies to all interior common area doors including:
•	Building entry doors (lobby, vestibule, corridor access)
•	Fire labeled doors (stairwells, mechanical rooms, rated corridors)
•	General interior doors (laundry, storage, community rooms)
•	Garage separation doors (interior door between building and attached garage)
If no interior common area doors exist → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Condition (IPMC §305.2)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, holes, delamination, or warping
•	No loose or unstable door panels
•	No damaged frames, jambs, or stops
•	No protruding fasteners or sharp edges
•	No rot, rust, or corrosion on metal doors
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose or unstable door → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural failure (warping, delamination) → Severe
3. Operability & Egress (IBC §1010)
Inspect:
•	Door opens/closes fully without binding
•	No excessive force required
•	Latch engages properly
•	No obstructions blocking door swing
•	Panic hardware (if present) operates correctly
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable door blocking egress → Immediate Hazard
•	Obstructed door → Immediate Hazard
4. Entry Doors (Lobby, Corridor Access)
Inspect:
•	Operable lock or latch (if required)
•	No broken glazing
•	Weather stripping intact (if exterior connected)
•	Door closers functioning (if installed)
•	No daylight gaps indicating misalignment
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken glazing → Immediate Hazard
•	Entry door not latching → Severe
5. Fire Labeled Doors (IBC §716 / IFC §703)
Inspect:
•	Fire label present and legible
•	Door fully closes and self latches

inside.deficiencySelected: Entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is damaged, inoperable or missing
inside.deficiencyDetail: Entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is damaged, inoperable or missing.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY I: ENTRY DOOR SEAL, GASKET, OR STRIPPING IS DAMAGED, INOPERABLE, OR MISSING
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: The entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is:
- damaged (i.e. visibly defective; impacts functionality);
- inoperable (i.e. overall system or component thereof not meeting function / purpose; with or without visible damage); or
- missing (i.e. evidence of prior installation, but now not present or is incomplete).
AND ONE OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS:
Condition 1:
- General door type: Results in a gap of ¼ inch wide or greater between the door slab and the stop molding on the jamb, or the jamb itself, or between the bottom of the door and the threshold or floor AND permits light around the closed door.
- Special door type: Results in a gap of ¼ inch wide or greater around or under the door or where the doors meet AND permits light around the closed door or where the doors meet.
Condition 2:
- General door type: There is evidence of water penetrating (e.g. water damage or dry rot) around or under the door.
- Special door type: There is evidence of water penetrating (e.g. water damage or dry rot) around or under the door or where the doors meet.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol Common Area Drainage Inspection
Multi Unit Residential Property
1. Scope & Applicability (IPC §701–§706 / IPMC §305)
Inspection applies to interior common area drainage components:
•	Floor drains
•	Drain lines (PVC, ABS, cast iron)
•	Drain cleanouts
•	Laundry drains
•	Mechanical room drains
•	Condensate drains
•	Mop sink drains
•	Drain traps (P traps, floor drain traps)
If no interior drainage components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Drain Presence & Accessibility (IPC §708)
Inspect:
•	Drain present where required (laundry, mechanical rooms, basements)
•	Drain accessible (not blocked by storage or equipment)
•	Cleanout visible and reachable
•	No obstructions preventing inspection
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing required drain → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked drain access → Severe
3. Drain Flow Performance (IPC §704)
Inspect:
•	Water drains freely without backing up
•	No standing water around drain
•	No slow drainage
•	No gurgling, bubbling, or backflow
•	No sewer gas odor during flow test
Hazard Severity:
•	Backflow or sewage → Immediate Hazard
•	Sewer gas odor → Immediate Hazard
•	Slow drainage → Moderate/Severe
4. Trap & Seal Integrity (IPC §1002)
Inspect:
•	Trap present (P trap or floor drain trap)
•	Trap seal depth between 2–4 inches
•	No dry traps (indicates lack of use or leak)
•	No cracks, corrosion, or improper materials
•	No flexible accordion traps
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing trap → Immediate Hazard
•	Dry trap with sewer odor → Immediate Hazard
5. Floor Drains (IPC §1002 / §1003)
Inspect:
•	Drain body intact
•	No debris blocking drain
•	Trap seal maintained (add water if dry)
•	No sewer gas odor
•	No backflow evidence
•	No rusted or missing drain covers
Hazard Severity:
•	Backflow → Immediate Hazard
•	Dry floor drain → Moderate/Severe
6. Laundry & Mechanical Room Drains
Inspect:
•	Laundry standpipe secure and properly trapped
•	No leaks at standpipe or trap
•	Mechanical room drains clear and unobstructed
•	Condensate drains properly routed
•	No water pooling near equipment
Hazard Severity:
•	Water pooling near mechanical equipment → Immediate Hazard
•	Improper condensate drain → Severe

inside.deficiencyDetail: Fire escape & Ladders, access to exteriors - doors and windows. (Double-key cylinder deadbolts and any locks or security features requiring a key, tool, or special effort from the street side are prohibited on exit doors, exit access doors, and egress windows.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: The exit access or exit is obstructed. 1. Exit access - path from any interior location to an exit. 2. Exit doors to the outside and enclosed exit stairways. Double-key cylinder deadbolts, or security features that require a key, a tool, or special effort from the inside to the exterior (street side), are not allowed
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol –  Common Area Egress Inspection
Multi Unit Residential Property
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1001–1003 / IPMC §702)
Inspection applies to:
•	Hallways & corridors
•	Exit access doors
•	Exit passageways
•	Stairways & stair towers
•	Ramps
•	Egress lighting
•	Exit signs
•	Common area pathways leading to exits
If no interior egress components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Egress Pathway Condition (IBC §1003.6)
Inspect:
•	Pathway clear and unobstructed
•	No storage, furniture, trash, or equipment blocking egress
•	No trip hazards (loose flooring, cords, uneven surfaces)
•	No narrowing of required width
•	No protruding objects reducing headroom
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked egress → Immediate Hazard
•	Trip hazards → Immediate Hazard
3. Corridor & Hallway Requirements (IBC §1020)
Inspect:
•	Corridor width maintained (minimum 44 inches typical)
•	No combustible storage in corridors
•	No penetrations in fire rated corridor walls or ceilings
•	No damaged corridor surfaces affecting safety
Hazard Severity:
•	Combustibles in corridor → Immediate Hazard
•	Fire rated breach → Immediate Hazard
4. Egress Doors (IBC §1010)
Inspect:
•	Doors open easily without special knowledge
•	No binding, sticking, or obstruction
•	Panic hardware (if required) functional
•	No locks or devices preventing egress
•	Door swings in direction of travel (where required)
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable egress door → Immediate Hazard
•	Illegal locking device → Immediate Hazard
5. Stairways & Stair Towers (IBC §1011)
Inspect:
•	Handrails secure and continuous
•	Guardrails present and intact
•	No loose treads or risers
•	No damaged nosings
•	No obstructions on stairs
•	Adequate lighting
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose handrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Damaged stair tread → Immediate Hazard
6. Ramps (IBC §1012)
Inspect:
•	Slope compliant (max 1:12)
•	Handrails present where required
•	No surface damage causing slip hazards
•	No obstructions
Hazard Severity:
•	Ramp obstruction → Immediate Hazard
•	Slip hazard → Immediate Hazard
7. Exit Signs (IBC §1013)
Inspect:
•	Exit signs present at required locations
•	Signs illuminated (internally or externally)
•	No missing or damaged signs
•	Directional indicators correct
•	Battery backup functional
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing exit sign → Immediate Hazard
•	Non illuminated exit sign → Severe
8. Emergency Lighting (IBC §1008 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Emergency lights present where required
•	Lights functional during test
•	Battery backup operational
•	No damaged fixtures
•	No obstructions blocking light coverage
Hazard Severity:
•	Non functional emergency lighting → Immediate Hazard
9. Fire Rated Egress Components (IBC §716 / IFC §703)
Inspect:
•	Fire rated doors close and latch
•	No wedges or hold opens (unless automatic release)
•	No penetrations in rated walls or ceilings
•	No missing fire blocking or fire stopping
•	No damaged fire rated glazing
Hazard Severity:
•	Fire rated door not closing/latching → Immediate Hazard
•	Open penetration in rated assembly → Immediate Hazard
10. Egress Discharge (IBC §1028)
(Interior areas leading to exterior exits)
Inspect:
•	Pathway to exterior clear
•	No obstructions at discharge point
•	No water pooling or slip hazards
•	No damaged flooring
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstructed discharge → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Common Area Electrical Inspection
Conductors • Outlets & Switches • GFCI • AFCI • Service Panel
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §604 / NEC)
DO NOT RESET TRIPPED BREAKERS. Notify management to contact a licensed electrician.
Inspection applies to electrical components in:
•	Hallways & corridors
•	Stair towers
•	Laundry rooms
•	Mechanical rooms
•	Community rooms
•	Storage rooms
•	Lobbies
•	Any interior common area with electrical equipment
If no electrical components exist → Not Applicable.
2. Conductors & Wiring (NEC Article 300)
Inspect:
•	No exposed live conductors
•	No damaged insulation (cracks, melting, abrasion)
•	No open junction boxes
•	No loose or hanging wiring
•	No improper splices or tape wrapped connections
•	No wiring contacting water or moisture
•	Conduit intact (no breaks, rust, or missing sections)
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed live wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
•	Damaged insulation → Severe
3. Outlets (Receptacles) (NEC 406)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, breaks, or missing covers
•	No burn marks or discoloration
•	Outlet firmly mounted (not loose)
•	No exposed wiring behind outlet
•	Polarity correct (if tested)
•	No open ground (if tested)
•	No backstabbed wiring if visible
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose outlet with exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Burn marks indicating overheating → Immediate Hazard
4. GFCI Protection (NEC 210.8)
Required in:
•	Laundry rooms
•	Janitorial closets
•	Mechanical rooms with sinks
•	Any common area with water source
Inspect:
•	GFCI present where required
•	TEST button trips power
•	RESET restores power
•	No downstream outlets without protection
•	No damaged or missing GFCI buttons
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing required GFCI → Immediate Hazard
•	Failed GFCI test → Immediate Hazard
5. Switches (NEC 404)
Inspect:
•	Switch operates smoothly
•	No cracking or missing cover plate
•	No buzzing, arcing, or delay
•	No heat damage or discoloration
•	No exposed wiring
•	Switch controls correct fixture
Hazard Severity:
•	Switch arcing or buzzing → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable switch controlling required lighting → Severe
6. AFCI Protection (NEC 210.12)
Required in:
•	Corridors serving dwelling units
•	Common rooms adjacent to residential areas
•	Areas with habitable space wiring
Inspect:
•	AFCI breaker labeled correctly
•	TEST button trips breaker
•	Reset restores circuit
•	No mixed circuits defeating AFCI protection
•	No buzzing or overheating at panel
Hazard Severity:
•	Failed AF+D41:D51CI test → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing required AFCI → Immediate Hazard
7. Service Panel / Breaker Panel (NEC 110 / 408)
Inspect:
•	Panel cover present and secure
•	No open knockouts
•	Breakers labeled
•	No double tapped breakers (unless rated)
•	No scorch marks or overheating
•	No water intrusion
•	No missing AFCI/GFCI breakers where required
•	Working clearance maintained (30" wide, 36" deep)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing panel cover → Immediate Hazard
•	Open energized components → Immediate Hazard
•	Water intrusion → Immediate Hazard
9. Mechanical & Laundry Room Electrical
Inspect:
•	No wiring contacting appliances
•	No damaged dryer or washer outlets
•	No extension cords used as permanent wiring
•	No electrical components within splash zones without GFCI
Hazard Severity:
•	Extension cords used as wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Damaged appliance outlet → Severe

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Elevator Safety Inspection
1. Elevator Car & Interior Condition (ASME A17.1 §2.14)
Inspect:
•	Car walls, ceiling, and floor intact
•	No loose panels or fixtures
•	No exposed wiring
•	Lighting functional
•	Emergency lighting functional
•	No water intrusion or moisture damage
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose interior panels → Immediate Hazard
2. Elevator Doors (Hoistway & Car Doors) (ASME A17.1 §2.12)
Inspect:
•	Doors open/close smoothly
•	No binding, slamming, or hesitation
•	No gaps exposing hoistway
•	Sensors (reopening devices) functional
•	No damaged or missing door panels
•	No obstructions in door tracks
Hazard Severity:
•	Door failing to reopen on obstruction → Immediate Hazard
•	Gap exposing hoistway → Immediate Hazard
3. Elevator Controls & Operating Panels (ASME A17.1 §2.26)
Inspect:
•	Call buttons functional
•	Car operating panel functional
•	Emergency stop functional
•	Alarm button functional
•	No missing or damaged buttons
•	No exposed wiring behind panel
Hazard Severity:
•	Emergency stop or alarm inoperable → Immediate Hazard
4. Emergency Communication (ASME A17.1 §2.27)
Inspect:
•	Two way communication system functional
•	Phone or intercom operable
•	No static, failure, or delay
•	Instructions posted and legible
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable emergency communication → Immediate Hazard
5. Elevator Safety Devices (ASME A17.1 §2.25)
Inspect:
•	Door sensors functional
•	Car leveling accurate (within ½ inch)
•	No sudden stops or jerks
•	No unusual noises or vibrations
•	No overspeed or uncontrolled movement
Hazard Severity:
•	Leveling failure → Immediate Hazard
•	Uncontrolled movement → Immediate Hazard
6. Elevator Machine Room 
Do not enter if not escorted by the servicing company.
7. Elevator Lobbies & Egress (IBC §3006 / IFC Chapter 10)
Inspect:
•	Egress path clear
•	No storage blocking elevator lobby
•	Fire rated lobby doors intact
•	Smoke detectors functional (if required)
•	No penetrations in rated walls or ceilings
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked egress → Immediate Hazard
•	Fire rated breach → Immediate Hazard

inside.deficiencySelected: Exit Sign
inside.deficiencyDetail: An exit sign is deficient if it’s damaged, missing, obstructed so “EXIT” isn’t clearly visible, or not adequately illuminated.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Exit sign is damaged (i.e., visibly defective; impacts functionality).
 OR
Exit sign is missing (i.e. evidence of prior installation, but now not present or is incomplete).
OR
Exit sign is obstructed such that the word “EXIT” is not clearly visible.
OR
Exit sign is not adequately illuminated.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Fire Safety Inspection
1. Fire Extinguishers (NFPA 10 / IPMC §704)
Presence & Accessibility
•	Extinguisher present where required (hallways, laundry rooms, mechanical rooms).
•	Mounted, visible, and unobstructed.
•	Correct type (ABC for general areas).
Condition
•	Gauge in green.
•	Pin and tamper seal intact.
•	No rust, dents, or damage.
•	Label legible.
Hazard Severity

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Fire Safety Inspection
1. Fire Extinguishers (NFPA 10 / IPMC §704)
Presence & Accessibility
•	Extinguisher present where required (hallways, laundry rooms, mechanical rooms).
•	Mounted, visible, and unobstructed.
•	Correct type (ABC for general areas).
Condition
•	Gauge in green.
•	Pin and tamper seal intact.
•	No rust, dents, or damage.
•	Label legible.
Hazard Severity
•	Missing extinguisher → Immediate Hazard
•	Inaccessible or discharged → Immediate Hazard
2. Flammable & Combustible Materials (IFC §605 / IPMC §302)
Storage & Placement
•	No flammables near ignition sources (heaters, dryers, electrical panels).
•	No gasoline, propane, kerosene stored indoors.
•	No excessive combustible clutter (paper, cardboard, clothing).
•	Aerosols stored away from heat.
Hazard Severity
•	Fuel stored indoors → Immediate Hazard
•	Combustibles near ignition sources → Severe
3. Smoke Alarms (NFPA 72 / IPMC §704
 Ask for the report and certificate; check if it is not connected with other smoke detectors.
Required Locations
•	In hallways serving dwelling units.
•	In common rooms where required by local code.
•	On every level of the building.
Condition & Testing
•	Alarm present and mounted correctly.
•	Battery installed or hardwired.
•	Alarm less than 10 years old.
•	TEST button activates audible alarm.
Hazard Severity
•	Missing alarm → Immediate Hazard
•	Alarm fails test → Immediate Hazard
4. Sprinkler Assemblies (NFPA 13 / IFC §903)
Head Condition
•	Sprinkler head present and unobstructed.
•	Minimum 18-inch clearance below head.
•	No paint, corrosion, dust, or foreign material.
•	Escutcheon plate present and flush.
System Indicators
•	No leaks or moisture staining.
•	No items hung from sprinkler head.
•	No missing or damaged piping.
Hazard Severity
•	Painted or obstructed head → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing escutcheon → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Floor & Flooring Component Inspection
1. Floor Surface Condition (IPMC §305.3)
Inspect:
•	No holes, missing sections, or broken flooring
•	No cracks, splits, or delamination
•	No loose tiles, planks, or boards
•	No buckling, warping, or uneven surfaces
•	No torn or frayed carpet
•	No loose carpet edges or transitions
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose flooring creating trip hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing flooring sections → Immediate Hazard
•	Buckling/warping causing fall risk → Severe
2. Moisture, Water Intrusion & Staining (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect:
•	Water stains or discoloration
•	Active leaks or dampness
•	Soft or swollen flooring materials
•	Mold like substance
•	Musty odors indicating hidden moisture
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Moisture damaged flooring at risk of collapse → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance → Severe
3. Transitions & Thresholds (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	Transition strips secure and flush
•	No raised edges
•	No gaps between flooring types
•	Thresholds intact and properly seated
•	No tripping hazards at doorways
Hazard Severity:
•	Raised transition → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose threshold → Severe
4. Floor Penetrations & Components
Inspect:
•	Floor registers secure and undamaged
•	No missing or broken covers
•	No gaps around penetrations (pipes, ducts)
•	No exposed sharp edges
•	No breached fire rated penetrations (mechanical rooms)
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing register cover → Immediate Hazard
•	Unsealed penetrations → Severe
5. Structural Integrity Indicators (IPMC §305.2)
Inspect:
•	No sagging or deflection
•	No soft spots indicating subfloor failure
•	No separation between flooring and subfloor
•	No structural rot or deterioration
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural failure risk → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Foundation (Accessible Area) Visual Inspection
1. Foundation Wall Condition (Concrete / Masonry)
Inspect:
•	No horizontal, stair step, or shear cracks
•	No bulging, bowing, or leaning walls
•	No spalling, delamination, or exposed aggregate
•	No loose or deteriorated mortar joints
•	No structural separation from framing
•	No efflorescence indicating moisture intrusion
Hazard Severity:
•	Bulging/bowing wall → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural cracks with displacement → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose masonry → Immediate Hazard
2. Slab on Grade Interior Surfaces
Inspect:
•	No major cracks with vertical displacement
•	No heaving or settlement
•	No moisture intrusion through slab
•	No soft spots indicating sub slab failure
•	No exposed rebar
Hazard Severity:
•	Heaving/settlement causing trip hazard → Immediate Hazard
3. Piers, Columns & Supports (IBC §1807)
Inspect:
•	No leaning or misalignment
•	No rot, rust, or corrosion
•	No deteriorated concrete piers
•	No damaged or missing steel posts
•	No loose or missing anchor bolts
•	No termite damage on wood supports
Hazard Severity:
•	Failed or leaning support → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing anchor bolts → Immediate Hazard
4. Moisture, Water Intrusion & Drainage (IPMC §305.4)
Inspect:
•	No active leaks
•	No standing water in accessible areas
•	No moisture staining on foundation walls
•	No mold like substance
•	No musty odors indicating chronic moisture
•	No damaged vapor barriers
Hazard Severity:
•	Standing water → Immediate Hazard
•	Active leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance → Severe
5. Foundation Penetrations & Openings
Inspect:
•	No unsealed penetrations (pipes, conduits)
•	No gaps allowing pest entry
•	No damaged sleeves or collars
•	No fire rated breaches in mechanical rooms
Hazard Severity:
•	Unsealed penetration in rated assembly → Immediate Hazard
•	Pest entry → Severe
6. Crawlspace Conditions (IRC §408)
(If accessible from common areas)
Inspect:
•	Adequate ventilation
•	No debris blocking access
•	No damaged or missing vapor barrier
•	No sagging insulation
•	No structural deterioration of beams or joists
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural deterioration → Immediate Hazard
•	Standing water → Immediate Hazard
7. Basement Foundation Conditions
Inspect:
•	No wall displacement
•	No cracks indicating settlement
•	No moisture seepage
•	No damaged sump pump (if present)
•	No rust on steel beams or columns
Hazard Severity:
•	Wall displacement → Immediate Hazard
•	Failed sump pump with water intrusion → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Grab Bar Inspection
1. Presence & Required Locations (ICC A117.1 §604 / §608)
Inspect:
•	Grab bar present where required (toilet side, rear wall, shower/tub).
•	No missing grab bars.
•	No removed or substituted bars.
•	Bars installed at correct height (typically 33–36 inches above floor for toilets).
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing required grab bar → Immediate Hazard.
2. Structural Stability & Mounting (IPMC §305.2)
Inspect:
•	Bar firmly anchored to wall.
•	No movement, rotation, or shifting when pulled.
•	No loose mounting hardware.
•	No separation between bar and wall surface.
•	No wall damage compromising support (soft wall, cracked tile, loose anchors).
Hazard Severity:
•	Grab bar moves or rotates → Immediate Hazard.
•	Wall damage affecting support → Immediate Hazard.
3. Accessibility Compliance (ICC A117.1)
Inspect:
•	Grab bar length meets standard (typically 36" rear, 42" side for toilets).
•	Bar clearance from wall is 1½ inches.
•	No obstructions (toilet paper dispensers, shelves, pipes).
•	Bar surface is graspable (not too thick, slippery, or obstructed).
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstruction preventing grasp → Severe.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Hazard Inspection (Infestation + Sharp Edges + Trip Hazards)
1. Infestation (IPMC §309 – Pest Management)
Inspect for:
•	Insects: roaches, ants, bedbugs, fleas, termites
•	Rodents: droppings, gnaw marks, nests, odors
•	Entry points: gaps at baseboards, holes in walls, pipe penetrations
•	Food sources: trash accumulation, food debris, dirty appliances
•	Moisture sources: leaks, damp areas, mold like substance
Severity Guidance:
•	Active infestation = Severe
•	Termite structural damage = Severe
•	Pest entry due to structural gaps = Moderate
2. Sharp Edges (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect for:
•	Broken fixtures or appliances
•	Exposed nails, screws, metal edges
•	Damaged window or door frames
•	Broken furniture creating injury risk
•	Sharp edges on flooring transitions or thresholds
Severity Guidance:
•	Sharp edge capable of causing immediate injury = Immediate Hazard
•	Minor sharp edges (non injury) = Moderate
3. Trip Hazards (IPMC §305 / IBC §1003 – Means of Egress)
Inspect for:
•	Loose flooring, tiles, or planks
•	Raised transitions or thresholds
•	Torn or bunched carpet
•	Electrical cords across pathways
•	Clutter blocking walking paths
•	Uneven surfaces or floor settlement
•	Poor lighting contributing to trip risk
Severity Guidance:
•	Major trip hazard in egress path = Severe
•	Minor unevenness = Moderate

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Hazard Inspection (Infestation + Sharp Edges + Trip Hazards)
1. Infestation (IPMC §309 – Pest Management)
Inspect for:
•	Insects: roaches, ants, bedbugs, fleas, termites
•	Rodents: droppings, gnaw marks, nests, odors
•	Entry points: gaps at baseboards, holes in walls, pipe penetrations
•	Food sources: trash accumulation, food debris, dirty appliances
•	Moisture sources: leaks, damp areas, mold like substance
Severity Guidance:
•	Active infestation = Severe
•	Termite structural damage = Severe
•	Pest entry due to structural gaps = Moderate
2. Sharp Edges (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect for:
•	Broken fixtures or appliances
•	Exposed nails, screws, metal edges
•	Damaged window or door frames
•	Broken furniture creating injury risk
•	Sharp edges on flooring transitions or thresholds
Severity Guidance:
•	Sharp edge capable of causing immediate injury = Immediate Hazard
•	Minor sharp edges (non injury) = Moderate
3. Trip Hazards (IPMC §305 / IBC §1003 – Means of Egress)
Inspect for:
•	Loose flooring, tiles, or planks
•	Raised transitions or thresholds
•	Torn or bunched carpet
•	Electrical cords across pathways
•	Clutter blocking walking paths
•	Uneven surfaces or floor settlement
•	Poor lighting contributing to trip risk
Severity Guidance:
•	Major trip hazard in egress path = Severe
•	Minor unevenness = Moderate

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area HVAC Inspection
1. Equipment Condition & Mounting (IPMC §603.1)
Inspect:
•	Equipment securely mounted
•	No loose, unstable, or vibrating units
•	No damaged housings or panels
•	No missing access covers
•	No sharp edges or exposed metal
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose or unstable HVAC unit → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing access panel → Immediate Hazard
2. Gas Fired Equipment (IFGC / IFC §603)
(If applicable)
Inspect:
•	No gas odor
•	Gas shutoff valve present and accessible
•	No damaged or corroded gas piping
•	No gaps at gas connection
•	No soot staining (indicates combustion failure)
•	Proper venting and draft
Hazard Severity:
•	Gas odor → Immediate Hazard
•	Damaged gas piping → Immediate Hazard
3. Ventilation & Exhaust (IMC §501–504)
Inspect:
•	Exhaust fans operable
•	No blocked or obstructed exhaust outlets
•	No damaged or missing fan covers
•	No excessive noise indicating failure
•	No backdrafting
•	No lint accumulation (laundry areas)
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked exhaust → Immediate Hazard
•	Backdrafting → Immediate Hazard
4. Air Distribution (IMC §603–607)
Inspect:
•	Ducts intact (no holes, gaps, disconnected sections)
•	No damaged or missing insulation
•	No crushed or kinked ducts
•	Registers and diffusers secure
•	No debris blocking airflow
•	No mold like substance at registers
Hazard Severity:
•	Disconnected duct → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance → Severe
5. Condensate Management (IMC §307)
(For AC, PTAC, mini split, air handlers)
Inspect:
•	Condensate drain line clear
•	No leaks or water pooling
•	Drain pan intact and not overflowing
•	No rust or corrosion on drain components
•	No mold like substance near drain
Hazard Severity:
•	Active condensate leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Overflowing drain pan → Immediate Hazard
6. Filters & Air Quality (IMC §602 / IBC §1203)
Inspect:
•	Filters present and properly seated
•	No excessively dirty or clogged filters
•	No bypass gaps around filter frame
•	No odors indicating mold or contamination
•	No debris inside return air plenum
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing filter → Severe
•	Clogged filter restricting airflow → Severe
7. Mechanical Room Requirements (IBC §3005 / IMC)
(If HVAC equipment is located in a mechanical room)
Inspect:
•	Room accessible only to authorized personnel
•	No storage or combustibles
•	Adequate ventilation
•	No water intrusion
•	No blocked access to equipment
•	Proper clearance around units
Hazard Severity:
•	Storage in mechanical room → Immediate Hazard
•	Water intrusion → Immediate Hazard
8. Thermostats & Controls
Inspect:
•	Thermostat operable
•	No exposed wiring
•	No damaged covers
•	Temperature control functional
•	No erratic cycling or failure to respond
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable thermostat affecting safety → Severe

Inspect:

•	Gas odor → Immediate Hazard

Inspect:
•	Exhaust fans operable
•	No blocked or obstructed exhaust outlets
•	No damaged or missing fan covers
•	No excessive noise indicating failure
•	No backdrafting
•	No lint accumulation (laundry areas)
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked exhaust → Immediate Hazard
•	Backdrafting → Immediate Hazard

Inspect:
•	Ducts intact (no holes, gaps, disconnected sections)
•	No damaged or missing insulation
•	No crushed or kinked ducts
•	Registers and diffusers secure
•	No debris blocking airflow
•	No mold like substance at registers

inside.deficiencyDetail: Storage component is damaged, inoperable, or missing.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Common arearea AFull Kitchen Inspection (All Items)
1. Cabinets & Storage (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect:
•	Doors open/close properly
•	No broken hinges, missing doors, or loose hardware
•	No sharp edges, splintered wood, or protruding fasteners
•	No water damage, swelling, delamination, or mold like substance
•	Shelves secure and not collapsing
•	No pest droppings or nesting inside cabinets
Hazards:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
•	Water damage/mold → Severe
•	Pest activity → Severe
2. Countertops & Food Prep Surfaces (IPMC §305.1 – Sanitation)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, missing sections, or exposed particleboard
•	No mold like substance or moisture damage
•	No loose laminate or sharp edges
•	No pest activity
•	Surface cleanable and intact
Hazards:
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
3. Cooking Appliances (Range, Oven, Cooktop) – IFC §603 / IMC §304
Inspect:
•	Burners ignite; oven heats
•	No gas odor (gas appliances)
•	No exposed wiring or damaged cords
•	No scorch marks, soot, or overheating
•	Anti tip bracket installed (required for ranges)
•	Controls functional and not broken
•	No combustibles stored near heat source
Hazards:
•	Gas leak → Immediate
•	Exposed electrical → Immediate
•	Missing anti tip bracket → Severe
•	Inoperable cooking appliance → Severe
4. Refrigerator (IPMC §605 – Electrical Safety)
Inspect:
•	Operates and cools properly
•	Door seals intact
•	No exposed wiring
•	No water leaks or condensation pooling
•	No mold like substance inside or around unit
•	No sharp edges on handles or frame
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Water + electrical → Immediate
•	Inoperable refrigerator → Severe
5. Sink, Faucet & Plumbing (IPC §701–§706 / IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Hot/cold water available
•	Drain flows freely
•	No leaks at P trap, supply lines, or drain
•	No mold like substance under sink
•	No corrosion or damaged piping
•	Garbage disposal (if present) operates safely
Hazards:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sewer odor/backflow → Immediate
6. Ventilation (Range Hood or Exhaust) – IMC §501 / IPMC §602
Inspect:
•	Hood/exhaust fan operable
•	No grease buildup creating fire hazard
•	Filter present and not clogged
•	No exposed wiring
•	No sharp edges on hood housing
•	Adequate airflow
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Heavy grease buildup → Severe
•	Inoperable vent → Moderate/Severe
7. Flooring & Trip Hazards (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	No loose tiles, planks, or peeling flooring
•	No torn or bunched carpet
•	No raised transitions or thresholds
•	No clutter blocking movement
•	No cords across walking paths
Hazards:
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
•	Minor unevenness → Moderate
8. Fire Safety (IFC §603 / IPMC §704)
Inspect:
•	No combustibles near stove or oven
•	No damaged electrical cords
•	No signs of overheating
•	Smoke alarm present outside kitchen (per code location)
•	No blocked egress routes
Hazards:
•	Combustibles near heat source → Severe
•	Electrical fire hazard → Immediate

inside.deficiencyDetail: There is evidence of a gas, propane, or oil leak, or there is an uncapped gas or fuel supply line. strong odor.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: There is evidence of a gas, propane, or oil leak. OR There is an uncapped gas or fuel supply line.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Inspection for Gas or Oil Leak in common area
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IMC §102 / IFC §604)
Before entering or inspecting:
•	Identify odor of gas (sulfur/rotten egg smell).
•	Listen for hissing near appliances or piping.
•	Look for visible oil residue, staining, or pooling.
•	Check for burning smell, overheating, or smoke.
•	Ensure no open flames, smoking, or ignition sources.
Immediate Hazard: Any suspected gas leak → evacuate, notify management, and stop inspection.
2. Gas Appliances (Wall Heater, Range, Water Heater) – IMC §304 / IFC §603
Inspect:
•	No gas odor around appliance.
•	No hissing at valves, flex lines, or connections.
•	Flex line intact, not kinked, crushed, or corroded.
•	Shutoff valve present and operable.
•	Burner flames steady (blue, not yellow/orange).
•	No soot, scorch marks, or overheating.
•	No combustible materials stored near appliance.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Gas odor
•	Damaged flex line
•	Leaking shutoff valve
•	Soot indicating incomplete combustion
3. Oil Fueled Appliances (If Present) – IFC §603.5
Inspect:
•	No oil drips, stains, or pooling under appliance.
•	No fuel odor.
•	No corrosion at tank or supply line.
•	No leaks at filter, pump, or burner assembly.
•	Flame burns clean and stable.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Active oil leak
•	Oil pooling
•	Fuel odor
•	Overheating or smoke
4. Piping, Valves & Connections (IMC §301 / §303)
Inspect:
•	No corrosion, rust, or deterioration.
•	No loose fittings or damaged threads.
•	No visible oil residue on piping.
•	No gaps at unions or couplings.
•	No vibration or movement at appliance connection.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Active leak
•	Damaged or loose connection
•	Corroded piping with seepage
5. Venting & Combustion Air (IMC §501 / §304.6)
Inspect:
•	Vent pipes intact, properly connected.
•	No gaps, disconnections, or backdrafting.
•	No soot at vent termination.
•	Combustion air openings unobstructed.
•	No signs of exhaust entering living space.
Severe:
•	Backdrafting
•	Blocked vent
•	Soot at vent outlet
6. HVAC Interaction (Wall Heater, Boiler/Chiller Fan Coil)
Inspect:
•	No gas odor near wall heater.
•	No oil residue near hydronic heating components.
•	No leaks at boiler/chiller fan coil piping.
•	No electrical hazard near fuel source.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Fuel leak + electrical hazard
•	Fuel leak near ignition source
7. Environmental Indicators (IPMC §305 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance near fuel lines (may indicate moisture + corrosion).
•	Moisture staining around gas/oil piping.
•	Musty or chemical odor indicating hidden leak.
•	Pest activity damaging insulation or flex lines.
Severe:
•	Mold + active leak
•	Corrosion from moisture exposure
8. Tenant Installed Appliances (IFC §603.4)
Inspect:
•	Portable heaters (prohibited if fuel burning).
•	Unauthorized gas appliances.
•	Improperly installed window A/C interfering with venting.
•	Damaged or unapproved fuel containers.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Unauthorized fuel burning appliance
•	Improper fuel storage

inside.deficiencySelected: Blocked sewage system.
inside.deficiencyDetail: Wastewater is unable to drain resulting in sewer backup.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Wastewater is unable to drain resulting in sewer backup.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Inspection of Leak: Sewage System (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability
A sewage system inspection applies when any of the following are present:
•	Wastewater leaks
•	Sewage backup
•	Missing drain/cleanout caps
•	Odors indicating sewer gas
•	Moisture or staining near sanitary drainage components
•	Clogged drains causing wastewater overflow
If none are present → mark Not Applicable.
2. Components to Inspect (IPC Chapters 7 & 8)
Inspect all sanitary drainage components inside the unit:
•	Bathroom sink, kitchen sink
•	Tub/shower drain
•	Toilet base and wax ring
•	Clothes washer standpipe
•	Dishwasher drain (visible portion)
•	Floor drains
•	P traps, tailpieces, waste arms
•	Cleanouts and drain caps
•	Branch lines visible in cabinets or closets
3. Visual Inspection (IPMC §305 – Interior Conditions)
Look for:
•	Active wastewater leaks
•	Dripping or seepage from traps or drain assemblies
•	Wet flooring, staining, or swelling
•	Sewage residue or solids
•	Missing drain caps or cleanout caps
•	Cracked or loose drain components
•	Mold like substance near plumbing
•	Sewer gas odor (sulfur/methane smell)
Immediate Hazard: Any visible sewage, active leak, or strong sewer gas odor.
4. Functional Drainage Test (IPC §707)
Perform at each fixture:
•	Run water briefly
•	Observe drainage speed
•	Stop immediately if backup occurs
•	Check for cross fixture backup (e.g., tub fills when toilet flushes)
Severe: Slow drainage, standing water, or cross fixture backup.
5. Toilet Base & Wax Ring (IPC §405.4)
Inspect:
•	No seepage at base
•	No rocking or instability
•	No wastewater staining around toilet
•	No sewer odor from base
Immediate Hazard: Active leak at toilet base.
6. Cleanouts & Drain Caps (IPC §708)
Inspect:
•	Cleanout caps present and tight
•	No open sanitary lines
•	No odor or moisture at cleanout location
•	No missing or damaged caps
Severe: Missing cap with odor or moisture. Immediate Hazard: Missing cap with sewage exposure.
7. Sewer Gas Odor (IFC §605 / IPMC §305.1)
Check:
•	Persistent sewer smell
•	Odor from open drains or missing caps
•	Odor near floor drains or washer standpipe
Immediate Hazard: Strong or continuous sewer gas odor.
8. Moisture & Mold Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance near drains or traps
•	Moisture staining under sinks
•	Swelling of cabinets or flooring
•	Active leaks contributing to mold
Severe: Mold + active leak. Immediate Hazard: Mold + electrical hazard.
9. Safety Hazards (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Water near electrical outlets or appliances
•	Slip hazards from wastewater
•	Contamination hazards from sewage exposure
•	No destructive inspection allowed (do not open cleanouts)
Immediate Hazard: Water + electrical interaction.

•	Mold like substance associated with moisture
•	Plumbing fixture or appliance leaks
•	Ceiling/wall/floor moisture indicators

•	Bathroom sink, kitchen sink

•	Clothes washer supply lines
•	Dishwasher supply/drain (visible portion)
•	Refrigerator ice maker line
•	Water heater (if located inside unit)

inside.deficiencySelected: Lighting - Auxiliary
inside.deficiencyDetail: Auxiliary lighting is damaged, missing, or fails to illuminate when tested.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Auxiliary lighting is damaged (i.e., visibly defective).
OR
Auxiliary lighting is missing (i.e., evidence of prior installation, but now not present or is incomplete).Or fail to illuminate when tested.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Lighting & Auxiliary Lighting Inspection
1. Required Illumination Levels (IBC §1008.2)
Inspect:
•	Corridors and egress paths illuminated at minimum 1 foot candle (fc)
•	Stairways illuminated at minimum 1 fc
•	Mechanical rooms adequately lit for safe operation
•	Laundry rooms and community rooms adequately lit for safe use
•	No dark spots or insufficient lighting in required areas
Hazard Severity:
•	Insufficient lighting in egress path → Immediate Hazard
•	Dark stairway → Immediate Hazard
2. Fixture Condition (NEC 410 / IPMC §605)
Inspect:
•	Fixtures securely mounted
•	No loose, hanging, or unstable fixtures
•	No broken lenses, globes, or covers
•	No exposed wiring
•	No cracked housings
•	No missing bulbs or LED modules
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose fixture → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
3. Lamp/Bulb Condition & Operation
Inspect:
•	All lamps operational
•	No flickering or dimming indicating electrical failure
•	No burned out bulbs
•	No mismatched lamp types causing overheating
•	LED drivers functioning properly
Hazard Severity:
•	Flickering indicating electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Burned out bulb in required egress area → Severe
4. Emergency Lighting (IBC §1008 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Emergency lights present where required
•	Battery backup functional (test button)
•	No damaged or missing emergency fixtures
•	No obstructions blocking emergency light coverage
•	Exit signs illuminated and functional
Hazard Severity:
•	Non functional emergency lighting → Immediate Hazard
•	Non illuminated exit sign → Immediate Hazard
5. Other Lighting (Closets, Alcoves, Small Rooms)
Inspect:
•	Fixtures present and operable
•	No bare bulbs in hazardous locations
•	No fixtures too close to combustibles
•	No damaged pull chains or switches
Hazard Severity:
•	Bare bulb near combustibles → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable auxiliary lighting → Severe
6. Electrical Safety Interaction (IPMC §604 / NEC)
Inspect:
•	No exposed wiring at fixtures or switches
•	No damaged conduit
•	No missing junction box covers
•	No overheating or burn marks
•	No water intrusion near lighting components
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
7. Mechanical & Utility Room Lighting (IMC / IPMC)
Inspect:
•	Adequate lighting for safe equipment operation
•	No flickering or dimming
•	No damaged fixtures
•	No blocked access to lighting controls
Hazard Severity:
•	Inadequate lighting affecting safe operation → Immediate Hazard

inside.deficiencySelected: Mold - Like Substance
inside.deficiencyDetail:
Elevated moisture level. (e.g., peeling paint or wallpaper, a wall that is warped or
stained, or a buckled, cracked, or water-stained ceiling, carpet, or wooden floor).
inside.standard:
Poor ventilation, (e.g., peeling paint or wallpaper, a wall that is warped or

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Mold Inspection - Common Area
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
A mold inspection applies when any of the following are present:
•	Mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, or fixtures
•	Moisture staining or water damage
•	Musty odor
•	Active leaks or condensation
•	Visible biological growth on building materials
If none are present → Not Applicable.
2. Visual Assessment (IPMC §305 – Interior Conditions)
Inspect:
•	Walls, ceilings, floors
•	Behind/under sinks, cabinets, appliances
•	Bathroom surfaces (tub, shower, tile, grout)
•	HVAC registers, window A/C, wall heaters
•	Windowsills and frames
•	Closets and low ventilation areas
Look for:
•	Dark, green, black, or white growth
•	Moisture staining or bubbling paint
•	Swollen drywall or flooring
•	Peeling or delaminated surfaces
•	Condensation on windows or walls
Immediate Hazard: Mold + electrical hazard or mold caused by sewage.
3. Moisture Source Identification (IPC §701–§706 / IMC §307)
Check for:
•	Active plumbing leaks
•	Roof or ceiling leaks from upper units
•	Window leaks or condensation
•	HVAC condensation issues
•	Water intrusion at slab or foundation edges
•	Poor ventilation in bathrooms/kitchens
Severe: Any active leak causing mold.
4. Bathroom & Kitchen Moisture Zones
Inspect:
•	Shower/tub tile, grout, caulking
•	Sink base cabinets
•	Dishwasher and refrigerator areas
•	Range hood and exhaust fan operation
•	Toilet base and wax ring area
Look for:
•	Mold like substance
•	Moisture staining
•	Musty odor
•	Soft or swollen materials
Severe: Mold + active plumbing leak.
5. HVAC & Ventilation (IMC §501 / §603)
Inspect:
•	Window A/C units (filters, frames, drainage)
•	Wall heaters (dust buildup, moisture exposure)
•	Supply/return vents
•	Bathroom exhaust fan operation
•	Kitchen hood ventilation
Look for:
•	Mold on vents or filters
•	Condensation around HVAC components
•	Poor airflow contributing to moisture buildup
Severe: Mold caused by HVAC moisture or blocked ventilation.
6. Odor Assessment (IPMC §305.1)
Check for:
•	Musty odor indicating hidden mold
•	Odor near plumbing fixtures
•	Odor near HVAC components
•	Odor near walls or ceilings with moisture history
Severe: Strong odor with visible moisture damage.
7. Structural Indicators (IPMC §305 / IBC Structural)
Inspect:
•	Soft drywall
•	Sagging ceilings
•	Warped flooring
•	Delaminated cabinets
•	Crumbling or deteriorated materials
Immediate Hazard: Ceiling collapse risk from moisture.

DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Cumulative area of patches is more than 1 square foot and less than 9 square feet in a room. Odor is an indicator, but not a diagnostic; if a musty odor is detected, visual confirmation of “mold-like substance” is required. Odor may be indicated in a “notes” field. This deficiency is not recorded if observed on household items (e.g., clothing, upholstery, food)
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Mold Inspection - Common Area
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
A mold inspection applies when any of the following are present:
•	Mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, or fixtures
•	Moisture staining or water damage
•	Musty odor
•	Active leaks or condensation
•	Visible biological growth on building materials
If none are present → Not Applicable.
2. Visual Assessment (IPMC §305 – Interior Conditions)
Inspect:
•	Walls, ceilings, floors
•	Behind/under sinks, cabinets, appliances
•	Bathroom surfaces (tub, shower, tile, grout)
•	HVAC registers, window A/C, wall heaters
•	Windowsills and frames
•	Closets and low ventilation areas
Look for:
•	Dark, green, black, or white growth
•	Moisture staining or bubbling paint
•	Swollen drywall or flooring
•	Peeling or delaminated surfaces
•	Condensation on windows or walls
Immediate Hazard: Mold + electrical hazard or mold caused by sewage.
3. Moisture Source Identification (IPC §701–§706 / IMC §307)
Check for:
•	Active plumbing leaks
•	Roof or ceiling leaks from upper units
•	Window leaks or condensation
•	HVAC condensation issues
•	Water intrusion at slab or foundation edges
•	Poor ventilation in bathrooms/kitchens
Severe: Any active leak causing mold.
4. Bathroom & Kitchen Moisture Zones
Inspect:
•	Shower/tub tile, grout, caulking
•	Sink base cabinets
•	Dishwasher and refrigerator areas
•	Range hood and exhaust fan operation
•	Toilet base and wax ring area
Look for:
•	Mold like substance
•	Moisture staining
•	Musty odor
•	Soft or swollen materials
Severe: Mold + active plumbing leak.
5. HVAC & Ventilation (IMC §501 / §603)
Inspect:
•	Window A/C units (filters, frames, drainage)
•	Wall heaters (dust buildup, moisture exposure)
•	Supply/return vents
•	Bathroom exhaust fan operation
•	Kitchen hood ventilation
Look for:
•	Mold on vents or filters
•	Condensation around HVAC components
•	Poor airflow contributing to moisture buildup
Severe: Mold caused by HVAC moisture or blocked ventilation.
6. Odor Assessment (IPMC §305.1)
Check for:
•	Musty odor indicating hidden mold
•	Odor near plumbing fixtures
•	Odor near HVAC components
•	Odor near walls or ceilings with moisture history
Severe: Strong odor with visible moisture damage.
7. Structural Indicators (IPMC §305 / IBC Structural)
Inspect:
•	Soft drywall
•	Sagging ceilings
•	Warped flooring
•	Delaminated cabinets
•	Crumbling or deteriorated materials
Immediate Hazard: Ceiling collapse risk from moisture.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
(ICC) Protocol – Common Area-Paint, Paint Deterioration & Lead Based Paint (Pre 1978 )
1. Scope & Applicability
Inspection applies when:
•	Paint is peeling, flaking, chipping, blistering, or chalking
•	Substrate (wood, drywall, plaster, metal) is exposed
•	Moisture damage is present
•	Unit was built before 1978 (lead based paint risk)
•	Dust, debris, or deterioration is visible on floors or surfaces
If none are present → Not Applicable.
2. Visual Assessment of Painted Surfaces (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect:
•	Walls, ceilings, trim, doors, frames
•	Window sills, jambs, casings (high risk lead areas)
•	Cabinets, built ins, shelving
•	Radiators, metal surfaces, stair rails
•	Behind furniture and appliances
Look for:
•	Peeling, flaking, chipping paint
•	Blistering or bubbling
•	Cracking or alligatoring
•	Exposed substrate
•	Dust accumulation from deteriorated paint
•	Moisture staining or swelling
•	Mold like substance on painted surfaces
Severe: Large areas of deterioration or exposed substrate.
3. Lead Based Paint Risk Indicators (Pre 1978 Units)
Inspect:
•	Window troughs and sills for paint chips/dust
•	Door frames where friction occurs
•	Baseboards and trim near floors
•	Radiators and metal surfaces with peeling paint
•	Floors for paint chips or dust
•	Areas disturbed by tenant repairs
Look for:
•	Paint chips on floors
•	Dust accumulation (possible lead dust)
•	Deteriorated paint on friction surfaces
•	Evidence of untrained paint disturbance
Immediate Hazard: Deteriorated paint in a pre 1978 unit on friction/impact surfaces.
4. Moisture Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Bathroom ceilings/walls
•	Under sinks and around dishwashers
•	Window frames with condensation
•	HVAC registers and A/C units
•	Areas with past water leaks
Look for:
•	Blistering paint
•	Swollen drywall or trim
•	Mold like substance
•	Water stains
Severe: Paint deterioration caused by active leak.
5. Substrate Condition (IPMC §305 – Good Repair Requirement)
Inspect:
•	Exposed drywall, plaster, or wood
•	Crumbling or deteriorated substrate
•	Delamination of drywall paper
•	Structural cracks affecting paint adhesion
Severe: Exposed or deteriorated substrate requiring repair.
6. Dust & Debris (Lead Safe Housing Rule 24 CFR 35)
Inspect:
•	Floors, window sills, window troughs
•	Radiator tops and shelves
•	Closet floors and corners
Look for:
•	Dust accumulation
•	Paint chips
•	Debris from deteriorated paint
Immediate Hazard: Lead dust or paint chips in a pre 1978 unit.
7. Tenant Caused Damage vs. Building Deficiency
Identify:
•	Holes, gouges, scratches
•	Unauthorized repainting
•	Improper patching or sanding
•	Adhesive/tape damage
Moderate/Minor: Cosmetic damage not affecting safety.
8. Safety Hazards (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Paint deterioration near electrical outlets
•	Slip hazards from paint chips
•	Sharp edges from peeling paint on metal surfaces
•	No destructive inspection allowed (no scraping or testing)
Immediate Hazard: Paint deterioration + electrical hazard.
•

inside.deficiencySelected: Guardrail
inside.deficiencyDetail: The guardrail is missing or not installed.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: The guardrail is missing (i.e., evidence of prior installation but is now not present or is incomplete) or not installed (i.e., never installed, but should have been) along a walking surface that is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Common Area-Railing Inspection (Guardrail + Handrail) 
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1015 / IPMC §305)
Inspection applies to:
•	Interior stairs
•	Interior landings
•	Mezzanines or lofts
•	Balconies inside the unit
•	Any elevated walking surface > 30 inches above floor
If none exist → Not Applicable.
2. Guardrail Inspection (IBC §1015 – Guards)
Inspect:
•	Guardrail height ≥ 42 inches (typical ICC standard)
•	Guard firmly attached; no wobbling or movement
•	No missing sections or loose posts
•	No openings > 4 inches (child safety requirement)
•	No sharp edges, splinters, or protruding fasteners
•	No rust, rot, or deterioration
•	No gaps between guardrail and wall/floor
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose/wobbly guardrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Openings > 4 inches → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
3. Handrail Inspection (IBC §1011–1014 – Handrails)
Inspect:
•	Handrail height 34–38 inches above stair nosing
•	Continuous along full stair run
•	Ends return to wall (no snag hazards)
•	Secure mounting; no looseness
•	Graspable profile (no wide, flat boards)
•	No sharp edges or splinters
•	No rust, rot, or deterioration
•	No missing handrail on stairs with >3 risers
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing handrail → Severe
•	Loose handrail → Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
4. Structural Condition (IPMC §305 – Good Repair)
Inspect:
•	No cracks in wood or metal
•	No rot, corrosion, or termite damage
•	No unstable posts or brackets
•	No separation from wall or floor
•	No sagging or bending under pressure
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural failure risk → Immediate Hazard
5. Stair & Landing Interaction (IBC §1003 – Means of Egress)
Inspect:
•	Handrail present on required side
•	Guardrail present on open side of landing
•	No trip hazards on stairs affecting handrail use
•	Adequate lighting for safe use of railing
•	No obstructions blocking grasping of handrail
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard + missing/loose railing → Severe/Immediate
6. Child Safety Requirements (IBC §1015.4)
Inspect:
•	Guardrail openings < 4 inches
•	No climbable horizontal elements
•	No gaps at bottom of guardrail
•	No protruding fasteners that create snag hazards
Hazard Severity:
•	Climbable guardrail → Severe
•	Large openings → Severe
7. Surface Condition
Inspect:
•	No peeling paint exposing sharp edges
•	No rust flakes or splinters
•	No rough surfaces that can cause injury
•	No loose decorative elements
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Rust/rot compromising strength → Severe

inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Only 1 bathtub or shower is present within the unit, and it is inoperable (i.e., overall system is not meeting function or purpose, with or without visible damage) or standing water is present such that the inspector believes water is unable to drain.
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Bathroom Inspection Protocol – Common Area Restroom (Including Mold & Grab Bars)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / §604)
•	Assess lighting and visibility.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, active leaks, sewage, slippery floors.
•	Confirm safe entry.
2. Required Fixtures (IPMC §505 / IPC §405–409)
Verify presence, stability, and operability of:
•	Toilet — flushes fully, refills, no leaks.
•	Sink — hot/cold water, drains properly.
•	Tub/Shower — hot/cold water, diverter works, drains properly.
Fixtures must be securely mounted and free of cracks.
3. Water Supply (IPC §604–606)
•	Test hot and cold water at sink and tub/shower.
•	Verify adequate pressure and temperature.
•	Inspect supply lines for leaks, corrosion, improper materials.
4. Drainage & Waste System (IPC §701–706)
•	Drains must flow freely; no standing water.
•	P traps must be present and properly installed.
•	No sewer gas odor.
•	No leaks at traps or drain connections.
5. Ventilation (IPMC §403 / IBC §1203)
•	Mechanical exhaust fan must operate and vent to exterior.
•	If no fan, window must open fully.
•	Check for moisture buildup, condensation, mildew indicators.
6. Electrical Safety (IPMC §604 / NEC reference)
•	Light fixture operable.
•	GFCI protection required for bathroom receptacles.
•	No exposed wiring, open junction boxes, or damaged devices.
•	No electrical components subject to moisture.
7. Surfaces & Structural Integrity (IPMC §305–309)
•	Floors intact; no slip/trip hazards.
•	Walls/ceilings intact; no holes or loose materials.
•	Inspect for water damage, swelling, rot, or mold like substance.
•	Tile, grout, and finishes must be intact and cleanable.
Mold specific ICC guidance:
•	Mold like substance indicates moisture failure and must be traced to source (ventilation, plumbing, envelope).
8. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
•	Identify any mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, fixtures, or caulking.
•	Check behind/around tub, shower, and sink for moisture staining.
•	Inspect for active leaks contributing to mold.
•	Note any persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold like substance = Moderate
•	Mold caused by active leak = Severe
•	Mold with electrical involvement = Immediate Hazard
9. Grab Bars & Accessibility (ICC A117.1 / ISO 21542)
(Required only in accessible units or designated accessible bathrooms)
•	Grab bars must be present, secure, and properly anchored.
•	No looseness or movement when pulled.
•	Bars must be free of rust, cracks, or sharp edges.
•	Clear floor space must be provided at toilet and tub/shower.
•	Controls (faucets, switches) must be operable with one hand.
Grab bar failure = Severe safety deficiency.
10. Sanitation & Hygiene (IPMC §502–503)
•	No human waste, sewage, or heavy filth.
•	No persistent sewage or mold odors.
•	Bathroom must be hygienic and free of infestation.
11. Privacy & Security (IPMC §702)
•	Bathroom door must close and latch.
•	Window must have privacy covering if visibility to exterior/common areas exists.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Inspection of Non Kitchen / Non Bathroom Sink (common area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305 / IPC Chapter 7)
Inspection applies to:
•	Laundry/utility sinks
•	Bar/wet bar sinks
•	Service sinks
•	Craft-room or workshop sinks
•	Any sink not located in a kitchen or bathroom
If no such sink exists → Not Applicable.
2. Fixture Condition (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect:
•	Basin intact (no cracks, chips, holes)
•	No sharp edges or broken porcelain/metal
•	No rust or corrosion compromising structure
•	Sink securely mounted (no wobbling or separation)
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural failure risk → Immediate Hazard
3. Faucet & Supply Lines (IPC §604–§605)
Inspect:
•	Hot and cold water operable
•	No leaks at faucet, handles, or supply lines
•	No corrosion on shutoff valves
•	No loose or damaged connections
•	No water hammer or vibration indicating loose piping
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Water + electrical interaction → Immediate Hazard
4. Drainage & P Trap (IPC §701–§706)
Inspect:
•	Drain flows freely (no standing water)
•	P trap intact, not leaking
•	No corrosion, cracks, or loose fittings
•	No sewer odor from drain
•	No missing or damaged drain components
Hazard Severity:
•	Sewer odor → Immediate Hazard
•	Active drain leak → Severe
5. Surrounding Surfaces (IPMC §305.1 – Moisture & Cleanliness)
Inspect:
•	Cabinet or support structure under sink
•	Wall surfaces behind/around sink
•	Flooring near sink
•	Look for moisture staining, swelling, delamination, mold like substance
Hazard Severity:
•	Mold + active leak → Severe
•	Moisture damage compromising structure → Severe
6. Ventilation & Odor Control (IMC §501)
Inspect:
•	Adequate ventilation in laundry/utility areas
•	No persistent musty or sewer odors
•	No condensation buildup around sink
Hazard Severity:
•	Persistent sewer odor → Immediate Hazard
7. Electrical Interaction (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	No electrical outlets or appliances exposed to water splash
•	GFCI protection present if sink is in laundry/wet area
•	No damaged cords near sink
•	No water pooling near electrical components
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
8. Access & Use Safety (IBC §1003 – Means of Egress)
Inspect:
•	No clutter blocking access to sink
•	No trip hazards around sink area
•	Adequate lighting for safe use
•	Sink height and stability appropriate for intended use
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard + poor lighting → Severe

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Steps & Stairs Inspection (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IBC §1003 / §1011)
Inspection applies to:
•	Interior stairways
•	Interior steps (single or multiple)
•	Loft/attic access stairs
•	Sunken living room steps
•	Basement steps inside the unit
If none exist → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Condition (IPMC §305 – Good Repair)
Inspect:
•	Treads and risers intact
•	No cracks, breaks, or missing sections
•	No loose or unstable steps
•	No sagging or deflection under load
•	No rot, corrosion, or termite damage (wood/metal stairs)
Immediate Hazard: Structural failure risk or unstable steps.
3. Tread & Riser Requirements (IBC §1011.5)
Inspect:
•	Treads uniform in depth
•	Risers uniform in height
•	No excessive variation (trip hazard)
•	No open risers that violate safety requirements
•	No slippery surfaces
Severe: Non uniform risers/treads causing trip hazards.
4. Surface Condition (IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	No loose carpet, tiles, or coverings
•	No peeling laminate
•	No protruding nails, screws, or fasteners
•	No sharp edges
•	No worn surfaces reducing traction
Immediate Hazard: Sharp edges or protruding fasteners.
5. Handrail Requirements (IBC §1011.11 / §1014)
Inspect:
•	Handrail present on stairs with more than 3 risers
•	Height between 34–38 inches
•	Secure mounting (no wobbling)
•	Continuous along full stair run
•	Ends return to wall (no snag hazards)
•	Graspable profile (not too wide or flat)
Immediate Hazard: Loose or missing handrail.
6. Guardrail Requirements (IBC §1015 – Guards)
Inspect:
•	Guardrail present on open sides of landings or stairs
•	Height ≥ 42 inches
•	Openings < 4 inches
•	No climbable horizontal elements
•	No loose posts or sections
Severe: Openings > 4 inches or climbable guardrail.
7. Lighting & Visibility (IBC §1003.2)
Inspect:
•	Adequate lighting for safe stair use
•	No dark areas or shadows hiding steps
•	No missing bulbs in stair lighting
•	Switches operable
Severe: Insufficient lighting causing trip hazard.
8. Trip Hazards (IPMC §305 / IBC §1003)
Inspect:
•	Loose rugs at top/bottom of stairs
•	Clutter on steps
•	Items stored on stairway
•	Uneven surfaces
•	Damaged transitions at landings
Severe: Trip hazard in egress path.
9. Moisture & Water Intrusion (IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Water on steps
•	Moisture causing slippery surfaces
•	Mold like substance on stair surfaces
•	Water damage to wood or drywall near stairs
Immediate Hazard: Water + electrical interaction near stair lighting.

inside.deficiencySelected: Structural system exhibits signs of serious failure and may threaten the resident’s safety.
inside.deficiencyDetail: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Structural system exhibits signs of serious failure and may threaten the resident’s safety.
inside.standard:
✅ NSPIRE – Common Area Structural System)
1. What to Inspect (Structural Elements)
Inspect all visible structural components in common areas:

Load‑bearing walls (interior & exterior portions visible)

Columns, posts, beams, headers

Floor systems (joists, subfloor, slab)

Ceiling/roof structural elements visible from common areas

Stair structural framing

Foundation walls visible from basements/common areas

Structural supports in mechanical rooms, storage rooms, basements

Elevated walkways, landings, mezzanines

2. Inspection Method
A. Observation – Look for
Cracks in walls, beams, columns, ceilings

Sagging floors, ceilings, beams

Bowing, leaning, shifting walls

Water‑damaged structural components

Rusted steel beams/connectors

Termite or pest‑damaged wood

Spalling concrete or exposed rebar

Gaps between structural connections

Separation between walls, floors, ceilings

Structural movement indicators (doors out of square, uneven floors)

B. Physical / Functional Check (Non‑Destructive)
Apply light pressure to suspect columns/posts

Check for excessive movement or instability

Walk floors to detect soft spots, bounce, deflection

Check stair landings for structural firmness

C. Environmental Check
Look for moisture sources affecting structural components

Check for mold‑like substance indicating long‑term moisture

Check for leaks from plumbing or roof systems impacting structure
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Structural System Inspection (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305 – Structural Integrity)
Inspection applies to:
•	Walls (interior & demising)
•	Ceilings
•	Floors
•	Columns, beams, posts
•	Load bearing partitions
•	Structural finishes (drywall, plaster, sheathing)
•	Stairs, landings, and structural supports
If none of these components show deterioration → Not Applicable.
2. Walls (Load Bearing & Non Load Bearing)
Inspect:
•	Cracks (vertical, horizontal, diagonal)
•	Bulging, bowing, or leaning walls
•	Loose or delaminated drywall/plaster
•	Moisture staining or swelling
•	Separation at corners or joints
•	Structural movement around doors/windows
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural cracks or bowing → Immediate Hazard
•	Moisture damaged structural wall → Severe
3. Ceilings
Inspect:
•	Sagging or deflection
•	Cracks (especially long or wide)
•	Water stains or active leaks
•	Loose drywall or plaster
•	Separation at seams or tape failure
•	Soft spots indicating structural compromise
Immediate Hazard: Ceiling collapse risk.
4. Floors
Inspect:
•	Soft spots, spongy areas
•	Uneven or sloped flooring
•	Cracked tile or concrete indicating movement
•	Moisture damage or swelling
•	Loose floorboards
•	Structural vibration or bounce
Severe: Structural floor movement or moisture compromised subfloor.
5. Columns, Beams & Posts (IBC Chapter 16)
Inspect:
•	Visible cracks or splits
•	Rust or corrosion (steel)
•	Rot or termite damage (wood)
•	Deflection or sagging
•	Loose connections or fasteners
•	Separation from bearing points
Immediate Hazard: Any structural member showing failure or separation.
6. Load Bearing Partitions
Inspect:
•	Cracks near door frames
•	Doors binding or misaligned (indicates movement)
•	Gaps at ceiling or floor
•	Bowing or bulging
•	Moisture damage affecting structural integrity
Severe: Movement or deformation of load bearing walls.
7. Stairs & Landings (Structural Portion Only)
Inspect:
•	Loose or unstable treads/risers
•	Structural cracks in stair framing
•	Sagging or deflection
•	Rot or corrosion
•	Separation from wall or support structure
Immediate Hazard: Structural instability of stairs.
8. Moisture & Structural Interaction (IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Water intrusion at walls, ceilings, floors
•	Mold like substance indicating long term moisture
•	Swollen or delaminated structural materials
•	Rust on fasteners or metal framing
•	Termite or pest damage
Severe: Moisture compromising structural integrity.

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Interior Common Area Trash Chute Inspection
1. Trash Chute Intake Doors (IBC §716 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	Door present and intact
•	Self closing and self latching
•	Fire rated label present and legible
•	No gaps >⅛ inch around frame
•	No damage, dents, or missing parts
•	No propped open doors
•	No missing or damaged gaskets
Hazard Severity:
•	Door not self closing or not latching → Immediate Hazard
•	Missing fire rated door → Immediate Hazard
•	Gaps compromising fire rating → Severe
2. Trash Chute Interior (Visual Only)
Inspect:
•	No visible obstructions
•	No trash buildup at intake
•	No signs of chute blockage
•	No excessive odors indicating sanitation failure
Hazard Severity:
•	Trash buildup causing blockage → Severe
•	Severe odor indicating sanitation hazard → Moderate/Severe
3. Compactor Room / Discharge Room (IFC §603 / IPMC §308)
Inspect:
•	Room clean and free of combustible storage
•	Compactor operable and intact
•	No exposed wiring
•	No missing guards or safety shields
•	No trash overflow
•	No water or sewage leaks
•	Fire rated door to room self closes and latches
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
•	Combustible storage → Immediate Hazard
•	Sewage leak → Immediate Hazard
•	Fire rated door not closing → Immediate Hazard
4. Ventilation & Odor Control (IMC §510)
Inspect:
•	Ventilation system operable
•	No blocked exhaust vents
•	No damaged ductwork
•	No mold like substance near vents
•	No excessive negative pressure preventing chute door closure
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked ventilation → Severe
•	Mold like substance → Severe
5. Fire Safety Interaction (IBC §716 / IFC §703)
Inspect:
•	No penetrations in fire rated walls around chute
•	No missing fire blocking or fire stopping
•	No damaged fire rated assemblies
•	No propped open fire doors
•	No combustible storage near chute
Hazard Severity:
•	Fire rated breach → Immediate Hazard
•	Combustibles near chute → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Ventilation (Other Than Kitchen & Bath) –Common Area
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §402–404 / IMC §501)
Inspection applies to:
•	Laundry/utility exhaust fans
•	Passive wall/ceiling vents
•	Transfer grilles
•	Closet ventilation openings
•	Window ventilation components
•	Mechanical exhaust fans not tied to HVAC
•	Any non kitchen, non bathroom ventilation system
If none exist → Not Applicable.
2. Laundry / Utility Exhaust Vent (IMC §504)
Inspect:
•	Fan operates and pulls air
•	No lint buildup blocking grille
•	No moisture staining around vent
•	No mold like substance
•	No exposed wiring
•	Ducting intact and connected (if visible)
Hazard Severity:
•	Lint buildup creating fire hazard → Severe
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
3. Passive Vents (Wall, Ceiling, Closet) – IPMC §402–403
Inspect:
•	Vents unobstructed
•	No paint sealing vents shut
•	No debris or dust blockage
•	No mold like substance
•	No damaged or missing vent covers
•	No sharp edges or broken louvers
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked ventilation → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
4. Transfer Grilles (Airflow Between Rooms)
Inspect:
•	Grille intact and secure
•	No blockage or obstruction
•	No dust buildup reducing airflow
•	No mold like substance
•	No sharp edges or broken fins
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked grille → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
5. Window Ventilation Components
Inspect:
•	Windows operable (open/close smoothly)
•	No broken glass
•	No damaged screens
•	No mold like substance on frames
•	No condensation causing deterioration
•	No gaps allowing pests
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken glass → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold + moisture → Severe
6. Closet / Enclosed Space Ventilation
Inspect:
•	Vent openings present (if required)
•	No blocked or sealed vents
•	No mold like substance
•	No moisture buildup
•	No odors indicating poor ventilation
Hazard Severity:
•	Mold + moisture → Severe
7. Mechanical Exhaust (Non Kitchen / Non Bath)
Inspect:
•	Fan operates and pulls air
•	No excessive noise or vibration
•	No dust blockage
•	No exposed wiring
•	No moisture staining around fan
•	No mold like substance
Hazard Severity:
•	Inoperable fan → Severe
•	Exposed wiring → Immediate Hazard
8. Moisture & Ventilation Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Moisture staining near vents
•	Mold like substance around ventilation openings
•	Condensation buildup
•	Odors indicating inadequate air movement
•	Poor ventilation causing humidity accumulation
Hazard Severity:
•	Mold + active moisture → Severe
•	Moisture + electrical → Immediate Hazard
9. Fire Safety Interaction (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	No lint buildup near laundry exhaust
•	No combustible materials near vents
•	No overheating of fan motors
•	No grease or dust accumulation creating ignition risk
Hazard Severity:
•	Lint fire hazard → Severe
•	Overheating motor → Immediate Hazard
