inside.deficiencySelected: Wall-Interior
inside.deficiencyDetail: Interior wall component(s), severe cracks, not functionally adequate. Damaged trim greater than 10% to 50% of the wall area.
inside.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Interior wall component(s) is not functionally adequate (i.e., impacts the integrity of the interior wall or does not allow interior wall to provide vertical separation between rooms or spaces).
inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Wall & Wall Component Inspection (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §305 – Interior Structure)
Inspection applies to:
•	Interior walls (load bearing & non load bearing)
•	Demising walls between units
•	Partition walls
•	Wall finishes (drywall, plaster, paneling)
•	Wall components (trim, baseboards, wall mounted fixtures)
•	Fire rated assemblies (where applicable)
If no wall deterioration exists → Not Applicable.
2. Structural Condition of Walls
Inspect:
•	Cracks (vertical, horizontal, diagonal)
•	Bulging, bowing, or leaning walls
•	Loose, delaminated, or unstable drywall/plaster
•	Separation at corners, joints, or seams
•	Movement around door/window frames
•	Holes or penetrations compromising structure
Hazard Severity:
•	Bowing or leaning → Immediate Hazard
•	Structural cracks indicating movement → Severe
3. Wall Surface Condition (IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Peeling, flaking, or blistering paint
•	Damaged drywall (holes, gouges, punctures)
•	Loose or missing wall panels
•	Exposed substrate (wood, gypsum, plaster)
•	Sharp edges or protruding fasteners
•	Stains or discoloration
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Exposed substrate → Severe
4. Moisture & Water Intrusion Indicators
Inspect:
•	Water stains
•	Bubbling or delaminated paint
•	Swollen drywall or paneling
•	Soft or spongy wall sections
•	Mold like substance
•	Moisture around plumbing walls, windows, or exterior facing walls
Hazard Severity:
•	Moisture + structural deterioration → Severe
•	Mold + electrical → Immediate Hazard
5. Fire Resistance & Penetrations (IBC §714)
Inspect:
•	Penetrations in fire rated demising walls
•	Missing or damaged fire blocking
•	Unsealed openings around pipes, cables, or conduits
•	Damaged fire rated gypsum board
Hazard Severity:
•	Breach in fire rated wall → Severe
6. Wall Mounted Components
Inspect:
•	Electrical outlets and switches
•	Wall heaters
•	Cabinets, shelves, and brackets
•	Handrails or grab bars
•	Thermostats and sensors
Check for:
•	Loose or unstable mounting
•	Exposed wiring
•	Damage to wall from mounting failure
Hazard Severity:
•	Exposed electrical → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose heavy wall mounted items → Severe
7. Baseboards, Trim & Joint Components
Inspect:
•	Loose or missing baseboards
•	Gaps between trim and wall
•	Moisture damage at baseboards
•	Termite or pest damage
•	Sharp edges or splintering
Hazard Severity:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Moisture damaged trim indicating leak → Severe
8. Pest & Termite Indicators (IPMC §309)
Inspect:
•	Holes or tunnels in drywall
•	Frass (termite droppings)
•	Chewed or damaged wall components
•	Soft or hollow sounding wood trim
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural termite damage → Severe
9. Safety Interaction (IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Water near electrical outlets
•	Loose wall sections that may fall
•	Trip hazards from fallen wall debris
•	No destructive inspection allowed (no opening walls)
Hazard Severity:
•	Water + electrical → Immediate Hazard
•	Falling wall material → Immediate Hazard

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Water Heater Inspection (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §505 / IPC Chapter 5)
Inspection applies to:
•	Gas water heaters
•	Electric water heaters
•	Tank type or tankless units
•	Water heaters located inside the dwelling unit (closet, laundry room, utility room)
If no water heater is present → Not Applicable.
2. General Condition & Installation
Inspect:
•	Unit securely installed, not leaning or unstable
•	No rust, corrosion, or deterioration on tank or housing
•	No scorch marks, soot, or burn discoloration
•	No water pooling around base
•	No missing access panels
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural instability → Immediate Hazard
•	Rust compromising tank → Severe
3. Temperature & Pressure Relief Valve (TPR Valve) – IPC §504.6
Inspect:
•	TPR valve present
•	Discharge pipe installed
•	Pipe terminates within 6–24 inches of floor (2-6 inches NSPIRE)
•	Pipe not capped, threaded, or reduced
•	No leaks at valve or discharge line
•	No corrosion at valve connection
Immediate Hazard: Missing or improperly installed TPR valve/discharge pipe.
4. Gas Water Heater (IFC §603 / IMC §303)
Inspect:
•	No gas odor
•	No hissing at gas line or shutoff valve
•	Flex connector intact, not kinked or corroded
•	Burner flame steady (blue, not yellow/orange)
•	No soot or combustion residue
•	Proper venting (draft hood secure, vent pipe intact)
•	No combustibles stored near heater
Immediate Hazard: Gas leak, damaged flex line, or improper venting.
5. Electric Water Heater (IPMC §604 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	No exposed wiring
•	No scorch marks at electrical connections
•	No water contacting electrical components
•	Breaker labeled and accessible
•	No damaged conduit or wiring insulation
Immediate Hazard: Water + electrical interaction.
6. Venting & Combustion Air (IMC §501 / §304.6)
Inspect:
•	Vent pipe intact, properly connected
•	No gaps, disconnections, or backdrafting
•	No soot at vent termination
•	Combustion air openings unobstructed
•	No signs of exhaust entering living space
Severe: Backdrafting or blocked vent.
7. Water Supply & Plumbing Connections (IPC §604–§605)
Inspect:
•	No leaks at cold/hot supply lines
•	No corrosion on shutoff valves
•	No damaged or loose fittings
•	No moisture staining on walls or flooring
•	No mold like substance near plumbing
Severe: Active leak or moisture damage.
8. Drain Pan & Overflow Protection (IPC §504.7)
Inspect:
•	Drain pan present if required

inside.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Window Inspection (Common Area)
1. Scope & Applicability (IPMC §304.13 / §305)
Inspection applies to:
•	All operable and fixed windows
•	Window frames, sashes, tracks, locks
•	Glazing (glass)
•	Screens
•	Window wells (if present)
•	Egress windows (bedrooms)
If no windows exist → Not Applicable.
2. Window Operation & Function (IPMC §304.13.2)
Inspect:
•	Window opens and closes smoothly
•	No binding, sticking, or excessive force required
•	Window stays open without falling
•	Locking mechanism operable
•	No missing or broken hardware
Hazard Severity:
•	Window that will not stay open → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable bedroom egress window → Severe
3. Glazing (Glass Condition) (IPMC §304.13.1)
Inspect:
•	No broken, cracked, or shattered glass
•	No sharp edges
•	No loose glazing or unsecured panes
•	No fogging between double pane units (seal failure)
Hazard Severity:
•	Broken glass → Immediate Hazard
•	Loose glazing → Severe
4. Frame, Sash & Track Condition
Inspect:
•	No rot, rust, or corrosion
•	No warped or swollen frames
•	No loose or unstable sashes
•	Tracks clean and unobstructed
•	No gaps allowing water intrusion or pests
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural frame deterioration → Severe
•	Gaps causing water intrusion → Severe
5. Weather Tightness & Moisture Indicators (IPMC §304.13 / §305.1)
Inspect:
•	No water leaks at window
•	No moisture staining on sill or wall
•	No swollen drywall or trim
•	No mold like substance
•	No condensation causing deterioration
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + moisture → Severe
•	Moisture + electrical → Immediate Hazard
6. Screens (IPMC §304.13.3)
Inspect:
•	Screens present where required
•	No tears, holes, or missing screens
•	Screens fit securely in frame
•	No bent or damaged frames
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing screen (if required for ventilation) → Moderate
•	Sharp edges on damaged screen → Immediate Hazard
7. Egress Requirements (IBC §1030 – Emergency Escape & Rescue Openings)
Inspect bedroom windows:
•	Minimum clear opening size (varies by jurisdiction)
•	Window opens without tools or special knowledge
•	No security bars without quick release mechanism
•	No obstructions (furniture, bars, locks)
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked or inoperable egress window → Immediate Hazard
8. Security & Safety (IPMC §304.13.2 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Locks present and operable
•	No missing or broken latches
•	No loose or unstable window assemblies
•	No falling hazard from loose sash
•	No sharp edges on frame or hardware
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose sash that may fall → Immediate Hazard
9. Window Wells (If Applicable)
Inspect:
•	No debris blocking exit
•	No standing water
•	No structural deterioration
•	No damaged or missing covers
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked window well → Severe

inside.deficiencySelected: Window component is damaged or missing, and the window is not functionally adequate
inside.deficiencyDetail: The window component is missing or damaged window seals (i.e., cannot protect from the elements), or the outer screen has a hole, tear, or cut that is 1 inch or greater.
inside.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Any portion of a visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) window component is damaged (i.e., visibly defective) and the window is not functionally adequate (i.e., cannot protect from the elements, bugs, or debris, permit illumination within the interior space, or permit visual access between spaces).
 OR 
Any portion of a visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) window component is missing (i.e., evidence of prior installation, but is now not present or is incomplete) and the window is not functionally adequate (i.e., cannot protect from the elements, bugs, or debris, permit illumination within the interior space, or permit visual access between spaces).
 OR 
A visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) window screen has a hole, tear, or cut that is 1 inch or greater.

•	Loose glazing → Severe
4. Frame, Sash & Track Condition
Inspect:
•	No rot, rust, or corrosion
•	No warped or swollen frames
•	No loose or unstable sashes
•	Tracks clean and unobstructed
•	No gaps allowing water intrusion or pests
Hazard Severity:
•	Structural frame deterioration → Severe
•	Gaps causing water intrusion → Severe
5. Weather Tightness & Moisture Indicators (IPMC §304.13 / §305.1)
Inspect:
•	No water leaks at window
•	No moisture staining on sill or wall
•	No swollen drywall or trim
•	No mold like substance
•	No condensation causing deterioration
Hazard Severity:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + moisture → Severe
•	Moisture + electrical → Immediate Hazard
6. Screens (IPMC §304.13.3)
Inspect:
•	Screens present where required
•	No tears, holes, or missing screens
•	Screens fit securely in frame
•	No bent or damaged frames
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing screen (if required for ventilation) → Moderate
•	Sharp edges on damaged screen → Immediate Hazard
7. Egress Requirements (IBC §1030 – Emergency Escape & Rescue Openings)
Inspect bedroom windows:
•	Minimum clear opening size (varies by jurisdiction)
•	Window opens without tools or special knowledge
•	No security bars without quick release mechanism
•	No obstructions (furniture, bars, locks)
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked or inoperable egress window → Immediate Hazard
8. Security & Safety (IPMC §304.13.2 / IFC §605)
Inspect:
•	Locks present and operable
•	No missing or broken latches
•	No loose or unstable window assemblies
•	No falling hazard from loose sash
•	No sharp edges on frame or hardware
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose sash that may fall → Immediate Hazard
9. Window Wells (If Applicable)
Inspect:
•	No debris blocking exit
•	No standing water
•	No structural deterioration
•	No damaged or missing covers
Hazard Severity:
•	Blocked window well → Severe

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Bathroom Inspection Protocol – Unit Bathroom (Including Mold & Grab Bars)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / §604)
•	Assess lighting and visibility.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, active leaks, sewage, slippery floors.
•	Confirm safe entry.
2. Required Fixtures (IPMC §505 / IPC §405–409)
Verify presence, stability, and operability of:
•	Toilet — flushes fully, refills, no leaks.
•	Sink — hot/cold water, drains properly.
•	Tub/Shower — hot/cold water, diverter works, drains properly.
Fixtures must be securely mounted and free of cracks.
3. Water Supply (IPC §604–606)
•	Test hot and cold water at sink and tub/shower.
•	Verify adequate pressure and temperature.
•	Inspect supply lines for leaks, corrosion, improper materials.
4. Drainage & Waste System (IPC §701–706)
•	Drains must flow freely; no standing water.
•	P traps must be present and properly installed.
•	No sewer gas odor.
•	No leaks at traps or drain connections.
5. Ventilation (IPMC §403 / IBC §1203)
•	Mechanical exhaust fan must operate and vent to exterior.
•	If no fan, window must open fully.
•	Check for moisture buildup, condensation, mildew indicators.
6. Electrical Safety (IPMC §604 / NEC reference)
•	Light fixture operable.
•	GFCI protection required for bathroom receptacles.
•	No exposed wiring, open junction boxes, or damaged devices.
•	No electrical components subject to moisture.
7. Surfaces & Structural Integrity (IPMC §305–309)
•	Floors intact; no slip/trip hazards.
•	Walls/ceilings intact; no holes or loose materials.
•	Inspect for water damage, swelling, rot, or mold like substance.
•	Tile, grout, and finishes must be intact and cleanable.
Mold specific ICC guidance:
•	Mold like substance indicates moisture failure and must be traced to source (ventilation, plumbing, envelope).
8. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
•	Identify any mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, fixtures, or caulking.
•	Check behind/around tub, shower, and sink for moisture staining.
•	Inspect for active leaks contributing to mold.
•	Note any persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold like substance = Moderate
•	Mold caused by active leak = Severe
•	Mold with electrical involvement = Immediate Hazard
9. Grab Bars & Accessibility (ICC A117.1 / ISO 21542)
(Required only in accessible units or designated accessible bathrooms)
•	Grab bars must be present, secure, and properly anchored.
•	No looseness or movement when pulled.
•	Bars must be free of rust, cracks, or sharp edges.
•	Clear floor space must be provided at toilet and tub/shower.
•	Controls (faucets, switches) must be operable with one hand.
Grab bar failure = Severe safety deficiency.
10. Sanitation & Hygiene (IPMC §502–503)
•	No human waste, sewage, or heavy filth.
•	No persistent sewage or mold odors.
•	Bathroom must be hygienic and free of infestation.
11. Privacy & Security (IPMC §702)
•	Bathroom door must close and latch.
•	Window must have privacy covering if visibility to exterior/common areas exists.

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Bathroom Inspection Protocol – Unit Bathroom (Including Mold & Grab Bars)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / §604)
•	Assess lighting and visibility.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, active leaks, sewage, slippery floors.
•	Confirm safe entry.
2. Required Fixtures (IPMC §505 / IPC §405–409)
Verify presence, stability, and operability of:
•	Toilet — flushes fully, refills, no leaks.
•	Sink — hot/cold water, drains properly.
•	Tub/Shower — hot/cold water, diverter works, drains properly.
Fixtures must be securely mounted and free of cracks.
3. Water Supply (IPC §604–606)
•	Test hot and cold water at sink and tub/shower.
•	Verify adequate pressure and temperature.
•	Inspect supply lines for leaks, corrosion, improper materials.
4. Drainage & Waste System (IPC §701–706)
•	Drains must flow freely; no standing water.
•	P traps must be present and properly installed.
•	No sewer gas odor.
•	No leaks at traps or drain connections.
5. Ventilation (IPMC §403 / IBC §1203)
•	Mechanical exhaust fan must operate and vent to exterior.
•	If no fan, window must open fully.
•	Check for moisture buildup, condensation, mildew indicators.
6. Electrical Safety (IPMC §604 / NEC reference)
•	Light fixture operable.
•	GFCI protection required for bathroom receptacles.
•	No exposed wiring, open junction boxes, or damaged devices.
•	No electrical components subject to moisture.
7. Surfaces & Structural Integrity (IPMC §305–309)
•	Floors intact; no slip/trip hazards.
•	Walls/ceilings intact; no holes or loose materials.
•	Inspect for water damage, swelling, rot, or mold like substance.
•	Tile, grout, and finishes must be intact and cleanable.
Mold specific ICC guidance:
•	Mold like substance indicates moisture failure and must be traced to source (ventilation, plumbing, envelope).
8. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
•	Identify any mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, fixtures, or caulking.
•	Check behind/around tub, shower, and sink for moisture staining.
•	Inspect for active leaks contributing to mold.
•	Note any persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold like substance = Moderate
•	Mold caused by active leak = Severe
•	Mold with electrical involvement = Immediate Hazard
9. Grab Bars & Accessibility (ICC A117.1 / ISO 21542)
(Required only in accessible units or designated accessible bathrooms)
•	Grab bars must be present, secure, and properly anchored.
•	No looseness or movement when pulled.
•	Bars must be free of rust, cracks, or sharp edges.
•	Clear floor space must be provided at toilet and tub/shower.
•	Controls (faucets, switches) must be operable with one hand.
Grab bar failure = Severe safety deficiency.
10. Sanitation & Hygiene (IPMC §502–503)
•	No human waste, sewage, or heavy filth.
•	No persistent sewage or mold odors.
•	Bathroom must be hygienic and free of infestation.
11. Privacy & Security (IPMC §702)
•	Bathroom door must close and latch.
•	Window must have privacy covering if visibility to exterior/common areas exists.

unit.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Stow items, including food, sanitation, and household supplies
unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Cabinets & Storage (Non Kitchen / Non Bathroom)
1. Required Components (IPMC §305 / §309)
Inspect all non kitchen, non bathroom storage:
•	Bedroom closets
•	Hallway closets
•	Linen closets
•	Laundry closets
•	Built in cabinets
•	Shelving (fixed or adjustable)
•	Closet rods, tracks, hinges, pulls
Cabinets and storage must be present, stable, and functional.
2. Structural Condition (IPMC §305.4 / §305.5)
Check for:
•	Secure mounting (no loose cabinets or shelves)
•	No rot, swelling, delamination, or structural failure
•	No broken shelves or missing supports
•	No sharp edges, splintered wood, or protruding fasteners
•	No holes exposing framing or pest pathways
ICC Hazard Rule: Any collapse risk or sharp edge = unsafe condition.
3. Operability (IPMC §305.3)
Test all components:
•	Doors open/close fully
•	Drawers slide smoothly
•	Hinges, pulls, and tracks secure
•	Shelves stable under light load
•	Closet rods secure and properly supported
4. Sanitation & Environmental Conditions (IPMC §308 / §309)
Verify:
•	No mold like substance
•	No water intrusion or staining
•	No pest intrusion (droppings, holes, nesting)
•	Surfaces cleanable and intact
5. Laundry Area Storage (IPC / IPMC Moisture Requirements)
Inspect:
•	Cabinets near washer/dryer securely mounted
•	No moisture damage from laundry equipment
•	No heat damage near dryer
•	Adequate clearance for appliance operation
6. Accessibility (ICC A117.1 / ISO 21542 where applicable)
For accessible units or required common areas:
•	Reachable storage heights
•	Operable hardware (one hand operation, no tight grasping)
•	Clear floor space in front of storage
•	No obstructions limiting access
7. Fire & Utility Safety (IBC §701 / IPMC §603)
Check:
•	No storage blocking electrical panels or shutoff valves
•	No combustible storage near heat producing appliances
•	No damaged wiring inside storage cabinets
•	Dryer venting unobstructed (if cabinet enclosed)
8. ICC Aligned Deficiency Classification
Unsafe / Immediate Hazard
•	Sharp edges
•	Collapse risk (loose shelves/cabinets)
•	Exposed electrical inside cabinet

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Call For Aid Inspection
Senior Living Multi Unit Residential Building
1. Scope & Applicability (NFPA 72 / IPMC §604)
Inspect all call for aid components inside the unit:
•	Pull cord stations (bathroom, bedroom, living area)
•	Nurse call buttons
•	Emergency call panels
•	Intercom or two way communication devices
•	Audible/visual annunciators
•	Indicator lights
•	Supporting electrical wiring
If no call for aid system exists → Not Applicable.
2. Device Presence & Required Locations
Inspect:
•	Pull cord present in bathroom (required in senior living units).
•	Pull cord present in bedroom (common requirement).
•	Call for aid button present near bedside or accessible location.
•	Device mounted at accessible height (typically 34–48 inches).
•	Cord length adequate to reach floor (bathroom).
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing required call for aid device → Immediate Hazard.
3. Operability & Functional Test (NFPA 72)
Inspect:
•	Device activates alarm when pulled/pressed.
•	Audible alarm sounds locally.
•	Visual indicator activates (light, panel indicator).
•	Signal reaches central monitoring station (if applicable).
•	No delay, intermittent activation, or failure.
•	Reset function works properly.
Hazard Severity:
•	Device fails activation test → Immediate Hazard.
•	No audible/visual alarm → Immediate Hazard.
4. Physical Condition of Device
Inspect:
•	No cracks, breaks, or missing components.
•	Pull cord intact (not frayed, cut, or shortened).
•	No loose mounting hardware.
•	No damaged buttons or switches.
•	No missing indicator lights.
Hazard Severity:
•	Damaged pull cord preventing activation → Immediate Hazard.
•	Loose device that may detach → Severe.
5. Accessibility & Reach Range (ICC A117.1)
Inspect:
•	Pull cord reaches floor in bathroom.
•	Device reachable from wheelchair position.
•	No obstructions blocking access (furniture, storage).
•	Cord not tied, shortened, or wrapped around fixtures.
Hazard Severity:
•	Obstructed or unreachable device → Severe.
6. Bathroom Specific Requirements
Inspect:
•	Pull cord located near toilet.
•	Pull cord located near shower/tub.
•	Device moisture resistant.
•	No mold like substance near device.
•	No water damage affecting mounting.
Hazard Severity:
•	Missing bathroom pull cord → Immediate Hazard.
•	Moisture damage compromising device → Severe.
7. Annunciator Panel / Remote Indicator (If Present)
Inspect:
•	Panel lights functional.
•	No missing bulbs/LED indicators.
•	No error codes or fault signals.
•	No audible alarm failure.
•	No loose or damaged panel components.
Hazard Severity:
•	Fault signal indicating system failure → Immediate Hazard.

unit.deficiencySelected: Carbon monoxide alarm does not produce audio or visual alarm when tested.

unit.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Carbon monoxide detector does not produce audio or visual alarm when tested.
unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Carbon Monoxide Alarm Inspection
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / §604)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, active leaks, missing life safety devices.
•	Ensure CO alarm is visible and unobstructed.
2. Required Presence & Location (IRC §315)
CO alarms must be installed:
•	Outside each sleeping area
•	In the immediate vicinity of bedrooms
•	On every level of the dwelling unit
•	In units with fuel burning appliances, fireplaces, or attached garages
Location rules:
•	Mounted per manufacturer instructions
•	Not blocked by furniture or drapes
•	Not installed in dead air spaces (corners, ceiling peaks)
Missing required CO alarm = Immediate Hazard.
3. Physical Condition (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect:
•	Housing intact; no cracks or missing covers
•	Battery door intact; battery present
•	No corrosion, rust, or moisture damage
•	No exposed wiring (hardwired units)
•	No paint or debris obstructing sensor openings
Exposed wiring = Unsafe Condition.
4. Expiration & Compliance
•	Check manufacture date on back of alarm
•	CO alarms expire at 7–10 years depending on model
•	Expired alarm = Severe deficiency
•	Confirm UL listed or equivalent certification
5. Functional Test (NFPA 720 Principles / IPMC §604)
Perform full activation:
•	Press TEST button
•	Confirm audible alarm activates
•	Confirm visual indicator activates (LED or display)
•	For combination alarms: verify CO function, not just smoke
•	Hardwired/interconnected alarms: confirm other alarms respond
•	Reset function must operate correctly
Failure of any required function = Severe.
6. Electrical & Power Source Safety (IPMC §604)
Check:
•	Hardwired alarms securely connected
•	No open junction boxes
•	No damaged wiring or loose connections
•	Battery powered alarms have fresh battery
•	No water intrusion near alarm
•	No water + electrical interaction (Immediate Hazard)
7. Environmental & Senior Safety Conditions
•	Alarm must be audible from sleeping areas
•	Alarm must not be installed behind doors or drapes
•	Alarm must be reachable for testing (or test via remote panel)
•	No mobility obstacles blocking access to alarm area
8. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on walls, ceilings, or alarm housing
•	Moisture staining around alarm
•	Active leaks contributing to mold
•	Persistent mold odor
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate

unit.deficiencySelected: carbon monoxide alarm is missing, not installed or not installed in the proper location.
unit.deficiencyDetail: The location of the previous installation is not relevant. Unit/building contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace. Carbon monoxide  alarm is missing alarms near sleeping areas, bathrooms, remote furnaces, or garages, making the unit noncompliant.
unit.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: One (1) or more of the following scenarios exists:

  1.    Unit contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace, and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:  
    a. in the immediate vicinity of each sleeping area.   
  OR
    b. within each bedroom.

  2. Bedroom or bathroom attached to bedroom:

  a. contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace.
 OR
  b. has adjacent spaces from which byproducts of combustion gases can flow.
 AND 
  c. Carbon monoxide alarm is not installed in each bedroom.    

3. Unit or sleeping area is served by a forced-air furnace that is located elsewhere and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
 a. in the immediate vicinity of each bedroom.
 OR
  b. within each bedroom.
 OR
c. within the room or area with the first duct register and the carbon monoxide alarm signals are automatically transmitted to an approved location

4. Unit or bedroom area is located in a building that contains a fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace and:     
  a.    a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed in an approved location between the fuel-burning appliance or fuel-burning fireplace and the Unit or bedroom
OR 
 b. a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed on the ceiling of the room containing the fuel burning appliance       or fuel-burning fireplace. 
OR
 c. the Unit or bedroom has communicated openings to the fuel-burning appliance or fuel burning fireplace and a carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
      i. in the immediate vicinity of each bedroom.
 OR
      ii. within each bedroom

5. Unit or bedroom is located one (1) story or less above or below an attached private garage that:
    a. does not have natural ventilation.
 OR
    b. is enclosed and does not have a ventilation system for vehicle exhaust.
 AND 
  c. Carbon monoxide alarm is not installed:
      i. in the immediate vicinity of each sleeping area.
 OR
     ii. within each sleeping area.

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Ceiling & Ceiling Components
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IBC Structural Safety)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: falling materials, collapse risk, exposed wiring, active leaks.
•	Ensure ceiling area is unobstructed for visual inspection.
2. Ceiling Surface Condition (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect entire ceiling for:
•	Holes, missing drywall, missing tiles
•	Cracks (hairline vs structural)
•	Sagging, bulging, delamination
•	Loose tape, peeling finishes
•	Soft spots indicating moisture damage
Any collapse risk = Unsafe Condition (Immediate Hazard).
3. Moisture & Water Intrusion (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Check for:
•	Water stains or discoloration
•	Bubbling, swelling, or soft material
•	Active leaks (ceiling, fixtures, penetrations)
•	Mold like substance on ceiling surface
Severity:
•	Active leak = Severe
•	Mold + leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
4. Structural Integrity (IBC Chapter 16 / IPMC §305.2)
Verify:
•	Ceiling is stable and securely attached
•	No major cracks indicating structural movement
•	No separation at seams or wall ceiling joints
•	No failing plaster, gypsum, or tile systems
Any structural failure indicator = Severe.
5. Ceiling Components (IPMC §605 / IBC Electrical Safety)
Inspect all components mounted in or through the ceiling:
•	Light fixtures
•	Smoke/CO alarms
•	Sprinkler heads & escutcheons
•	HVAC registers
•	Access panels
•	Junction boxes
Check for:
•	Secure mounting
•	No gaps around penetrations
•	No exposed wiring
•	No damaged escutcheons
•	No missing covers
Exposed wiring = Immediate Hazard.
6. Ventilation & Mechanical Penetrations (IPMC §403 / IBC §1203)
Verify:
•	Exhaust fan housings secure
•	No moisture damage around vents
•	No gaps that allow pest entry
•	No condensation staining around mechanical penetrations
7. Fire Safety Penetrations (IBC §714 / IPMC §703)
Check:
•	Penetrations sealed with proper fire rated materials
•	No open gaps around pipes, ducts, or wiring
•	Sprinkler heads unobstructed and properly seated
Unsealed penetrations = Severe.
8. Sanitation & Environmental Conditions (IPMC §308 / §309)
Inspect for:
•	Mold like substance
•	Pest intrusion (droppings, holes, nesting)
•	Odors indicating moisture or mold
•	Surface contamination or heavy filth
9. Accessibility (ICC A117.1)
(Only applies to accessible units) Verify:
•	Ceiling mounted alarms and controls reachable per design
•	No protruding hazards affecting mobility routes
•	Components operable without tight grasping or twisting

unit.deficiencyDetail: A chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is incomplete or damaged such that it may not safely contain the fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior.
unit.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA:  Visually accessible (i.e., can be reasonably accessed and observed) chimney, flue, or firebox connected to a fireplace or wood-burning appliance is damaged (i.e., visibly defective; impacts functionality) such that it may not safely contain fire and convey smoke and combustion gases to the exterior.
unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Chimney Inspection (If Applicable)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IFC §603)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: falling masonry, active leaks, soot accumulation, or exposed wiring.
•	Ensure fireplace/chimney area is unobstructed.
2. Verify Applicability
A chimney inspection applies only if the unit contains:
•	A fireplace (wood burning, gas, or decorative)
•	A wood stove
•	A vented gas appliance using a chimney
•	A shared or individual flue serving the unit
If no chimney or flue is present → mark “Not Applicable.”
3. Exterior Chimney Interface (Visible Portions)
Inspect visible interior portions of the chimney chase or enclosure for:
•	Cracks, gaps, or missing masonry
•	Loose or deteriorated brick, stone, or tile
•	Damaged or missing fire rated enclosure materials
•	Signs of structural movement or separation
Any collapse risk = Immediate Hazard.
4. Firebox & Hearth Condition (IRC §1001 / IFC §603)
Check:
•	Firebox walls intact, no cracks or missing firebrick
•	Hearth extension present, stable, and non combustible
•	No combustible materials within required clearance
•	No soot buildup indicating improper draft
•	No rust or deterioration in gas log fireboxes
5. Flue & Venting (IRC §1002 / IFGC §503)
Inspect visible flue components:
•	No obstructions (soot, debris, nests)
•	No visible gaps, cracks, or missing flue tiles
•	Proper connection of gas appliance venting
•	No backdrafting or smoke stains indicating poor draft
•	Damper operable (if present)
Backdrafting = Severe deficiency.
6. Moisture & Mold Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Check for:
•	Water stains on chimney surfaces
•	Moisture intrusion around chimney chase

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Door Inspection (Entry, Fire, General, Garage)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IBC Chapter 7)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: falling door panels, exposed sharp edges, active leaks, or compromised fire rated assemblies.
•	Ensure door area is unobstructed.
2. Door Type Verification
Verify correct door type is installed:
•	Entry Door — solid core or rated per building requirements; provides security and weather protection.
•	Fire Door — labeled, rated, self closing, self latching; required at fire separation walls.
•	General Interior Door — operable, free of hazards.
•	Garage Door (Unit Attached Garage) — fire rated in most cases; must self close; must seal air transfer.
Missing required fire rated or garage separation door = Immediate Hazard.
3. Door Condition (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect:
•	No holes, cracks, delamination, or warping.
•	No rot, rust, or structural deterioration.
•	No loose panels or failing veneer.
•	No mold like substance on door surfaces or frame.
Structural failure = Severe.
4. Frame, Jamb & Hinges (IPMC §305 / NFPA 80)
Check:
•	Frame plumb, secure, and free of damage.
•	Hinges tight, not bent, rusted, or missing screws.
•	No excessive gaps between door and frame.
•	Strike plate present and secure.
Fire door hinge or frame damage = Severe.
5. Operability (IPMC §305.3)
Verify:
•	Door opens and closes fully without binding.
•	Door latches securely.
•	No excessive force required.
•	No obstruction preventing full swing.
Inoperable entry or fire door = Immediate Hazard.
6. Locks & Security (IPMC §304 / IBC §1010)
Inspect:
•	Entry door has operable lock or deadbolt.
•	No broken lock cylinders or loose hardware.
•	No double keyed deadbolts (generally prohibited).
•	Fire doors must not have unapproved locking devices.
Non functional entry lock = Severe.
7. Fire Rated Door Requirements (NFPA 80 / IBC §716)
(Only applies to fire doors & garage separation doors) Verify:
•	Fire label present and legible.
•	Door self closes completely.
•	Door self latches without manual assistance.
•	No field modifications to door or frame.
•	No missing or damaged intumescent seals.
•	No penetrations through door or frame.
Missing label or non closing fire door = Immediate Hazard.
8. Weather Stripping & Threshold (Entry & Garage Doors)
Check:
•	Weather stripping intact and properly seated.
•	No daylight visible around door edges.
•	Threshold secure and free of tripping hazards.
•	No water intrusion at bottom of door.
•	Garage door must prevent air transfer from garage to unit.
Water intrusion = Moderate to Severe depending on extent.
9. Garage Door (If Applicable) – Special Requirements (IRC / IBC)
Inspect:
•	Door is fire rated (typically 20 minute).
•	Door has self closing device (hinge or closer).
•	No openings allowing garage air into unit.
•	No damaged seals or penetrations.
•	No missing closer hardware.
Garage door not self closing = Immediate Hazard.
10. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on door, frame, or surrounding wall.
•	Moisture staining or swelling of wood components.
•	Active leaks from exterior or plumbing.
•	Persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + structural damage = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate
11. Accessibility (ICC A117.1)
(Applies to accessible units) Verify:
•	Door hardware operable with one hand (no tight grasping).
•	Lever handles present where required.
•	Clear width of 32 inches minimum.
•	Threshold height compliant (≤ 1/2 inch typical).
•	Door force within allowable limits.
Non compliant accessible door = Moderate to Severe depending on impact.

unit.deficiencySelected: Entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is damaged, inoperable or missing
unit.deficiencyDetail: Entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is damaged, inoperable or missing. or nonfunctional—causing a gap ≥¼ inch that lets in light or shows signs of water damage or dry rot.
unit.standard:
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: The entry door seal, gasket, or stripping is:
- damaged (i.e. visibly defective; impacts functionality);
- inoperable (i.e. overall system or component thereof not meeting function / purpose; with or without visible damage); or
- missing (i.e. evidence of prior installation, but now not present or is incomplete).
AND ONE OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS:
Condition 1:
- General door type: Results in a gap of ¼ inch wide or greater between the door slab and the stop molding on the jamb, or the jamb itself, or between the bottom of the door and the threshold or floor AND permits light around the closed door.
- Special door type: Results in a gap of ¼ inch wide or greater around or under the door or where the doors meet AND permits light around the closed door or where the doors meet.
Condition 2:
- General door type: There is evidence of water penetrating (e.g. water damage or dry rot) around or under the door.
- Special door type: There is evidence of water penetrating (e.g. water damage or dry rot) around or under the door or where the doors meet.

Inspect:
•	No holes, cracks, delamination, or warping.
•	No rot, rust, or structural deterioration.
•	No loose panels or failing veneer.
•	No mold like substance on door surfaces or frame.

Check:
•	Frame plumb, secure, and free of damage.

8. Weather Stripping & Threshold (Entry & Garage Doors)
Check:
•	Weather stripping intact and properly seated.
•	No daylight visible around door edges.
•	Threshold secure and free of tripping hazards.
•	No water intrusion at bottom of door.
•	Garage door must prevent air transfer from garage to unit.
Water intrusion = Moderate to Severe depending on extent.
9. Garage Door (If Applicable) – Special Requirements (IRC / IBC)
Inspect:
•	Door is fire rated (typically 20 minute).
•	Door has self closing device (hinge or closer).
•	No openings allowing garage air into unit.
•	No damaged seals or penetrations.
•	No missing closer hardware.
Garage door not self closing = Immediate Hazard.
10. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on door, frame, or surrounding wall.
•	Moisture staining or swelling of wood components.
•	Active leaks from exterior or plumbing.
•	Persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + structural damage = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate
11. Accessibility (ICC A117.1)
(Applies to accessible units) Verify:
•	Door hardware operable with one hand (no tight grasping).
•	Lever handles present where required.
•	Clear width of 32 inches minimum.
•	Threshold height compliant (≤ 1/2 inch typical).
•	Door force within allowable limits.
Non compliant accessible door = Moderate to Severe depending on impact.

unit.deficiencySelected: Drain
unit.deficiencyDetail: Drain is fully blocked. Or there is a problem with the drainage.
unit.standard: DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Standing water is present over the floor drain, or the floor drain is blocked such that the inspector believes water would be unable to drain.
unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Drainage Inspection
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / §604)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: active leaks, sewage backup, slippery floors, exposed plumbing.
•	Ensure access to all fixtures with drains (sink, tub/shower, laundry, floor drains if present).
2. Required Drainage Components (IPC §701–§706)
Verify presence and proper installation of:
•	Sink drain assembly
•	Tub/shower drain
•	Toilet waste connection
•	Laundry standpipe (if applicable)
•	Floor drain (if applicable)
•	P traps at all fixtures except toilets
Missing trap or improper connection = Immediate Hazard.
3. Drain Flow Performance (IPC §704 / §708)
Test each fixture:
•	Run water for 30–60 seconds
•	Confirm water drains freely
•	No standing water or slow drainage
•	No gurgling, bubbling, or backflow
•	No sewer gas odor during or after flow test
Slow drainage = Moderate Backflow or sewer gas = Severe.
4. Trap & Seal Integrity (IPC §1002)
Inspect:
•	P trap present and properly oriented
•	Trap seal depth between 2–4 inches
•	No dry traps (indicates lack of use or leak)
•	No cracks, corrosion, or improper materials (no flexible accordion traps)
Dry trap or missing trap = Immediate Hazard.
5. Leak Inspection (IPMC §305.1 / IPC §405–§409)
Check:
•	Drain connections under sinks
•	Tub/shower drain shoe and overflow
•	Toilet wax ring area
•	Laundry standpipe and trap
•	Floor drain body and surrounding slab
Active leak = Severe.
6. Venting & Airflow (IPC §901–§916)
Verify:
•	No gurgling or siphoning sounds
•	No sewer odor indicating vent blockage
•	Proper venting for all fixtures
•	No illegal S traps or unvented fixtures
Improper venting = Severe.
7. Drain Pipe Condition (IPMC §305 / IPC §704)
Inspect visible piping:
•	No cracks, corrosion, or deterioration
•	No improper materials (e.g., thin flex hose, non rated plastic)
•	No missing or loose slip joint nuts
•	No signs of past leaks (staining, swelling, mold like substance)
Corroded or failing pipe = Moderate to Severe depending on severity.
8. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance under sinks, around tubs, or near drains
•	Moisture staining or swelling of cabinets or walls
•	Persistent mold or sewage odor
•	Active leaks contributing to mold
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate
9. Floor Drain (If Applicable) (IPC §1002 / §1003)
Verify:
•	Drain present in laundry or mechanical areas
•	Trap seal maintained (add water if dry)
•	No debris blocking drain
•	No sewer gas odor
•	No backflow evidence
Dry floor drain = Moderate Backflow = Severe.
10. Accessibility (ICC A117.1)
(If unit is designated accessible) Verify:
•	Drain controls (e.g., pop up stoppers) operable with one hand
•	No tight grasping or twisting required
•	Clear floor space at fixtures
•	No protruding hazards under sinks (protective covers required)

unit.deficiencyDetail: Fire escape & Ladders, access to exteriors - doors and windows. (Double-key cylinder deadbolts and any locks or security features requiring a key, tool, or special effort from the street side are prohibited on exit doors, exit access doors, and egress windows.

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Egress (Exit Access) Inspection
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IBC §1001)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: blocked exits, collapse risks, exposed wiring, or fire door failures.
•	Ensure the egress path is fully visible and unobstructed.
2. Required Egress Path Identification (IBC §1006 / §1008)
Verify the unit has a compliant exit access path:
•	From unit interior → corridor → exit discharge
•	Path must be continuous, unobstructed, and clearly defined
•	No storage, furniture, or debris blocking the route
•	No dead end corridors exceeding allowed length
Blocked egress = Immediate Hazard.
3. Doorway Requirements (IBC §1010 / IPMC §304)
Inspect the unit entry door and any interior doors along the egress path:
•	Door must open easily without special knowledge or tools
•	No excessive force required
•	No broken hardware, binding, or obstruction
•	Clear width maintained (minimum 32 inches for accessible units)
•	Door must latch securely (entry door)
Inoperable entry door = Immediate Hazard.
4. Fire Rated Door Requirements (IBC §716 / NFPA 80)
(If the unit opens into a rated corridor) Verify:
•	Fire label present and legible
•	Door self closes fully
•	Door self latches without manual assistance
•	No field modifications
•	No missing intumescent seals
•	No penetrations through door or frame
Fire door not self closing = Immediate Hazard.
5. Egress Pathway Condition (IPMC §305 / IBC §1003)
Inspect:
•	Floors intact, no tripping hazards
•	No loose tiles, torn carpet, or uneven surfaces
•	No water intrusion or slippery conditions
•	No mold like substance along the path
•	No protruding hazards reducing clear width
Trip hazards = Moderate to Severe depending on severity.
6. Lighting & Visibility (IBC §1008 / IPMC §605)
Verify:
•	Adequate lighting along the egress path
•	Light fixtures operable
•	No exposed wiring
•	No missing or damaged covers
•	Emergency lighting (if required) functional
Exposed wiring = Immediate Hazard.
7. Egress Signage (If Applicable) (IBC §1013)
In some multi unit buildings:
•	Exit signs must be visible from the unit corridor
•	Signs must be illuminated
•	No missing or damaged signage
Missing required signage = Severe.
8. Stairways & Ramps (If Part of Unit Egress) (IBC §1011 / §1012)
Inspect:
•	Handrails secure
•	No loose or damaged steps
•	No uneven risers or treads
•	No obstructions
•	No water or mold accumulation
•	Adequate lighting
Loose handrail = Severe.
9. Mold & Moisture Assessment (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on walls, ceilings, floors, or doors along egress
•	Moisture staining or active leaks
•	Persistent mold odor
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate
10. Accessibility Requirements (ICC A117.1)
(If unit is designated accessible) Verify:
•	Clear width of 32 inches minimum
•	Door hardware operable with one hand
•	No tight grasping, pinching, or twisting
•	Threshold height compliant
•	No protruding objects reducing accessible route width
•	Adequate turning space at doorways
Non compliant accessible egress = Moderate to Severe.

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Electrical, Outlets, Switches, AFCI, GFCI & Minimum Lighting
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / NEC Article 110)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, burn marks, arcing, overheating, or water intrusion.
•	Ensure electrical components are accessible and unobstructed.
2. Required Electrical Components (IPMC §604 / NEC)
Verify presence and proper installation of:
•	Working lighting in all required rooms
•	Outlets spaced per NEC (typically every 12 ft, and on each wall >2 ft)
•	GFCI protection in wet/damp areas
•	AFCI protection in living spaces
•	Properly installed switches controlling lighting or receptacles
Missing required protection (GFCI/AFCI) = Immediate Hazard.
3. Outlet Inspection (Standard & GFCI)
General Outlets
Inspect:
•	No cracks, missing covers, or loose devices
•	No burn marks, discoloration, or melting
•	No exposed wiring
•	Outlet firmly mounted
•	Polarity correct (if tester used)
•	No backstabbed wiring if visible
GFCI Outlets (NEC 210.8)
Required in:
•	Bathrooms
•	Kitchens
•	Laundry areas
•	Exterior locations
•	Wet/damp areas
Test:
•	Press TEST → power must shut off
•	Press RESET → power must restore
•	Confirm downstream outlets behave correctly
GFCI failure = Immediate Hazard.
4. Switch Inspection
Inspect:
•	Switch operates smoothly
•	No cracking, looseness, or missing cover
•	No arcing, buzzing, or delay
•	No exposed wiring
•	Switch controls correct fixture or outlet
•	No heat damage or discoloration
Inoperable switch controlling required lighting = Severe.
5. AFCI Protection (NEC 210.12)
Required in:
•	Bedrooms
•	Living rooms
•	Hallways
•	Closets
•	Most habitable rooms
Inspection:
•	AFCI breaker labeled correctly
•	Press TEST → breaker must trip
•	Reset breaker → circuit must restore
•	No buzzing, arcing, or overheating
•	No mixed circuits defeating AFCI protection
AFCI failure = Immediate Hazard.
6. Minimum Lighting Requirements (IPMC §605 / IBC §1205)
Verify:
•	Each habitable room has a permanent light fixture or switched outlet
•	Bathrooms must have permanent lighting
•	Hallways and egress paths must be illuminated
•	No missing bulbs in required fixtures
•	No flickering, dimming, or unsafe fixtures
•	No exposed wiring or broken globes/shades
Missing required lighting = Severe.
7. Electrical Panel (If Located Inside Unit)
Inspect:
•	Panel cover present and secure
•	No open knockouts
•	Breakers labeled
•	No contamination (infestation-paint-foreign materials)
•	No scorch marks or overheating
•	No water intrusion
•	No missing AFCI/GFCI breakers where required
Exposed bus bars or missing panel cover = Immediate Hazard.
8. Moisture, Mold & Water Intrusion (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance near outlets, switches, or fixtures
•	Moisture staining or swelling of walls
•	Active leaks near electrical components
•	Condensation near lighting fixtures
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate
9. Accessibility (ICC A117.1)
(If unit is designated accessible) Verify:
•	Switches and outlets within reach ranges
•	Controls operable with one hand
•	No tight grasping, pinching, or twisting required
•	Clear floor space at switches and outlets

•	Working lighting in all required rooms

•	AFCI protection in living spaces
•	Properly installed switches controlling lighting or receptacles
Missing required protection (GFCI/AFCI) = Immediate Hazard.

General Outlets
Inspect:
•	No cracks, missing covers, or loose devices
•	No burn marks, discoloration, or melting
•	No exposed wiring
•	Outlet firmly mounted
•	Polarity correct (if tester used)
•	No backstabbed wiring if visible
GFCI Outlets (NEC 210.8)
Required in:
•	Bathrooms
•	Kitchens
•	Laundry areas
•	Exterior locations
•	Wet/damp areas
Test:
•	Press TEST → power must shut off
•	Press RESET → power must restore
•	Confirm downstream outlets behave correctly
GFCI failure = Immediate Hazard.
4. Switch Inspection
Inspect:
•	Switch operates smoothly
•	No cracking, looseness, or missing cover
•	No arcing, buzzing, or delay
•	No exposed wiring
•	Switch controls correct fixture or outlet
•	No heat damage or discoloration
Inoperable switch controlling required lighting = Severe.

Required in:
•	Bedrooms
•	Living rooms
•	Hallways
•	Closets

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Fire Safety Inspection
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IFC §603)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: exposed wiring, active leaks, burning smell, blocked exits.
•	Ensure fire safety components are visible and unobstructed.
2. Fire Extinguisher (If Provided) – NFPA 10 / IPMC §704
Inspect:
•	Presence (only required if local code or property policy mandates it).
•	Mounting: secure, visible, accessible.
•	Gauge: needle in the green.
•	Condition: no rust, dents, missing pin, missing tamper seal.
•	Label: readable; correct type (usually ABC).
•	No obstruction blocking access.
Immediate Hazard: missing pin, discharged extinguisher, or inaccessible extinguisher.
3. Smoke Alarms – NFPA 72 / IRC §314 / IPMC §704
Verify:
•	Required locations:
o	Inside each bedroom
o	Outside sleeping areas
o	On every level of the unit
•	Mounting: secure, correct placement (not near vents).
•	Power: battery present or hardwired.
•	Expiration: alarms older than 10 years are invalid.
•	Testing: press TEST → audible alarm must sound.
•	Combination alarms (Smoke/CO): both functions must operate.
Immediate Hazard: missing required alarm or alarm fails test.
4. Sprinkler Assembly (If Present) – NFPA 13 / IFC §903
Inspect:
•	Sprinkler head present and unobstructed.
•	Clearance: minimum 18 inches below head.
•	Condition: no paint, corrosion, dust, or foreign material.
•	Escutcheon plate: present, flush, not missing.
•	No leaks or moisture staining around head.
•	No items hanging from sprinkler head.
Immediate Hazard: painted head, missing escutcheon, or obstruction within 18 inches.
5. Flammable & Combustible Materials – IFC §605 / IPMC §302
Check for:
•	Improper storage near ignition sources (stoves, heaters, electrical panels).
•	Excessive accumulation of combustibles (paper, cardboard, clothing).
•	Fuel storage (gasoline, propane, kerosene) inside unit — prohibited.
•	Aerosols stored near heat sources.
•	Smoking materials improperly discarded.
Severe: fuel stored inside unit or combustibles near ignition sources.
6. Electrical Fire Hazards – IPMC §604 / IFC §605
Inspect:
•	No exposed wiring.
•	No overloaded outlets or daisy chained power strips.
•	No burn marks on outlets or switches.
•	No extension cords used as permanent wiring.
•	No water intrusion near electrical components.
Immediate Hazard: exposed live electrical or water + electrical interaction.
7. Egress & Fire Door Safety – IBC Chapter 10 / NFPA 80
Verify:
•	Entry door operable and latching.
•	Fire rated corridor door (if applicable) self closes and self latches.
•	No storage blocking egress path.
•	No combustibles stored in hallways or near exit doors.
Immediate Hazard: blocked egress or non closing fire door.
8. Mold & Moisture Interaction with Fire Safety (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance near alarms, sprinkler heads, or electrical devices.
•	Moisture staining indicating leaks affecting fire safety components.
•	Persistent mold odor.
Severity:
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Unit Floor & Flooring Components Inspection
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IBC Structural Safety)
•	Confirm safe entry and adequate lighting.
•	Identify immediate hazards: collapse risk, tripping hazards, exposed nails, slippery surfaces, or active leaks.
•	Ensure floor area is visible and unobstructed.
2. Floor Surface Condition (IPMC §305.3 / §305.4)
Inspect entire floor for:
•	Holes, missing sections, or broken tiles
•	Cracks, splits, or delamination
•	Loose boards, tiles, or planks
•	Warping, buckling, or uneven surfaces
•	Torn carpet, loose edges, or frayed transitions
•	Soft spots indicating moisture damage
Any collapse risk = Immediate Hazard.
3. Structural Integrity (IBC Chapter 16 / IPMC §305.2)
Verify:
•	Subfloor is stable and free of movement
•	No sagging or deflection beyond normal tolerance
•	No separation between flooring and subfloor
•	No structural rot or deterioration
Structural failure = Severe.
4. Moisture & Water Intrusion (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Check for:
•	Water stains or discoloration
•	Swelling, bubbling, or soft flooring materials
•	Active leaks from plumbing, appliances, or exterior
•	Mold like substance on flooring or baseboards
•	Musty odors indicating hidden moisture
Severity:
•	Active leak = Severe
•	Mold + leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
5. Flooring Type Specific Requirements
Hardwood / Laminate
•	No cupping, crowning, or buckling
•	No loose planks
•	No rot or moisture swelling
Tile / Stone
•	No cracked or missing tiles
•	No loose tiles or hollow sound when tapped
•	Grout intact, no missing sections
Vinyl / Linoleum
•	No peeling, bubbling, or lifting
•	No tears or gaps at seams
Carpet
•	No tears, fraying, or loose edges
•	No tripping hazards
•	No heavy staining or mold like substance
6. Transitions & Thresholds (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	Transition strips secure and flush
•	No raised edges creating tripping hazards
•	Thresholds intact and properly seated
•	No gaps allowing pest intrusion
Loose or raised transitions = Moderate to Severe depending on severity.
7. Floor Penetrations & Components
Check:
•	Floor registers secure and undamaged
•	No missing or broken covers
•	No gaps around penetrations (pipes, ducts)
•	No exposed sharp edges
•	No fire rated penetrations breached (if applicable)
Unsealed penetrations = Severe.
8. Slippery Conditions (IPMC §305 / IFC §603)
Verify:
•	No wet floors creating slip hazards
•	No wax buildup or improper coatings
•	No algae or mold causing slick surfaces
Slip hazard = Moderate to Severe depending on risk.
9. Mold & Moisture Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on flooring, baseboards, or lower walls
•	Moisture staining or swelling
•	Persistent mold odor
•	Active leaks contributing to mold
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate

•	No structural rot or deterioration
Structural failure = Severe.
4. Moisture & Water Intrusion (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Check for:
•	Water stains or discoloration
•	Swelling, bubbling, or soft flooring materials
•	Active leaks from plumbing, appliances, or exterior
•	Mold like substance on flooring or baseboards
•	Musty odors indicating hidden moisture
Severity:
•	Active leak = Severe
•	Mold + leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
5. Flooring Type Specific Requirements
Hardwood / Laminate
•	No cupping, crowning, or buckling
•	No loose planks
•	No rot or moisture swelling
Tile / Stone
•	No cracked or missing tiles
•	No loose tiles or hollow sound when tapped
•	Grout intact, no missing sections
Vinyl / Linoleum
•	No peeling, bubbling, or lifting
•	No tears or gaps at seams
Carpet
•	No tears, fraying, or loose edges
•	No tripping hazards
•	No heavy staining or mold like substance
6. Transitions & Thresholds (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	Transition strips secure and flush
•	No raised edges creating tripping hazards
•	Thresholds intact and properly seated
•	No gaps allowing pest intrusion
Loose or raised transitions = Moderate to Severe depending on severity.
7. Floor Penetrations & Components
Check:
•	Floor registers secure and undamaged
•	No missing or broken covers
•	No gaps around penetrations (pipes, ducts)
•	No exposed sharp edges
•	No fire rated penetrations breached (if applicable)
Unsealed penetrations = Severe.
8. Slippery Conditions (IPMC §305 / IFC §603)
Verify:
•	No wet floors creating slip hazards
•	No wax buildup or improper coatings
•	No algae or mold causing slick surfaces
Slip hazard = Moderate to Severe depending on risk.
9. Mold & Moisture Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance on flooring, baseboards, or lower walls
•	Moisture staining or swelling
•	Persistent mold odor
•	Active leaks contributing to mold
Severity:
•	Mold + active leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone = Moderate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Foundation Inspection (Interior Indicators)
1. Applicability Check
Foundation inspection applies when the unit shows:
•	Structural movement
•	Settlement or heaving
•	Moisture intrusion at slab or perimeter
•	Cracking in floors, walls, or ceilings
•	Sloping or uneven floors
•	Door/window misalignment
If none of these indicators exist → Not Applicable.
2. Garage Adjacent Foundation (SFR or Townhome Units)
If the unit includes a garage:
•	Inspect slab edges for cracking
•	Check for moisture intrusion from driveway slope
•	Verify no settlement at garage to unit transition
•	Inspect for structural separation at fire rated wall
3. Wall & Ceiling Cracking Patterns (IPMC §305.3 / IBC Structural)
Foundation movement often shows as:
•	Diagonal cracks from door/window corners
•	Horizontal cracks at mid wall height
•	Stair step cracks (if masonry visible)
•	Cracks > 1/8 inch
•	Cracks with moisture staining
Structural cracking = Severe Hairline cracks = Minor
4. Door & Window Alignment (IBC §1001 / IPMC §304)
Check:
•	Doors rubbing, binding, or not latching
•	Windows difficult to open/close
•	Gaps between frames and walls
•	Misaligned strike plates
Door cannot latch due to structural shift = Severe
5. Moisture Intrusion at Slab or Perimeter (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Moisture staining at baseboards
•	Damp carpet or flooring
•	Swelling or bubbling of flooring
•	Efflorescence (white powder) at slab edges
•	Mold like substance near floor level
•	Active water intrusion
Severity:
•	Active leak = Severe
•	Mold + leak = Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard = Immediate Hazard
6. Foundation Related Plumbing Issues (IPC §701–§706)
Foundation movement can affect plumbing:
•	Slow drains due to slope changes
•	Cracked drain lines causing leaks
•	Sewer gas odor from broken pipes
•	Water supply line movement causing wall cracks
Sewer backflow = Immediate Hazard Active plumbing leak = Severe
7. Visible Structural Components (If Applicable)
Some units expose foundation related elements:
•	Concrete slab edges (closets, mechanical rooms)
•	Crawlspace access hatches
•	Basement walls (garden level units)
•	Post tension cable access points
Inspect for:
•	Cracks, spalling, exposed rebar
•	Moisture intrusion
•	Rust staining
•	Pest entry points
Spalling with exposed rebar = Severe Structural instability = Immediate Hazard
8. Pest Activity Related to Foundation Gaps (IPMC §309)
Check:
•	Rodent/insect entry at slab/wall junction
•	Gaps at baseboards
•	Termite mud tubes
•	Damaged wood near floor level
Termite structural damage = Severe

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Hazard Inspection (Infestation + Sharp Edges + Trip Hazards)
1. Infestation (IPMC §309 – Pest Management)
Inspect for:
•	Insects: roaches, ants, bedbugs, fleas, termites
•	Rodents: droppings, gnaw marks, nests, odors
•	Entry points: gaps at baseboards, holes in walls, pipe penetrations
•	Food sources: trash accumulation, food debris, dirty appliances
•	Moisture sources: leaks, damp areas, mold like substance
Severity Guidance:
•	Active infestation = Severe
•	Termite structural damage = Severe
•	Pest entry due to structural gaps = Moderate
2. Sharp Edges (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect for:
•	Broken fixtures or appliances
•	Exposed nails, screws, metal edges
•	Damaged window or door frames
•	Broken furniture creating injury risk
•	Sharp edges on flooring transitions or thresholds
Severity Guidance:
•	Sharp edge capable of causing immediate injury = Immediate Hazard
•	Minor sharp edges (non injury) = Moderate
3. Trip Hazards (IPMC §305 / IBC §1003 – Means of Egress)
Inspect for:
•	Loose flooring, tiles, or planks
•	Raised transitions or thresholds
•	Torn or bunched carpet
•	Electrical cords across pathways
•	Clutter blocking walking paths
•	Uneven surfaces or floor settlement
•	Poor lighting contributing to trip risk
Severity Guidance:
•	Major trip hazard in egress path = Severe
•	Minor unevenness = Moderate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – HVAC Inspection (Wall Heater + Window AC + Boiler/Chiller System)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IMC §102)
Inspect for:
•	Burning smell, overheating, smoke
•	Exposed wiring or damaged cords
•	Water intrusion near electrical HVAC components
•	Obstructions blocking airflow or access
•	Loose, unstable, or improperly mounted units
Immediate Hazard: fire risk, exposed live electrical, or water + electrical interaction.
2. Wall Heater Inspection (IMC §304 / IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Heater securely mounted
•	No scorch marks, soot, or discoloration
•	No combustible materials within required clearance
•	No gas odor (for gas wall heaters)
•	Thermostat operable
•	Safety guards intact
•	Heater cycles on/off properly
•	No sharp edges on housing or grille
Hazard Severity:
•	Gas leak, exposed wiring, overheating → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable heater → Severe
3. Window Air Conditioner Inspection (IMC §307 / IPMC §605)
Inspect:
•	Unit securely installed; no risk of falling
•	No gaps around unit allowing pests or water intrusion
•	No mold like substance on or around unit
•	Proper drainage; no dripping inside the unit
•	Cord intact; not frayed, pinched, or overheated
•	No extension cords used as permanent wiring
•	Filter present and not heavily clogged
•	No sharp edges on frame or mounting brackets
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose unit, electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Water intrusion or mold from A/C → Severe
4. Boiler/Chiller System Components (Fan Coil, Radiator, Convector) – IMC §603 / IPMC §602
Inspect:
•	Fan coil/radiator securely mounted
•	No leaks at hydronic piping or valves
•	No rust, corrosion, or staining indicating past leaks
•	No mold like substance near unit or piping
•	No blocked or obstructed airflow
•	No missing covers exposing moving parts
•	No overheating at motors or fans
•	Thermostat responds and controls system
•	Radiators warm/cool appropriately when system is active
Hazard Severity:
•	Hydronic leak → Severe
•	Exposed moving parts or electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable heating/cooling → Severe
5. General HVAC Components (IMC §603 / IPMC §602)
Inspect:
•	Vents and registers secure; no sharp edges
•	No blocked or obstructed supply/return airflow
•	No damaged ductwork (if visible)
•	No excessive dust buildup indicating poor filtration
•	No overheating at motors or fans
•	No trip hazards from cords or portable units
Hazard Severity:
•	Falling components or sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked airflow affecting habitability → Severe
6. Trip Hazards Related to HVAC (IBC §1003)
Inspect:
•	Window A/C cords across walking paths
•	Portable heaters placed in egress routes
•	Loose or damaged HVAC covers creating trip hazards
•	Poor lighting around HVAC equipment
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
•	Minor obstruction → Moderate
7. Infestation Indicators Related to HVAC (IPMC §309)
Inspect:
•	Pest entry through gaps around window A/C
•	Rodent droppings near heaters or vents
•	Insects nesting inside unused heaters or A/C units
•	Damaged insulation from pests
Hazard Severity:
•	Active infestation → Severe
•	Pest entry points → Moderate
8. Mold & Moisture Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance around A/C, vents, heaters, or fan coils
•	Moisture staining from condensation or leaks
•	Musty odor indicating hidden moisture
•	Water intrusion affecting electrical HVAC components
Hazard Severity:
•	Mold + active leak → Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone → Moderate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – HVAC Inspection (Wall Heater + Window AC + Boiler/Chiller System)
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IPMC §305 / IMC §102)
Inspect for:
•	Burning smell, overheating, smoke
•	Exposed wiring or damaged cords
•	Water intrusion near electrical HVAC components
•	Obstructions blocking airflow or access
•	Loose, unstable, or improperly mounted units
Immediate Hazard: fire risk, exposed live electrical, or water + electrical interaction.
2. Wall Heater Inspection (IMC §304 / IFC §603)
Inspect:
•	Heater securely mounted
•	No scorch marks, soot, or discoloration
•	No combustible materials within required clearance
•	No gas odor (for gas wall heaters)
•	Thermostat operable
•	Safety guards intact
•	Heater cycles on/off properly
•	No sharp edges on housing or grille
Hazard Severity:
•	Gas leak, exposed wiring, overheating → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable heater → Severe
3. Window Air Conditioner Inspection (IMC §307 / IPMC §605)
Inspect:
•	Unit securely installed; no risk of falling
•	No gaps around unit allowing pests or water intrusion
•	No mold like substance on or around unit
•	Proper drainage; no dripping inside the unit
•	Cord intact; not frayed, pinched, or overheated
•	No extension cords used as permanent wiring
•	Filter present and not heavily clogged
•	No sharp edges on frame or mounting brackets
Hazard Severity:
•	Loose unit, electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Water intrusion or mold from A/C → Severe
4. Boiler/Chiller System Components (Fan Coil, Radiator, Convector) – IMC §603 / IPMC §602
Inspect:
•	Fan coil/radiator securely mounted
•	No leaks at hydronic piping or valves
•	No rust, corrosion, or staining indicating past leaks
•	No mold like substance near unit or piping
•	No blocked or obstructed airflow
•	No missing covers exposing moving parts
•	No overheating at motors or fans
•	Thermostat responds and controls system
•	Radiators warm/cool appropriately when system is active
Hazard Severity:
•	Hydronic leak → Severe
•	Exposed moving parts or electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Inoperable heating/cooling → Severe
5. General HVAC Components (IMC §603 / IPMC §602)
Inspect:
•	Vents and registers secure; no sharp edges
•	No blocked or obstructed supply/return airflow
•	No damaged ductwork (if visible)
•	No excessive dust buildup indicating poor filtration
•	No overheating at motors or fans
•	No trip hazards from cords or portable units
Hazard Severity:
•	Falling components or sharp edges → Immediate Hazard
•	Blocked airflow affecting habitability → Severe
6. Trip Hazards Related to HVAC (IBC §1003)
Inspect:
•	Window A/C cords across walking paths
•	Portable heaters placed in egress routes
•	Loose or damaged HVAC covers creating trip hazards
•	Poor lighting around HVAC equipment
Hazard Severity:
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
•	Minor obstruction → Moderate
7. Infestation Indicators Related to HVAC (IPMC §309)
Inspect:
•	Pest entry through gaps around window A/C
•	Rodent droppings near heaters or vents
•	Insects nesting inside unused heaters or A/C units
•	Damaged insulation from pests
Hazard Severity:
•	Active infestation → Severe
•	Pest entry points → Moderate
8. Mold & Moisture Interaction (IPMC §305.1 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance around A/C, vents, heaters, or fan coils
•	Moisture staining from condensation or leaks
•	Musty odor indicating hidden moisture
•	Water intrusion affecting electrical HVAC components
Hazard Severity:
•	Mold + active leak → Severe
•	Mold + electrical hazard → Immediate Hazard
•	Mold like substance alone → Moderate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Full Kitchen Inspection (All Items)
1. Cabinets & Storage (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect:
•	Doors open/close properly
•	No broken hinges, missing doors, or loose hardware
•	No sharp edges, splintered wood, or protruding fasteners
•	No water damage, swelling, delamination, or mold like substance
•	Shelves secure and not collapsing
•	No pest droppings or nesting inside cabinets
Hazards:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
•	Water damage/mold → Severe
•	Pest activity → Severe
2. Countertops & Food Prep Surfaces (IPMC §305.1 – Sanitation)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, missing sections, or exposed particleboard
•	No mold like substance or moisture damage
•	No loose laminate or sharp edges
•	No pest activity
•	Surface cleanable and intact
Hazards:
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
3. Cooking Appliances (Range, Oven, Cooktop) – IFC §603 / IMC §304
Inspect:
•	Burners ignite; oven heats
•	No gas odor (gas appliances)
•	No exposed wiring or damaged cords
•	No scorch marks, soot, or overheating
•	Anti tip bracket installed (required for ranges)
•	Controls functional and not broken
•	No combustibles stored near heat source
Hazards:
•	Gas leak → Immediate
•	Exposed electrical → Immediate
•	Missing anti tip bracket → Severe
•	Inoperable cooking appliance → Severe
4. Refrigerator (IPMC §605 – Electrical Safety)
Inspect:
•	Operates and cools properly
•	Door seals intact
•	No exposed wiring
•	No water leaks or condensation pooling
•	No mold like substance inside or around unit
•	No sharp edges on handles or frame
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Water + electrical → Immediate
•	Inoperable refrigerator → Severe
5. Sink, Faucet & Plumbing (IPC §701–§706 / IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Hot/cold water available
•	Drain flows freely
•	No leaks at P trap, supply lines, or drain
•	No mold like substance under sink
•	No corrosion or damaged piping
•	Garbage disposal (if present) operates safely
Hazards:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sewer odor/backflow → Immediate
6. Ventilation (Range Hood or Exhaust) – IMC §501 / IPMC §602
Inspect:
•	Hood/exhaust fan operable
•	No grease buildup creating fire hazard
•	Filter present and not clogged
•	No exposed wiring
•	No sharp edges on hood housing
•	Adequate airflow
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Heavy grease buildup → Severe
•	Inoperable vent → Moderate/Severe
7. Flooring & Trip Hazards (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	No loose tiles, planks, or peeling flooring
•	No torn or bunched carpet
•	No raised transitions or thresholds
•	No clutter blocking movement
•	No cords across walking paths
Hazards:
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
•	Minor unevenness → Moderate
8. Fire Safety (IFC §603 / IPMC §704)
Inspect:
•	No combustibles near stove or oven
•	No damaged electrical cords
•	No signs of overheating
•	Smoke alarm present outside kitchen (per code location)
•	No blocked egress routes
Hazards:
•	Combustibles near heat source → Severe
•	Electrical fire hazard → Immediate

DEFICIENCY C: Presence of mold-like substance at high levels is observed visually
DEFICIENCY CRITERIA: Cumulative area of patches is more than 1 square foot and less than 9 square feet in a room. Odor is an indicator, but not a diagnostic; if a musty odor is detected, visual confirmation of “mold-like substance” is required. Odor may be indicated in a “notes” field. This deficiency is not recorded if observed on household items (e.g., clothing, upholstery, food)
unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Full Kitchen Inspection (All Items)
1. Cabinets & Storage (IPMC §305 – Interior Surfaces)
Inspect:
•	Doors open/close properly
•	No broken hinges, missing doors, or loose hardware
•	No sharp edges, splintered wood, or protruding fasteners
•	No water damage, swelling, delamination, or mold like substance
•	Shelves secure and not collapsing
•	No pest droppings or nesting inside cabinets
Hazards:
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
•	Water damage/mold → Severe
•	Pest activity → Severe
2. Countertops & Food Prep Surfaces (IPMC §305.1 – Sanitation)
Inspect:
•	No cracks, missing sections, or exposed particleboard
•	No mold like substance or moisture damage
•	No loose laminate or sharp edges
•	No pest activity
•	Surface cleanable and intact
Hazards:
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sharp edges → Immediate
3. Cooking Appliances (Range, Oven, Cooktop) – IFC §603 / IMC §304
Inspect:
•	Burners ignite; oven heats
•	No gas odor (gas appliances)
•	No exposed wiring or damaged cords
•	No scorch marks, soot, or overheating
•	Anti tip bracket installed (required for ranges)
•	Controls functional and not broken
•	No combustibles stored near heat source
Hazards:
•	Gas leak → Immediate
•	Exposed electrical → Immediate
•	Missing anti tip bracket → Severe
•	Inoperable cooking appliance → Severe
4. Refrigerator (IPMC §605 – Electrical Safety)
Inspect:
•	Operates and cools properly
•	Door seals intact
•	No exposed wiring
•	No water leaks or condensation pooling
•	No mold like substance inside or around unit
•	No sharp edges on handles or frame
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Water + electrical → Immediate
•	Inoperable refrigerator → Severe
5. Sink, Faucet & Plumbing (IPC §701–§706 / IPMC §305.1)
Inspect:
•	Hot/cold water available
•	Drain flows freely
•	No leaks at P trap, supply lines, or drain
•	No mold like substance under sink
•	No corrosion or damaged piping
•	Garbage disposal (if present) operates safely
Hazards:
•	Active leak → Severe
•	Mold + leak → Severe
•	Sewer odor/backflow → Immediate
6. Ventilation (Range Hood or Exhaust) – IMC §501 / IPMC §602
Inspect:
•	Hood/exhaust fan operable
•	No grease buildup creating fire hazard
•	Filter present and not clogged
•	No exposed wiring
•	No sharp edges on hood housing
•	Adequate airflow
Hazards:
•	Electrical hazard → Immediate
•	Heavy grease buildup → Severe
•	Inoperable vent → Moderate/Severe
7. Flooring & Trip Hazards (IBC §1003 / IPMC §305)
Inspect:
•	No loose tiles, planks, or peeling flooring
•	No torn or bunched carpet
•	No raised transitions or thresholds
•	No clutter blocking movement
•	No cords across walking paths
Hazards:
•	Trip hazard in egress path → Severe
•	Minor unevenness → Moderate
8. Fire Safety (IFC §603 / IPMC §704)
Inspect:
•	No combustibles near stove or oven
•	No damaged electrical cords
•	No signs of overheating
•	Smoke alarm present outside kitchen (per code location)
•	No blocked egress routes
Hazards:
•	Combustibles near heat source → Severe
•	Electrical fire hazard → Immediate

unit.inspectionProtocol:
International (ICC) Protocol – Inspection for Gas or Oil Leak in a Unit
1. Safety & Initial Conditions (IMC §102 / IFC §604)
Before entering or inspecting:
•	Identify odor of gas (sulfur/rotten egg smell).
•	Listen for hissing near appliances or piping.
•	Look for visible oil residue, staining, or pooling.
•	Check for burning smell, overheating, or smoke.
•	Ensure no open flames, smoking, or ignition sources.
Immediate Hazard: Any suspected gas leak → evacuate, notify management, and stop inspection.
2. Gas Appliances (Wall Heater, Range, Water Heater) – IMC §304 / IFC §603
Inspect:
•	No gas odor around appliance.
•	No hissing at valves, flex lines, or connections.
•	Flex line intact, not kinked, crushed, or corroded.
•	Shutoff valve present and operable.
•	Burner flames steady (blue, not yellow/orange).
•	No soot, scorch marks, or overheating.
•	No combustible materials stored near appliance.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Gas odor
•	Damaged flex line
•	Leaking shutoff valve
•	Soot indicating incomplete combustion
3. Oil Fueled Appliances (If Present) – IFC §603.5
Inspect:
•	No oil drips, stains, or pooling under appliance.
•	No fuel odor.
•	No corrosion at tank or supply line.
•	No leaks at filter, pump, or burner assembly.
•	Flame burns clean and stable.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Active oil leak
•	Oil pooling
•	Fuel odor
•	Overheating or smoke
4. Piping, Valves & Connections (IMC §301 / §303)
Inspect:
•	No corrosion, rust, or deterioration.
•	No loose fittings or damaged threads.
•	No visible oil residue on piping.
•	No gaps at unions or couplings.
•	No vibration or movement at appliance connection.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Active leak
•	Damaged or loose connection
•	Corroded piping with seepage
5. Venting & Combustion Air (IMC §501 / §304.6)
Inspect:
•	Vent pipes intact, properly connected.
•	No gaps, disconnections, or backdrafting.
•	No soot at vent termination.
•	Combustion air openings unobstructed.
•	No signs of exhaust entering living space.
Severe:
•	Backdrafting
•	Blocked vent
•	Soot at vent outlet
6. HVAC Interaction (Wall Heater, Boiler/Chiller Fan Coil)
Inspect:
•	No gas odor near wall heater.
•	No oil residue near hydronic heating components.
•	No leaks at boiler/chiller fan coil piping.
•	No electrical hazard near fuel source.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Fuel leak + electrical hazard
•	Fuel leak near ignition source
7. Environmental Indicators (IPMC §305 / §309)
Inspect:
•	Mold like substance near fuel lines (may indicate moisture + corrosion).
•	Moisture staining around gas/oil piping.
•	Musty or chemical odor indicating hidden leak.
•	Pest activity damaging insulation or flex lines.
Severe:
•	Mold + active leak
•	Corrosion from moisture exposure
8. Tenant Installed Appliances (IFC §603.4)
Inspect:
•	Portable heaters (prohibited if fuel burning).
•	Unauthorized gas appliances.
•	Improperly installed window A/C interfering with venting.
•	Damaged or unapproved fuel containers.
Immediate Hazard:
•	Unauthorized fuel burning appliance
•	Improper fuel storage
